RECORDS MANAGEMENT
TITLE:   Records Management
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   City Clerk
   I.   Scope: This Administrative Instruction governs the production of public
records pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act ("IPRA"),
NMSA 1978, Sections 14-2-1 to -12, and the retention and disposition of public
records within the City of Albuquerque.
   II.   Rescission of Prior Administrative Instructions: Administrative
Instruction 1-5 and Administrative Instruction 1-7 are hereby rescinded.
   III.   Definitions. For the purpose of this AI, the following definitions
apply:
   a.   "City records," as opposed to non-records, are those City records that
evidence the organization, functions, policies, contractual obligations,
decisions and other final actions, directives, procedures, or other operational
activities of the City. Draft records are not considered City records under the
Functional Records Retention and Disposition Schedule ("FRRDS").  1
   b.   "Disposition" is the final action for a City record, such as transfer
to archives or destruction.
   c.   "Non-records" are public records kept for convenience that are not
considered City records, such as preliminary drafts, blank forms, extra copies
of City records, transmittal letters, personal communications, and other
materials intended only for reference or exhibition. (See Section VII for
further discussion and examples of non-records).
   d.   "Official copy of record" is the particular copy of a City record that
is considered the official copy for the purposes of fulfilling the retention
requirements.
   e.   "Official repository" is the Department designated, through policy or
practice, as having responsibility for retaining specific types of public
records, particularly official copies of records.
   f.   "Public records" are records, regardless of physical format, produced,
received, or held by the City of Albuquerque and relating to City business.
Public records may be City records or non-records.
   g.   "Records Analysis and Disposition Committee:" ("the committee") A
committee established pursuant to ROA 1994, Section 2-6-4-2 for the purpose of
analyzing the minimum bookkeeping, auditing, legal, and historical needs of the
City; analyzing current departmental records retention needs; ensuring
compliance with State and Federal laws and regulations; determining whether
modification of the FRRDS is necessary; and recommending changes to the Mayor
and State of New Mexico Commission on Public Records. The Committee shall not
have rule making authority and shall be considered a task force for purposes of
ROA 1994, Section 2-6-1-5.
   h.   "Records Custodian:" The Office of the City Clerk.
   i.   "Records Manager:" A City employee designated as responsible for the
maintenance, care, or keeping of a City department's records regardless of
whether the records are in that person's actual physical custody and control.
   j.   "Retention period" is the minimum period of time during which a
Department should maintain the official copy of record.
   k.   "Transitory records" are a specific type of non-records that serve to
convey information of temporary importance, and often in lieu of oral
communications; they are retained for a limited time to ensure the completion
of a routine action or the preparation of a subsequent record.
   IV.   Roles and responsibilities
   a.   The City Clerk: As the records custodian for the City of Albuquerque,
the City Clerk shall have primary responsibility for ensuring compliance with
IPRA. See § 14-2-7. The Office of the City Clerk shall train and communicate
with all departmental records managers regarding updates on issues related to
IPRA, public records, records retention, and applicable ordinances. The City
Clerk shall also ensure that the Regulations and Procedures on Requests to
Inspect Public Records are up-to-date and compliant with the law. The Office of
the City Clerk shall administer and maintain the electronic IPRA request
tracking system. The Office of the City Clerk, as well as the Office of the
City Attorney, shall advise and direct City employees and officials on issues
related to the inspection of public records.
   b.   Department Directors: All Department Directors shall appoint a
department records manager and provide the City Clerk with all applicable
contact information. Upon a vacancy of a department records manager, the
Director shall inform the City Clerk of the vacancy and shall provide either a
replacement designee or an acting designee until a permanent department records
manager is selected.
   c.   Departmental Records Managers: Department Records Managers are
responsible for assisting the Office of the City Clerk with gathering records
responsive to requests to inspect public records and reviewing and applying the
proper retention period for the Department or Division 's public records .
Records managers shall attend training with the Office of the City Clerk as
soon as practicable after their designation to the position and attend periodic
public records training. All department records managers shall notify the
Office of the City Clerk of any planned absences or vacations from work and
provide an alternate designee that will handle records requests in that person
's absence. All department records managers shall timely review and respond to
all requests from the Office of the City Clerk regarding records requests,
delegate responsibilities within the department in order to respond to
requests, and maintain communication with the Office of the City Clerk
regarding requests and responses.
   d.   City employees: City employees shall help the Office of the City Clerk
and department records managers in responding to requests to inspect public
records. Employees shall also timely address requests for records, and shall
integrate requests for records they maintain into their workflow in order to
ensure timely compliance with IPRA. City employees receiving a public records
request shall immediately forward the request to the Office of the City Clerk.
   e.   "Records Analysis and Disposition Committee" ("the Committee") A
committee established pursuant to ROA 1994, Section 2-6-4-2 for the purpose of
analyzing the minimum bookkeeping, auditing, legal, and historical needs of the
City; analyzing current departmental records retention needs; ensuring
compliance with State and Federal regulations; determining whether modification
of the FRRDS is necessary; and recommending changes to the Mayor and State of
New Mexico Commission on Public Records. The Committee shall have an annual
general meeting and shall meet as needed throughout the year to address records
management and retention issues.
   V.   Retention and Disposition of City Records
   Except as otherwise required by federal or state law, regulation, or
contract, the retention periods for general records common to and maintained by
all City departments, agencies, and offices shall be in accordance with the
FRRDS codified in the New Mexico Administrative Code at NMAC 1.21.2.1 to 943,
as recommended by the Committee on September 19, 2019, and approved by the
Chief Administrative Officer on October 6, 2019. The Records Retention Schedule
posted on the City Clerk's website lists minimum retention periods for basic
types of records and is not intended to be exhaustive in scope. Special
circumstances, such as federal regulations, contractual obligations, and
professional guidelines, may warrant extending a retention period.
   City departments and agencies requesting changes, exceptions, or additions
to the FRRDS shall meet with the Committee to present and discuss proposed
additions, exceptions, or changes to the retention schedule. In lieu of meeting
with the Committee, City departments may meet with the Office of the City
Clerk, who may then relay the proposed additions, exceptions, or changes to the
Committee. The Committee shall recommend to the Mayor and the New Mexico
Commission on Public Records any proposed additions, exceptions, and changes to
the FRRDS. Based on the particular records retention issue raised by a City
department, the Committee or City Clerk may decide to create a city-specific
exception to the FRRDS or request that the FRRDS be modified.
   VI.   Requests for Public Records
   a.   Processing requests: The City Clerk shall process requests for public
records directed to any City Departments, Boards, Commissions, and agencies.
Any city employee receiving a request for records shall immediately forward the
request to the Office of the City Clerk. The City Clerk shall establish
procedures for the processing of public records requests by the staff of the
Office of the City Clerk.
   b.   Denial of Requests: If after appropriate review, the City Clerk finds
that the City should deny the request, in whole or in part, the City Clerk
shall submit its finding, along with the request, to the Office of the City
Attorney. The Office of the City Clerk, in consultation with the City Attorney,
will make an independent determination whether the City should deny the
request, in whole or in part. Upon concurrence, the Office of the City Clerk
will then notify the requester of the determination. The notification shall
contain all information required for a denial under Section 14-2-11(B),
including the legal basis for the denial.
   VII.   Holds for Litigation Matters, Audits, Investigations, and IPRA
Requests:
   The retention periods in the RRS may be lengthened when there is pending,
foreseeable, or ongoing litigation matters, audits, investigations, or IPRA
requests involving the records. In these situations, steps must be taken to
ensure that the City preserves all of its public records that relate to the
subject matter of the litigation matter, audit, investigation, or IPRA request.
   To preserve records, various administrative offices of the City described
below will send out hold notices. Holds control the preservation, retention,
and disposition of specifically listed public records, including non-records
such as draft documents. Holds apply to all forms of public records, including
emails and other electronic records and communications. No one notified of a
hold may alter or delete any record that falls within the scope of the hold
while the hold is in effect.
   The City distributes hold notices through several means. In the case ofIPRA
requests, the City Clerk's Office will reach out to individual City
Departments, Divisions, and employees requesting responsive public records.
Even if those documents are past their retention period or are non-records, the
relevant entity will pause destruction of such records. The records retention
schedule related to public records requests will then apply to the responsive
records.
   When the City Risk Management Division of DFAS receives a preservation
notice within a Tort Claims Notice, it shall distribute the preservation notice
to Departments and individuals who are likely to have records related to the
matters addressed in the notice. Other preservation notices may be distributed
to the relevant departments by the City Legal Department or the City Clerk's
Office.
   To ensure the City's compliance with court rules regarding the preservation
of evidence, the affected Departments and employees must identify, preserve,
and sequester all public records within the Department's control that relate to
the hold, regardless of any established retention periods. Litigation hold
notices are in effect until rescinded by the Legal Department.
   VIII.   Electronic Records and Communications:
   Public records include electronic records and communications that relate to
official City business, such as email and any attachments, as well as postings
on official City websites, biogs, and other social media websites and
applications.
   To the extent that electronic records and communications are City records,
they shall be retained depending upon the nature and content of the document,
consistent with the retention periods for that type or content of document had
it been created in paper form. In general, if the content of the email or
electronic record makes it a "non-record" the document is not subject to
retention and can be destroyed. Employees must comply with any applicable
regulatory requirements , such as FERPA, HIPAA, and state confidentiality laws,
to maintain confidentiality when transmitting information electronically.
   All employees are urged to use the same discretion and good judgment in
creating electronic records and communications as they would in creating paper
documents. Employees should segregate, as much as possible, personal from
professional correspondence and also segregate correspondence that concerns
City business from other professional correspondence, such as work for
scholarly publications and organizations.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/35cea8d42b9362d804e1add43109a67648282f64/
IMAGES/0-0-0-2032.png]
 
   IX.   Public Records Storage and Disposition
   City Departments may store City records in the City Records Center storage
facilities until the applicable retention periods are met, or they may store
them within their Departments .
   The City Clerk is the only City Department authorized to approve destruction
of City records. Prior to the destruction of any City records, the following
requirements must be met:
   •   The retention period in the Records Retention Schedules must have
expired;
   •   There must be no pending, foreseeable, or ongoing litigation matters,
audits, investigations, and IPRA requests related to the documents;
   •   There must be no current Litigation hold on the records; and
   •   The Department seeking to dispose of City Records must complete a
disposition request and obtain signatures from the Department Director and the
City Clerk or designee.
   Once these requirements have been met, the City Clerk authorizes destruction
of City records in coordination with City Departments. Certain types of City
records must be destroyed in a manner that ensures the confidentiality of the
records and renders the information no longer recognizable. The City Clerk
contracts with approved vendors for records destruction stored at the Records
Center. City Departments are responsible for destruction of City Records they
store and which are past their retention period pursuant to the chart attached
as exhibit A. Any exceptions to this destruction procedure must be approved in
writing by the City Clerk.
   X.   Non-Records Storage and Disposition
   Although non-records are not City records, they may be valuable to the
workflow of Departments and, as such, are often kept locally within a
Department to facilitate future business processes. Non-records typically have
one of the following attributes:
   •   The material communicates information of short-term value (such as
reminders about scheduled meetings, announcements of office events, telephone
message slips, self­ sticking notes, and voice mail messages). For example, an
employee prepares notes on the status of projects and initiatives within their
division for their supervisor for use in an upcoming meeting.
   •   The material is a working paper or draft (such as work-in-progress
toward the development of a new policy). For example, a department public
information officer prepares a draft press release and receives feedback on the
draft over email on the draft. Upon issuance of the final press release, the
draft and correspondence about the draft may be disposed of when no longer
needed for reference.
   •   The material is used for reference purposes (such as a downloaded
version of a professional journal article). For example, an employee conducts
research on the budgets of other municipalities and, as part of that research,
prints copies of the annual budgets for the City of Santa Fe. These copies may
be disposed of when no longer needed for reference.
   •   The material is duplicative of a City record for which another
Department serves as the official copy of record (such as a duplicate of the
official copy of a contract).
   Non-records may be destroyed by the Department once they are no longer
useful. Please note, non-records are still public records and therefore subject
to IPRA as long as they are retained by the individual or Department.
 
REFERENCES: ROA 1994, Section 2-6-1-5

OBJECTIVES, DUTIES, AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE OFFICE OF INTERNAL AUDIT
TITLE:   Objectives, Duties, and Responsibilities of the Office of Internal
Audit
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Chief Administrative Officer
The Office of Internal Audit was established by City Ordinance the
Accountability in Government Ordinance.
The independent Office of Internal Audit assists the City Council, the Mayor
and the Chief Administrative Officer in performing their oversight
responsibilities for City functions and activities by conducting audits to
assure accountability and management studies to improve integrity.
All officials, employees, vendors and contractors of the City shall timely
furnish the Office of Internal Audit with requested information and records in
their custody regarding City activities. In addition, they shall provide access
for the Office of Internal Audit to inspect all property, equipment and
facilities in their custody.
The Office of Internal Audit shall adhere to professional standards in
conducting its work and will be considered independent as defined by those
standards.

ACCEPTANCE OF LAWSUITS AND SUBPOENAS
TITLE:   Acceptance of Lawsuits and Subpoenas
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Legal
SECONDARY DEPARTMENT:   City Clerk
Purpose of Administrative Instruction:
This Administrative Instruction will provide the procedure for accepting
lawsuits and subpoenas issued to the City and various sub parties of the City.
Background:
The city, its employees, and its officials are frequently asked to accept
service of lawsuits and subpoenas relating to City business. "Service" occurs
when a summons and complaint or subpoena is delivered to the City, its
employees or officials. Service of legal documents creates a legal duty to
respond and, therefore, these procedures should be carefully followed.
General Policy:
SUMMONS AND COMPLAINT
   1.   The City Clerk and City Attorney are the City of Albuquerque's agents
authorized to accept the service of a summons and complaint for:
      a.   City of Albuquerque
      b.   Mayor
      c.   City Councilors
      d.   Chief Administrative Officer
      e.   Deputy/Associate Chief Administrative Officers
      f.   City Departments
      g.   City Department Directors
   2.   The City Clerk or City Attorney are authorized to accept summonses and
complaints addressed to the parties enumerated in paragraph one (1) of this
Administrative Instruction, by mail, email, or in person. Summonses and
complaints addressed to City employees not listed in paragraph one (1) shall
not be accepted by the City Clerk or the City Attorney.
   3.   Summonses and Complaints addressed to a City employee or official, not
covered in paragraph 1, should only be accepted by the employee or official
named in the summons. Employees or officials may get served at work, at home,
by email, or by posting at their home. The named employee or official shall
immediately give a copy of the legal documents to their Department Director's
office or the Mayor's office. The Department or Mayor's office shall
immediately deliver the legal documents to the City Attorney's office.
   4.   The City Attorney may accept service as otherwise provided by law.
SUBPOENAS
   1.   Subpoenas must be personally served to the individual named in the
subpoena with only three exceptions: the City Attorney, City Clerk, or Deputy
City Clerks may accept service of subpoenas directed to the Mayor or Chief
Administrative Officer. City employees may accept service only of those
subpoenas issued in their name.
   2.   If the subpoena is served on the individual City employee named in the
subpoena, the employee shall accept service and determine if a witness fee in
the correct amount is attached to the subpoena. Currently, the correct amount
of the witness fee is $95.00 for cases in state courts and $40.00 for cases in
federal courts. If the response to the subpoena will be accomplished through
appearance on City time, the employee is to immediately turn the witness fee
over to his or her department finance officer. If the appearance will be done
on the employee's personal time, the employee may accept the witness fee.
   3.   If the correct witness fee is missing, the employee named in the
subpoena shall accept service, make a written note to his or her supervisor
that the fee is missing and make an oral demand for the correct witness fee.
   4.   Following acceptance of a subpoena, the employee is to immediately
contact the City Attorney's office. The City Attorney's office will instruct
the employee on how to handle the subpoena.
   5.   Any subpoena issued for the production of City records shall be served
upon the City Clerk in-person, by mail, or by email at cityclerkipra@cabq.gov.
Writ of Garnishment
   1.   The Payroll Division of the Department of Finance and Administrative
Services shall accept service of all writs of garnishment. No other person or
department shall accept service of writs of garnishment.

LITIGATION DEFENSE OF MEMBERS OF INFORMAL COUNCILS, COMMITTEES AND TASK FORCES
TITLE:   Litigation Defense of Members of Informal Councils, Committees and
Task Forces
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Legal Department
In order to obtain and maintain the best assistance and involvement by the
Albuquerque citizenry in City government, the City Attorney shall provide a
defense for members of informal City task forces, review committees, advisory
councils, or other informal committees established to assist the City in
various subjects and studies. This policy applies to those informal committees
not created by City Council and covered by the indemnification ordinance.
Pursuant to the New Mexico Tort Claims Act and the Albuquerque Boards,
Commissions and Committees Defense and Indemnification Ordinance, the City will
provide a defense when liability is sought for actions alleged to have been
committed by the member while acting within the scope of the member's duties,
responsibilities and service to the committee. At the time of providing such
defense, an agreement will be entered into with the member that the City will
have the right to recover the amount expended by the City if it is shown that
the member acted fraudulently or with actual intentional malice.
The Chief Administrative Officer will designate which of the City task forces,
review committees, advisory councils, or other informal committees will be
eligible for such a defense. In order for the Chief Administrative Officer to
make these designations, all department directors are directed to request
approval by the Chief Administrative Officer of all such committees and task
forces in service to their department and approval of indemnification of those
committees and task forces. Department directors shall request approval of
creation and indemnification of committees in an ongoing manner as they are
established. Those committees and task forces currently in existence but not
approved by the Chief Administrative Officer shall cease to exist.
REFERENCES:
New Mexico Tort Claims Act, 41-4-1 – 41-4-27, et seq.
Albuquerque Boards, Commissions, and Committees Defense and Indemnification
Ordinance

ADOPTION OF PROCEDURE FOR ADMINISTRATION OF THE GRIEVANCE RESOLUTION PROCEDURE
ESTABLISHED BY THE MERIT SYSTEM ORDINANCE
TITLE: Adoption of Procedure for Administration of the Grievance Resolution
Procedure Established by the Merit System Ordinance
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Purpose
To adopt a procedure for the orderly and expeditious administration of the
Grievance Resolution Procedure established by the Merit System Ordinance § 3-1-
24.
Policy
The City has enacted the Grievance Resolution Procedure of the Merit System
Ordinance to provide a means for reconciling complaints concerning minor
disciplinary actions and working conditions or departmental rules. The purpose
of the Grievance Resolution Procedure is to promote harmonious relations among
employees, supervisors and managers; to encourage the settlement of
disagreements informally at the employee-supervisor level; to provide an
orderly procedure to handle grievances through the various supervisory levels
when necessary; to resolve grievances as quickly as possible; and to discourage
the filing of unfounded grievances.
The Grievance Resolution Committee (GRC) created by the Merit System Ordinance
serves in an advisory capacity to investigate disputes and make a
recommendation to the Chief Administrative Officer on resolving the disputes.
The Chief Administrative Officer is the sole decision maker.
Scope  
Pursuant to § 3-1-24 of the Merit System Ordinance, this Grievance Resolution
Procedure applies to all permanent classified employees who are not covered by
labor agreements providing an alternate grievance procedure.
Procedures for Filing and Processing Grievances
A. General Rules:
   1. When calculating time limits under this Administrative Instruction the
date of the act or occurrence that triggers the time limit shall not be
included. If the last day of the time limit is a weekend or holiday, the
following business day shall be considered the last day.
   2. Failure of an employee to comply with the time limits established by the
Merit System Ordinance shall result in the grievance being dismissed. A
grievance dismissed for failure to comply with time limits may not be refiled.
   3. A written grievance shall be deemed submitted on the date it is received
by the City’s Human Resources Department.
   4. A written response shall be deemed submitted on the date it is received
by the employee, if hand delivered, or the date it is placed in the United
States mail to the employee's last known address. Whenever the City or the
employee delivers a paper to the other party which requires a response within a
certain time period and the paper is delivered by U.S. mail, an additional
three (3) days shall be added to the time period for responding.
   5. The original Grievance Request Form (attached), which the employee fills
out to initiate the grievance, will be used throughout the entire grievance
process. The form is obtained through the Human Resources Department and that
Department will assure that a copy is returned to the employee at the end of
the process.
B. Step One:
   1. The employee shall obtain the Grievance Resolution Form through the Human
Resources Department and assure that Parts 1 and 2 are filled out thoroughly.
The employee shall then initiate a grievance by filing a request for review
with the City Employee Mediation Program in the Alternative Dispute Resolution
(ADR) Office, 2nd Floor Old City Hall 768-4500 (FAX 768-4525).
   2. The request for review shall be submitted in writing, on the Grievance
Resolution Form attached as Appendix 1 to this Administrative Instruction.
   3. The request for review shall be submitted within ten (10) calendar days
of the date of the act being grieved or from the date the employee became aware
of the action.
   4. Within seven (7) calendar days of receipt of the request for review, the
City ADR Coordinator or his/her designee will determine if mediation of the
dispute is appropriate.
   5. If the City ADR Coordinator or his/her designee determines that mediation
of the dispute is not appropriate, the ADR Coordinator shall notify the
employee in writing, and the employee may proceed to Step Two of the Grievance
Resolution Procedure.
   6. If the City ADR Coordinator or his/her designee determines that mediation
of the dispute is appropriate, the mediation will be held according to the
guidelines of the City Employee Mediation Program.
   7. If the mediation process results in a resolution consistent with existing
City policy and acceptable to all mediation participants, the matter shall be
deemed concluded.
   8. If the parties do not resolve the grievance in mediation, the ADR
Coordinator shall notify the employee in writing that the employee may proceed
to Step Two of the Grievance Resolution Procedure.
C. Step Two:
   1. The employee shall initiate Step Two of the Grievance Resolution
Procedure by submitting the grievance to his/her Department Director within
seven (7) calendar days after the mediation or the decision of the ADR
Coordinator that mediation is not appropriate.
   2. The grievance shall be in writing on the Grievance Request Form, attached
as Appendix 1 to this Administrative Instruction.
   3. Either the employee or the Department Director may request a meeting.
   4. The decision of whether or not to have a meeting between the Department
Director and the employee shall be at the sole discretion of the Department
Director.
   5. Within seven (7) calendar days from the meeting, or, if no meeting is
held, within seven (7) calendar days of receipt of the grievance, the
Department Director should respond, in writing to the employee on the original
Grievance Request Form.
   6. If the employee is not satisfied with the decision of the Department
Director, the employee may proceed to Step Three of the Grievance Resolution
Procedure.
D. Step Three:
   1. Within seven (7) calendar days after the Department Director submits his/
her written response to the employee, the employee shall submit his/her Step
Three grievance, in writing, to the Human Resources Department, which shall be
responsible for receiving Step Three Grievances on behalf of the Chief
Administrative Officer.
   2. The Step Three Grievance shall be submitted on the Grievance Request Form
originally obtained from the Human Resources Department and also attached to
this Administrative Instruction as Appendix 1.
   3. Upon receipt of the grievance, the Human Resources Department shall
forward the written grievance to the Chief Administrative Officer or his/her
designee who shall determine grievability on behalf of the Chief Administrative
Officer.
   4. If the Chief Administrative Officer or his/her designee determines that
the matter is not grievable, the Human Resources Department shall notify the
employee in writing, on Part 9 of the original Grievance Request Form, and the
matter shall be deemed concluded.
   5. If the Chief Administrative Officer or his/her designee determines that
the matter is grievable, the Chief Administrative Officer or designee shall
convene a Grievance Resolution Committee to investigate the dispute and
recommend a resolution.
Rules and Procedures for the Grievance Resolution Committee
A. Qualifications of Members of the Grievance Resolution Committee:
   1. Members of the Grievance Resolution Committee shall be full-time,
permanent non-probationary employees.
   2. An individual shall not serve on a Grievance Resolution Committee if he/
she has received a disciplinary suspension or demotion within the last two (2)
years, unless the disciplinary action was overturned by action of a Grievance
Resolution Committee, the Personnel Board or a court of competent jurisdiction.
   3. An individual shall not serve on a Grievance Resolution Committee for any
individual employed within his/her own department/division.
   4. An individual shall not serve on a Grievance Resolution Committee for any
grievant or respondent to whom the Grievance Resolution Committee member is
related by blood or by marriage.
   5. Individuals selected for the Grievance Resolution Committee shall receive
a minimum of four (4) hours training. All training for the Grievance Resolution
Committee shall be approved by the Chief Administrative Officer or his/her
designee.
B. Selection of Members of the Grievance Resolution Committee
   1. The Director of Human Resources shall develop guidelines for selecting a
pool of twenty-five (25) qualified supervisory and twenty-five (25) qualified
non-supervisory employees. A new pool of qualified employees shall be
established as often as is determined necessary by the Chief Administrative
Officer.
   2. Each Grievance Resolution Committee that is convened shall consist of two
(2) supervisory and two (2) non-supervisory employees, selected at random from
the pool of qualified employees.
   3. Individuals selected to serve on a Grievance Resolution Committee shall
not be excused from service without a documented valid reason approved by the
Director of Human Resources or designee, or unless the individual is employed
within the same department/division as the grievant, or the individual is
related by blood or marriage to the grievant or the respondent.
C. Grievance Resolution Committee Hearing Procedures
   1. Upon selection of the Grievance Resolution Committee, the Human Resources
Department shall notify the grievant, respondent and committee members of the
selection.
   2. The Human Resources Department shall act as coordinator and record keeper
for the Grievance Resolution Committee.
   3. Within thirty (30) days of selection, the Grievance Resolution Committee
shall convene a hearing to investigate the matter.
   4. At a minimum of ten (10) working days prior to the investigative hearing,
the grievant and respondent shall submit any documentation they wish to have
considered by the Grievance Resolution Committee to the Human Resources
Department. The Human Resources Department shall be responsible for preparing
copies of the documentation and providing them to the respective parties and
the Grievance Resolution Committee members prior to the hearing.
   5. At a minimum of ten (10) working days prior to the investigative hearing,
the grievant and respondent shall submit a list of any individuals they wish to
appear before the Grievance Resolution Committee in support of their position.
The Human Resources Department shall be responsible for notifying those
employees who are requested to appear before the Grievance Resolution
Committee.
   6. Grievants and respondents appearing before the Grievance Resolution
Committee may be accompanied by a representative, but the role of the
representative is limited to advising the grievant or respondent. A
representative may not make arguments, question the committee or individuals
appearing before the committee or make objections to the proceedings. Labor
unions do not have representation rights for non-bargaining unit employees.
   7. The Grievance Resolution Committee may make a decision based on the
documents submitted, or it may permit the grievant and the respondent to make a
presentation to the Grievance Resolution Committee. The total time allowed for
a presentation by a party to the committee shall not exceed one-half hour for
each party.
   8. In addition to any presentation made by the grievant and respondent, the
Grievance Resolution Committee may elect to question individuals who have been
requested to appear in support of a party's position. A grievant or respondent
may submit, in writing to the Grievance Resolution Committee, questions he/she
wishes to have asked, but only the committee members may ask questions of any
individual. The total time allowed for questioning all individuals supporting a
party's position shall not exceed one (1) hour for each party.
   9. At the conclusion of the investigative hearing, the Grievance Resolution
Committee shall deliberate in closed session. Following deliberations, the
Grievance Resolution Committee shall make a written recommendation and forward
it to the Chief Administrative Officer.
   10. The written recommendation shall be submitted within five (5) working
days of the conclusion of the investigative hearing.
Chief Administrative Officer Review
   1. The Chief Administrative Officer shall review the written recommendation
and make a final written resolution.
   2. The final written resolution shall be forwarded to the employee and the
Department Director by the Human Resources Department.
   3. The Chief Administrative Officer's decision shall be the final step in
the Grievance Resolution Process.
REFERENCES: Merit System Ordinance § 3-1-24

CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE S.A.F.E. AT WORK
TITLE: City of Albuquerque S.A.F.E at Work
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Albuquerque Police Department
Purpose of Administrative Instruction:
To support the City of Albuquerque's S.A.F.E. at Work campaign by posting
informational flyers in City facilities and introducing the program during New
Employee Orientation.
The S.A.F.E. at Work program (Support, Awareness, Freedom, Empowerment) raises
awareness about domestic violence, conflict management, and behavioral health
support, offering confidential resources to employees who may need assistance
for themselves or others.
Background:
The City of Albuquerque and the Albuquerque Police Department are launching the
S.A.F.E at Work campaign, aiming to bring awareness and provide resources about
domestic violence. The campaign idea came about in January 2025, when it was
determined that many victims who may be facing domestic violence may feel most
empowered to find help while at their place of employment. The City of
Albuquerque, being one of the biggest employers in the city, is a place to
bring awareness and resources to potentially hundreds of victims, family,
friends, coworkers and supervisors of victims.
Through this initiative, information flyers would be posted in all city
facilities with links to a city website that provides details and resources for
victims. This campaign is different than most because there is also a focus and
outreach for those who may also be potential offenders, possibly facing stress
or anger management issues. This campaign will direct those in needs of
services to the website where they can also learn about how the Employee
Assistance Program can help with behavioral health issues.
The hopes for this campaign is to reach potential victims who may be employed
with the City and have finally found the empowerment and safe place to get the
resources they need to leave a violent situation and also encourage other big
employers to follow the City's lead and bring awareness to all work places.
Instructions
1. Flyer Posting Requirements
   • Post the S.A.F.E. at Work flyer in the following areas:
   • Restrooms
   • Break rooms
   • Announcement boards
   • Digital facility boards
   • Near employee wage, labor law, and workers ' compensation postings
   • All City facilities, including but not limited to:
      o Pino Yards
      o Transit facilities
      o Community Centers
      o Multigenerational Centers
      o Senior Centers
Ensure flyers are:
   • Clearly visible and replace them if damaged or missing.
   • The flyer includes a QR code and a link to cabq.gov/safe, where employees
can access confidential resources for domestic violence support, conflict
management, and behavioral health services.
2. New Employee Orientation Requirements
Introduce the S.A.F.E. at Work program during the Employee Assistance Program
(EAP) portion of New Employee Orientation.
Use the following talking points:
   • S.A.F.E. at Work stands for Support, Awareness, Freedom, and Empowerment.
   • Support is available if you are experiencing domestic violence, struggling
with conflict, or are concerned about someone else.
   • Your workplace can be more than a job-it can be a lifeline.
   • Scan the QR code on the flyer or visit cabq.gov/safe for confidential
resources.
3. Current Employee Requirements
Require current employees to take the updated Domestic Violence Awareness
training every 2 years through the HR Employee Portal.
The updated Domestic Violence Training will be given during all City of
Albuquerque new supervisor trainings.
4. Responsibilities
Department Directors - Ensure flyers are posted and maintained in all
designated locations.
Human Resources Department - Ensure New Employee Orientation includes the
introduction of the S.A.F.E. at Work program.
Facility Managers - Regularly monitor and maintain flyer postings to ensure
visibility and availability.

NOTARY PUBLIC ACTS AND FEES
TITLE:   NOTARY PUBLIC ACTS and FEES
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Legal Department
Certain Departments of City government have need for a notary public in
connection with the execution of official City documents. To mitigate delays in
the prompt handling of these documents, it is appropriate that those
Departments have one or more persons who are authorized by the State to perform
notarial acts.
Effective July 1, 2003, the New Mexico Secretary of State implemented new
requirements with respect to notaries public under the provisions of the Notary
Public Act passed by the 2003 New Mexico Legislature. After the effective date
of the Act, any application for appointment or re-appointment as a New Mexico
notary public must be accompanied by an application fee of $20.00. In addition,
the application must be accompanied by a bond in the amount of $10,000.00
executed by a licensed surety for a term of four years commencing on the
effective date of the notary's commission and terminating on its expiration
date.
The Legal Department will maintain a master list of all notaries public for
whom the City provides the required bond and pays the application fee. Each
Department must provide a letter of justification at least thirty (30) days in
advance of the date when an application for appointment or re-appointment is to
be filed. If the Legal Department concurs with the justification, the Legal
Department will make the necessary arrangements for the required surety bond.
Upon receipt from the licensed surety, the bond, application and an E&O policy
naming the City of Albuquerque will be forwarded to the applicant. The
applicant will fill out the application for appointment or re-appointment,
obtain the application fee from the applicant's Department and submit the
following to the New Mexico Secretary of State: (1) the application form; (2)
the application fee; and (3) the surety bond. The Legal Department will retain
the E&O policy and provide a copy to the applicant. Charges for the surety bond
will be charged to the requesting Department.
Persons for whom the City has paid the costs associated with compliance with
the Notary Public Act are encouraged to limit their notarial acts to those
rendered on behalf of the City during their period of employment with the City.
Further, such persons are required to maintain a log of all acts undertaken as
a notary public, which log shall be submitted to the Legal Department for
review at the request of the Legal Department.
This policy is effective for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2017.
REFERENCES:   NMSA 1978 § 14-14-1 et seq.

OPEN MEETINGS ACT – COMPLIANCE BY CITY BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS
TITLE:   OPEN MEETINGS ACT – COMPLIANCE BY CITY BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   City Clerk
Background:
The City Charter and City ordinances create various City boards, commissions
and other bodies with adjudicatory authority that are subject to the Open
Meetings Act, Sec. 10-15-1 NMSA 1978 et. seq.
Policy:
Members of all formal City boards, commissions or other bodies with
adjudicatory authority who are subject by operation of law to the state Open
Meetings Act shall receive training with respect to compliance with that Act
and take all necessary actions to ensure that they are consistently in
compliance with that Act. To that end, the meetings of all formal City boards,
commissions or other bodies with adjudicatory authority shall cause each and
every public meeting to be recorded through the use of analog or digital media.
The analog or digital media shall be retained until minutes of the meeting have
been prepared and approved by the board, commission or other body with
adjudicatory authority; provided, however, that if the action of the board,
commission or other body with adjudicatory authority is subject to appeal or
review under any provision of law, the analog or digital media recording shall
be retained for a period expiring concurrently with the last date for the
filing of such appeal or review.
Minutes of meetings are generally subject to the Retention and Disposition
Schedule for General Administrative Records, unless some other standard
applies.
All formal city boards, commissions or other bodies subject to the Open
Meetings Act shall meet one of four ways:
•   In person;
•   remotely by use of a webinar platform with sufficient administrative
controls to allow for controlled participation of the public;
•   remotely while streaming the meeting on the official City of Albuquerque
YouTube page; or
•   by using a hybrid format utilizing two or more of the above methods.
REFERENCES:   Open Meetings Act, Sec. 10-15-1 NMSA 1978 et. seq

TITLE:   Rescission and Repeal of Chief Administrative Officer’s 1983 Policies
and Procedures Manual and Similar Documents
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Chief Administrative Officer
A document titled “Chief Administrative Officer’s 1983 Policies and Procedures
Manual”, believed to have last been updated in December, 1986, may still be
available in hard copy in some areas of City government. The directives,
policies and procedures included in that document were superseded by the

PROTOCOL FOR ADDRESSING SIGNAGE ISSUES
TITLE:   Protocol for Addressing Signage Issues
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Planning
With the exception of street banners or identification signs approved by the
City, signs located within the public right-of-way are prohibited and will be
discarded as soon as they are collected.
Various City departments are responsible for the disposal of illegal signs.
Illegal signs attached to traffic signals, utility poles, traffic signs, and
arroyos and bridges within City jurisdiction, are disposed of by the Department
of Municipal Development. Illegal signs located within unimproved street
medians or other unimproved public right-of- way, are disposed of by the Solid
Waste Management Department. Illegal signs placed within parks, improved,
landscaped medians and streetscapes within the City are disposed of by the
Parks & Recreation Department. The Zoning Enforcement division of the Planning
department will resolve all sign related to 311 calls on private property.
While performing their normal job duties in the field, the employees of the
departments responsible for the disposal of illegal signs shall dispose of all
illegal signs in each department's designated areas of responsibility, and will
dispose of any other illegal signs observed even if those signs may be the
responsibility of another department.
Improperly placed political signs within the public right-of-way, that may have
been collected by the City of Albuquerque during an election season to which
the sign pertains will be temporarily stored and may be retrieved at the City
of Albuquerque, Pino Yards facility located at 5501 Pino Ave NE, Albuquerque NM
87109. All political signs collected by the city will be held for 20 days after
the conclusion of the election and then will be disposed of by the City. To
retrieve political signs, individuals will be required to check in at the
security guard station at the Pino Yard facility and a photo ID. Political
signs may be retrieved Monday through Friday, between 8:00 am and 6:00 p.m. All
other illegal signs within the public right-of-way will be discarded as soon as
they are collected.
To help reduce the improper placement of signs within the right-of-way, the
Planning Department shall continue to notify all registered candidates in
writing at least 60 days prior to an election of the proper placement
locations, areas prohibited from posting, and size limitations throughout the
City. Similarly, yearly notifications are sent to various professional real
estate organizations throughout Albuquerque. The Planning Department shall also
continue to address all permitting and enforcement duties for illegal signs
located on private property, including their removal as outlined in Section 14-
16-4-11 of the zoning code.
REFERENCES: Section 14-16-4-11 of the zoning code

ELECTRONIC IDENTIFICATION
TITLE: Electronic Identification
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:Department of Finance and Administrative Services, Transit,
Cultural Services, Parks and Recreation, Family and Community Services,
Department of Senior Affairs
The purpose of this Administrative Instruction is to establish City policy
regarding the acceptance of electronic identification in the provision of City
services and benefits. This instruction is not intended to apply to activities
of law enforcement, the airport or City concessionaires or transactions in
which proof of identity is otherwise mandated by law.
The following definitions shall apply to this instruction:
   1.   “Electronic” means relating to technology having electrical, digital,
magnetic, wireless, telephonic, optical, electromagnetic or similar
capabilities.
   2.   “Electronic identification (ID)” means an electronic representation of
an identification document, such as a student ID, a driver’s license, or a
military/veteran’s ID, that an issuing authority has created, generated, sent,
communicated, or stored by electronic means.
   3.   “Issuing authority” means a school, governmental or other entity that
issues electronic IDs.
Acceptance of Electronic IDs. Upon request and unless otherwise prohibited by
state or federal law, City departments that require proof of an individual’s
identity to verify eligibility for a City service or benefit shall accept an
electronic ID in lieu of a physical ID.
Monitoring and Implementation. The Department of Finance and Administrative
Services (DFAS) shall be responsible for implementing this instruction as
follows:
   1.   DFAS shall periodically monitor legal notices, websites and other
available sources to determine those issuing authorities who are currently
using electronic IDs. DFAS shall contact each issuing authority for
confirmation that the entity is using electronic IDs.
   2.   The DFAS shall maintain, update, and circulate to all departments a
list of issuing authorities. The list shall include information designed to
assist the departments in determining the validity of electronic IDs, including
information explaining the features of the electronic ID and/or a photographic
representation of the electronic ID.
   3.   DFAS shall update the list and promptly notify City departments when it
becomes aware that an issuing authority starts accepting electronic IDs.
   4.   DFAS shall coordinate responses to questions from City departments
related to the authenticity or legal validity of electronic IDs.
This Administrative Instruction is effective immediately.

SOCIAL MEDIA POLICY (2025)
TITLE: Social Media Policy
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Technology and Innovation
Purpose of Administrative Instruction: The purpose of this policy is to
establish rules and responsibilities around the use of social media for City of
Albuquerque departments. It is intended to guide City departments and employees
as they create and publish content and maintain user standards on social media
sites on behalf of the City of Albuquerque.
Background:
Social media has the potential to fundamentally change the way in which
residents and City Government communicate and interact. To address the evolving
landscape of the Internet and the way we communicate online, Departments within
the City of Albuquerque may use social media as a tool to reach a broader
audience. The City encourages the use of social media to further the goals of
the City and the mission of its departments.
The City of Albuquerque has an overriding interest and expectation in deciding
what is communicated on behalf of the City on social media sites. This policy
establishes standards for the official use of City of Albuquerque social media.
City of Albuquerque sites include all accounts representing City of Albuquerque
departments, programs, facilities or divisions.
Violations of this policy may be grounds for discipline up to and including
termination.
Definitions:
Blog: A self-published diary or commentary on a particular topic that may allow
visitors to post responses, reactions, or comments. The term is short for "Web
log."
Page: The specific portion of a social media website where content is displayed
and managed by an individual or individuals with administrator rights.
Post: A discrete piece of content an individual shares on a social media site
or the act of publishing content on a site.
Profile: Information that a user provides about themself on a social networking
site.
Social Media: A category of Internet-based resources that integrate user
generated content and user participation. This includes, but is not limited to,
social network sites, microblogging sites, photo and video sharing sites,
wikis, blogs, and news sites.
Social Networks: Online platforms where users can create profiles, share
information, and socialize with others using a range of technologies.
Wiki: Web page(s) that can be edited collaboratively.
General Policy:
Rules and Responsibilities:
   1.   The City of Albuquerque's website (www.cabq.gov) will remain the City's
primary website and online presence.
   2.   Departmental staff are responsible for the content and upkeep of any
social media sites their department creates. Department directors must
authorize employees to post prior to them receiving credentials.
   3.   Department directors, the Communications Director, or their designee
will be responsible for updating passwords and removing social media access for
employees who are separating from service with the City.
   4.   New Accounts.
      a.   The decision to create a social media site or account shall be part
of a well thought out social media strategy approved by communications staff
and the Department Director and based on an assessment and understanding of the
risks associated with social media.
      b.   All new social media sites proposed for City use will be approved by
the Communications Director or other designated staff member.
      c.   All departments and divisions must fill out a New Social Media form
and send it to the Communications Director or their designee to receive
approval.
   5.   All City of Albuquerque social media sites shall be created and
maintained with the identifiable characteristics of an official City site.
   6.   All City of Albuquerque social media sites shall comply with all
appropriate City of Albuquerque policies and standards, including but not
limited to:
      a.   Website Responsibility;
      b.   Purpose and Commitment to Quality;
      c.   User standards to maintain appropriate content on City pages; and
      d.   All exceptions will be approved by the Director of Communications.
   7.   City of Albuquerque social media sites shall comply with the City of
Albuquerque's Code of Ethics, the City of Albuquerque's Election Code, and all
administrative rules created under those codes.
   8.   City of Albuquerque social media sites are subject to the State of New
Mexico's public records laws. This means that any content maintained in a
social media format that is related to City business may be a public record.
The Department maintaining the site is responsible for providing records to the
City Clerk's Office when the City receives a request for records which includes
social media content.
   9.   There is not a specific retention schedule for social media, though
most social media content is likely non-record and not subject to retention.
When transmitting through social media information which has a specific
retention schedule, such as press and news releases, a copy of the information
must be transmitted rather than the original. Save the original content in a
shared X drive or in another readily accessible location.
   10.   Users and visitors to social media sites shall be notified that the
intended purpose of the site is to serve as a mechanism for communication
between City departments and members of the public.
   11.   City of Albuquerque social media site posts or comments made by
constituents/followers containing any of the following content are prohibited,
and may be removed without notice by the Communications Director or their
designee:
      a.   Posts not topically related to the particular social media site, or
comments not topically related to the post or article being commented upon;
      b.   Posts or comments in support of or opposition to political campaigns
or ballot measures;
      c.   Profane language or content;
      d.   Posts or comments intended to spread false information or threaten,
harass or defame others;
      e.   Content that promotes, fosters, or perpetuates discrimination on the
basis of race, creed, color, age, religion, gender, marital status, status with
regard to public assistance, national origin, physical or mental disability or
sexual orientation;
      f.   Sexual content or links to sexual content;
      g.   Solicitations of commerce not directly related to City business;
      h.   Conduct or encouragement of illegal activity;
      i.   Information that is intentionally factually incorrect and which may
tend to compromise the safety or security of the public or public systems; j.
Content that violates any federal, state or local law or a legal ownership
interest of any other party;
      k.   Information about actual or potential claims and litigation
involving the City, unless such claims have been resolved;
      l.   Any protected or confidential information regarding any City
employee, resident, or elected official.
   12.   The guidelines in subsection K shall be displayed to users or made
available by linking to the City's website.
   13.   City of Albuquerque accounts may respond to comments or posts relevant
to the department, division, or program in order to provide information. When
responding or posting to social media on behalf of the City:
      a.   Maintain professionalism and a respectful tone at all times.
      b.   Correct errors, and if modifying an earlier post, identify the
change.
      c.   Refrain from engaging in arguments or personal attacks. Responses to
negative or inflammatory comments should be handled respectfully and with the
goal of informing.
      d.   Departments may delete, merge, or unpublish a social media post only
with prior approval from the Director of Communications or their Department
Director.
   14.   City department social media sites will serve as the primary social
media presence for Boards & Commissions, initiatives, events and programs.
   15.   Administration of City of Albuquerque social media sites will be as
follows:
      a.   DTI will maintain a list of social media sites which are approved
for use by City departments and staff. DTI will review this list annually for
changes such as, but not limited to, usage agreements and new or expired
offerings.
      b.   DTI will maintain a list of all City of Albuquerque social media
sites, including login and password information. This list must be accessible
to the Director of Communications. Departmental staff will inform DTI of any
administrative or password changes to existing sites. If an administrator
leaves City employment, the Department will change the password and inform DTI
of the new password. DTI will update the password list.
      c.   The City must be able to immediately edit or remove content from
social media sites. 16. For each social media tool approved for use by the
City, the following documentation will be developed and adopted:
         a.   User guidelines;
         b.   Standards and processes for managing accounts on social media
sites; and
         c.   City and departmental branding standards.
   Q.   City websites shall not contain automatic feeds to uncensored social
media site content. Prior to approving content for display on City websites,
departments shall consult with DTI to ensure they have sufficient monitoring
protocols in place to ensure content and links are appropriate and free from
harmful technical attacks.
   R.   City of Albuquerque departments can develop their own social media
policy with additional rules and regulations. These departments must also
comply with the City of Albuquerque social media policy and their departmental
social media policy must be approved by the Communications Director.
   S.   The Albuquerque Police Department is responsible for keeping a list of
active Department social media sites.
      a.   Any APD division proposing a new social media site must obtain
approval from the APD Director of Communications.
      b.   This policy does not apply to any social media site that is part of
a law enforcement tactical operation.
   T.   Personal Social Media Accounts:
      a.   Do not use a City of Albuquerque email address when using social
media in a personal capacity. For example, don't create a personal Facebook or
Twitter account using your cabq.gov email address.
      b.   If you identify yourself as a City of Albuquerque employee when
conducting personal social media activities, consider stating in your profile
that your comments are not representative of the City of Albuquerque. Examples
include:
         i.    Twitter bio: Tweets are my own.
         ii.   Blog or website bio: While I work for the City of Albuquerque,
anything I publish is my personal opinion and should not be considered the
opinion or position of the City of Albuquerque.
      c.   Regardless of whether you identify your employment with the City of
Albuquerque on personal social media accounts, your status as a City employee
is public information. Accordingly, employees should be aware that any online
activity or commentary, whether made in a personal or professional capacity,
may be associated with their role as a representative of the City.
      d.   Nothing in this AI is meant to prevent an employee from exercising
his or her right to make a complaint of discrimination or other workplace
misconduct, engage in lawful collective bargaining activity, or to express an
opinion on a matter of public concern.
      e.   City employees may post about City-related programs, initiatives, or
events from their personal social media accounts only when they have received
prior written approval from their Department Director or designee. The content
must be factual, professional, and consistent with the employee's assigned
duties.
   17.   The following additional rules also apply to employees' use of social
media, on and offduty:
      a.   Social media content that relates to City business may be a public
record subject to retention and disclosure under state law. For that reason,
unless it is part of their official duties or they have received written
approval from their Department Director or designee as described in section T
( e ), employees are prohibited from using social media to conduct City
business.
      b.   Employees are required to protect and maintain the confidentiality
of all private and confidential City information.
      c.   Employees may not create a link from their blog, website or other
social networking site to a City website if such a link causes the viewer to
reasonably believe that the City endorses the contents of the employee's social
media site.
      d.   Employees may not use the City or Department's official logo for
personal online communications or activities except for incidental use allowed
by a written Department policy.
   18.   City officials will only use logos, slogans, signs, graphics, and
other media, consistent with Article XII, Section 6 of the City Charter.
References:

DESIGNATED AGENTS FOR ORDINANCE VIOLATION CITATIONS (2023)
ADMINISTRATIVE INSTRUCTION NO. 1-20 (2025)
TITLE: Designated Agents for Ordinance Violation Citations
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: General Services Department
Pursuant to my authority under Section 1-1-98 (B)(2) R.O.A. 1994, I hereby
authorize the General Services Department ("Department") to designate Officers
in the Metro Security Division as agents to issue Ordinance Violation Citations
when they have probable cause to believe that a person has violated any
ordinance of the City punishable by fine and/or imprisonment. Once designated
by the Department, the Officers will have the authority to issue citations for
violations of the following City ordinances:
   1.   § 5-8-6 R.O.A. 1994 (prohibited activities in open space)
   2.   § 7-2-2-1(B) R.O.A. 1994 (transit boarding area restrictions)
   3.   § 8-2-7-2 R.O.A. 1994 (occupying medians)
   4.   § 8-2-7-13 R.O.A. 1994 (articles obstructing sidewalks)
   5.   § 9-8-6 R.O.A. 1994 (litter in public places)
   6.   § 9-8-12R.O.A.1994 (litter in parks)
   7.   § 9-25-4 R.O.A. 1994 (unlawful camping)
   8.   § 9-25-5 R.O.A. 1994 (unlawful storage of personal property)
   9.   § 10-1-1-3(A)(3) R.O.A. 1994 (no structures in parks)
   10.   § 10-1-1-3(A)(4) R.O.A. 1994 (no shopping carts in parks)
   11.   § 10-1-1-10(A) (R.O.A. 1994 (occupying parks after closing time)
   12.   § 11-8-3 R.O.A. 1994 (public indecency)
   13.   § 12-2-3 R.O.A. 1994 (criminal trespass)
   14.   § 12-2-5 R.O.A. 1994 (disorderly conduct)
   15.   § 12-2-30 R.O.A. 1994 (camping in arroyos)
   16.   § 12-3-1 R.O.A. 1994 ( criminal damage to property)
   17.   § 12-3-8 R.O.A. 1994 (damaging or tampering with a vehicle)
   18.   § 12-4-8 R.O.A. 1994 (drinking in public)
   19.   § 12-4-14 R.O.A. 1994 (indecent exposure)
The Department shall develop an Ordinance Violation Citation form that meets
the requirements of the Ordinance.

AI NO: 2-1
ASSESSMENT OF INDIRECT OVERHEAD
TITLE:   Assessment of Indirect Overhead
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
   1.   City policy for Administrative Overhead - It is the City's policy to
recover for the General Fund, Internal Service Funds and Enterprise Funds costs
incurred in providing services to departments and agencies which are not
financed by the General Fund. Therefore, indirect costs will be assessed
against all applicable activities in accordance with the City's approved
Central Services Cost Allocation Plan, updated annually.
      a.   Charges for indirect costs are to be considered a basic element of
project and program budgets. They are not to be considered a residual after
other costs have been determined.
      b.   All grant applications must include: (i) a request for reimbursement
of any position working directly for the grant program, including department
fiscal staff, but not included in the indirect overhead plan; and (ii) a
request for the grantor to pay the indirect overhead amount applicable for the
year.
      c.   There are two types of administrative overhead rates: rates based on
percentage of wages and rates based on percentage of non-personnel operating
costs. A comparison of the two rates should be presented in the fiscal impact
analysis form submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). The
criteria for determining what method to use is below:
         1.   Rates based on percentage of wages - if a grant or project fund
has at least one full time equivalent employee, or the expenditures are
predominately made up of wages and fringe benefits, the indirect overhead rate
based on percentage of wages should be used. The administrative rate should be
applied to all wages (regular, overtime, and temporary).
         2.   Non-personnel rates based on total operating costs - If a grant
or project has less than one fulltime employee or operating & capital
expenditures make up the majority of the expenditures, the non-personnel rate
should be used. The non-personnel rate should be applied to all non-personnel
costs except transfers or indirect overhead.
         3.    Indirect costs are to be included in the following situations:
            ∙    All grant proposals when allowable.
            ∙    Setting rates for utilities.
            ∙    Establishing capital project budgets.
            ∙    As one of the elements of cost in the establishment of City
fees or other charges.
            ∙    Other appropriate areas.
      d.   An exception to the indirect cost assessment policy can be made if
the external funding source does not allow such costs or the external funding
is on a direct reimbursement for goods or services only. Such exceptions shall
require documentation from the external funding source.
      e.   Any other exceptions must be approved by the Director of Finance and
Administrative Services Department.
   2.   Direct Charges - In providing a specific service, if the hours used and
the hourly cost to provide the service can be isolated, the cost for the
service shall be billed directly when the service is provided.
   3.   Capital Overhead Rate - A rate to recover the costs of central service
support shall be charged to all capital projects.
      a.   The Capital Overhead Rates shall be calculated by the Department of
Finance and Administrative Services Director (“DFAS Director”). The Capital
Overhead Rates may be based on the ratio of the estimated central service costs
associated with the capital program to the estimated expenditures on capital
projects, and are subject to change during the fiscal year by the Director of
DFAS. The central service costs may include costs from DMD Construction in
Process (CIP) Fiscal, DFAS Director’s Office, Accounting, Budget, Purchasing
and Legal. Overhead rates on tax-exempt bonds are subject to federal
limitations.
      b.   All capital projects shall be assessed a capital overhead charge
equal to the project or department Capital Overhead Rate, as established by the
DFAS Director. It is a department's responsibility to seek an appropriation for
those projects that lack the resources to pay the capital overhead charge.
      c.    ny exemptions to capital indirect overhead charges must be approved
by the DFAS Director.
REFERENCES:   AI 2-26, Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200), Budget Ordinance § 2-11-17
APPLICATION FOR FEDERAL AND STATE GRANTS; BUDGETING FEDERAL FUNDS
