APPLICATION INTERFACE WITH PEOPLESOFT ERP SYSTEM
TITLE:   Application Interface with PeopleSoft ERP System
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Technology and Innovation
The citizens of the City of Albuquerque expect and deserve efficient and
effective local government. Delivering services most efficiently and
effectively entails prudent use of the resources provided to the City by its
constituency. Administrative support services – accounting, budgeting,
procurement, human resources, and others – can be delivered in a manner that
will facilitate more optimal primary City service delivery. The key is the
combination of enterprise-wide business practice standardization and re-
engineering with an integrated technology solution. As such, the City has
created a Program (the ERP Program) and chosen a software vendor (Oracle) to
drive widespread improvement in administrative value to citizens.
The City of Albuquerque owns and utilizes the Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise
Resource Planning (ERP) application as its primary administrative support
services system of record. One of the purposes of the ERP initiative is to
consolidate the work of as many of the organization’s functions and processes
as is practical and beneficial into a single enterprise resource planning tool.
This can be accomplished by utilization of the ERP system to replace all
current applications and systems that at their core are utilized to perform
accounting, budgeting, financial analysis, and human resources functions.
PeopleSoft and other integrated Oracle solutions are capable of fulfilling most
City business needs; however, the City recognizes that the need for specialized
solutions not offered by the PeopleSoft vendor will occasionally be required.
This need for an interfaced solution applies to both prospective and existing
applications. In such instances, a compelling business case will need to be
made to acquire the new software (or maintain the existing alternative) in lieu
of utilizing PeopleSoft ERP, as well as to interface a third party solution
with the ERP system.
Whenever a business need arises for an application solution, the City should
look first to its ERP vendor. Although a specialized solution may appear to be
superior to the ERP offering, the following issues/pitfalls with making the
non-ERP choice must be considered:
·   Most interfaces are two-way, as opposed to only one-way from the
specialized solution to PeopleSoft. The need to feed ERP data to the third-
party application increases the complexity of the interface.
·   Using non-ERP databases as repositories of detailed information compromises
auditability, reconciliation, and transparency.
·   Support risk increases significantly as City staff must own and maintain
knowledge of the specialized application as well as the PeopleSoft environment.
This risk is exacerbated with the introduction of upgrades to either the
interfaced application or ERP. Further, the number of contracts and vendor
relationships that have to be managed increases.
·   Consistency and standardization of business rules can easily be compromised
by the use of functionally and/or departmentally segmented applications.
·   Reporting needs can be met more efficiently when a single data repository
can be used for report building.
Policy
Effective immediately, existing City governance mechanisms will be utilized to
help ensure the most effective use of the ERP application, while providing
enterprise-wide consideration of proposed non-ERP solutions. Specifically, the
following process is to be used for vetting City needs for enterprise
technology solutions:
·   All proposals for business application solutions must be submitted to the
chairs of the ITSD Technology Review Committee (TRC) and the ERP Business
Alignment Committee (BAC), accompanied by a detailed business case (ERP Program
management should be consulted for assistance in business case development).
This submittal requirement applies to new acquisitions as well as proposals for
interfaces to existing City owned applications. Approval from these Committees
should be sought prior to beginning the solicitation process in the case of new
acquisition.
·   At a minimum, the business case should include the following elements:
   ·   Executive summary of the business need. The summary must include
designation of one individual from the proposing business unit as the proposed
project’s sponsor, as well as designation of a project manager who is a
functional staff member of the proposing business unit.
   ·   Analysis and description of business process improvements to accompany
the proposal;
   ·   If proposing a non-Oracle solution, the business justification for that
approach including a detailed functionality comparison with the relevant ERP
solution, highlighting the specific business needs unable to be accommodated by
ERP;
   ·   Summary of the specific benefits for the City of Albuquerque to be
derived from the proposal;
   ·   A preliminary project plan with critical path, resource requirements,
and resource dependencies;
   ·   Estimated cost budget, to include software license fees and maintenance
charges, consultancy fees, estimated benefits-loaded City staff project costs,
and other;
   ·   Return on investment (ROI) analysis, stated as the net present value
(NPV) of quantifiable benefits in excess of costs;
   ·   An overview of the software support plan.
·   All data proposed for interface with ERP must meet any and all regulatory
requirements.
·   The TRC and BAC will request and receive from the ERP Program Manager a
review and recommendation of the proposal, to include suggestions for revision
of the business case.
·   The TRC must approve requests for non-ERP applications, and the BAC must
approve requests to interface such solutions with the PeopleSoft system.
Approval of both governance bodies is required.
REFERENCES:   None

POLLUTION REMEDIATION OBLIGATIONS
TITLE:   Pollution Remediation Obligations
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Finance and Administrative Services
New Mexico State Statutes Section 12-6-12, NMSA 1978 and New Mexico
Administrative Code Section 2.2.2 requires the City to have an annual financial
and compliance audit in accordance with Governmental Accounting and Financial
Reporting Standards issued by the Governmental Accounting Standards Board. For
the City's 2009 annual audit and thereafter, the Department of Finance and
Administrative Services (DFAS) is now required to estimate the components of
expected pollution remediation outlays for the five event categories listed
below and determine whether the liability should be accrued in the City's
annual financial statements. All City departments are now required to
immediately notify the DFAS Director and Accounting Officer upon discovery of
one or more of the following events:
• The City is compelled to take pollution remediation action because of an
imminent endangerment;
• The City violates a pollution prevention related permit or license;
• The City is named, or evidence indicates mat it will be named, by a regulator
as a responsible party or potentially responsible party for remediation, or as
a government responsible for sharing costs;
• The City is named, or evidence indicates that it will be named, in a lawsuit
to compel participation in pollution remediation;
• The City commences or legally obligates itself to commence pollution
remediation; or
• The City is subject to cost attributed to compliance with environmental
regulations.
The measurement of the City's pollution remediation liability should include
remediation work that the City expects to perform for other parties less any
expected recoveries from third parties or insurance companies. The scope of
this administrative instruction as it relates to City department's obligation
to notify the DFAS excludes pollution prevention or control obligations with
respect to current operations, and future pollution remediation activities that
are required upon retirement of an asset, such as landfill closure and
postclosure care. Departments should plan and budget for required environmental
cost similar to their other departmental operations.
REFERENCES: New Mexico State Statutes Section 12-6-12, NMSA 1978 and New Mexico
Administrative Code Section 2.2.2

PROCEDURES FOR APPLYING AND IMPLEMENTING FEDERAL/STATE GRANTS
TITLE:   Procedures for Applying and Implementing Federal/State Grants
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Finance and Administrative Services
Background:
This administrative instruction is intended to provide guidance and
interpretation to Budget Ordinance § 2-11-17 APPLICATION FOR FEDERAL AND STATE
GRANTS; BUDGETING FEDERAL FUNDS.
GRANTS SUBJECT TO THIS RULE: This process applies to all grants implemented by
City Departments, both capital and operating.
Each Department (Managing Department for the grant) is responsible for ensuring
that all grant reporting requirements, drawdowns and other activities are
current. The Department is also responsible for ensuring that all grant
activity is properly recorded in the City’s accounting system and prior year
grants are properly closed out with the grantor agency and the City’s
Department of Finance and Administrative Services Department Accounting
Division Grants Section. The Department should not apply for new grants if
reporting and accounting requirements are delinquent for current or prior year
grants; should extenuating circumstances require the application, contact the
Grant Administrator immediately.
Procedures:
1.   PRE-APPLICATION CONFERENCE:
a)   When a Department contemplates applying for a grant, a pre-application
conference must be scheduled as follows:
   i)   If the prospective grant is an operating grant, the pre-application
meeting must include representatives from the Department applying for the
grant, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and the Accounting Division
Grants Section of the Department of Finance and Administrative Services (DFAS).
   ii)   If the prospective grant is a capital grant, the Fiscal Division of
Capital Implementation Program (CIP) of the Department of Municipal Development
should be substituted in lieu of OMB as a required representative.
   iii)   The Department must:
      (1)   Prepare a draft resolution, fiscal impact analysis and application
(when applicable) for review at the meeting; and
      (2)   Provide the name of the Department manager for the grant (an update
of Department grant contacts will be required each April by DFAS Accounting
Division Grants Section); and
      (3)   Use the applicable City Department’s Dun and Bradstreet (D & B)
identification number (DUNS number) if required. The DUNS number shall be
supplied by the Treasury Division of DFAS; and
      (4)   Include the indirect overhead charge per Administrative Instruction
2-1. (If a waiver is contemplated, a draft waiver must be provided at the pre-
application conference.) Ensure inclusion of the current predetermined indirect
cost rate in the grant application.
2.   SUBMISSION TO COUNCIL: Upon review and agreement among the Department,
OMB/CIP and DFAS Accounting Division, the Department shall submit a resolution
for introduction to City Council prior to submitting the application to the
grantor agency. If the grant application deadline is prior to the next regular
meeting of the Council, the application may be submitted to the grantor agency
prior to Council approval, but then must be submitted to the Council at its
next regular meeting. All grant applications must be approved by Council
except:
a)   Applications for less than $1,500 where the matching funds have already
been budgeted or the award does not require a monetary match or have any future
financial implications for the City.
3.   SUBMITTING THE GRANT APPLICATION TO THE GRANTOR AGENCY: All grant
applications must be signed by the Department Director or his/her authorized
designee. A designee must be authorized in writing and a copy of the
authorization must be submitted to the City’s Department of Finance and
Administrative Services Department Accounting Division Grants Section’s Grant
Administrator.
4.   COUNCIL ACTION: If Council approves the application, the Department shall
submit the application, accept the award and expend with no further action by
the Council. However, under the following conditions the grant agreement must
be introduced to Council for consideration:
a)   conditions are subsequently added to the grant agreement which have major
financial or policy implications for the City. (A major financial implication
is defined as an increase of 10%, in the commitment of City funds or resources.
A major policy change is defined as a change in the goals, objectives and
proposed programs included in the grant.)
b)   if it is an ongoing grant that does not require application and the
agreement is only seen by the City at the award stage.
Council may approve, take no action, disapprove, or recommend revision to the
proposed agreement with or without conditioning approval on the adoption of
such revisions. If no action is taken within 21 days from the date of the
Council meeting immediately following receipt of the proposed agreement, the
Department may proceed with the grant process as if approval had been granted.
5.   AWARD OF THE GRANT: The following events shall be promptly executed after
notification of award:
a)   The Department’s grant manager will coordinate with the Accounting
Division Grants Section/CIP to set up a project, activity number, contract,
rate plan/set and budget plan for the operating/capital grant. The grant must
be approved on the City’s financial system by Accounting Division Grant
Section/CIP before any expenditures, including payroll, are incurred;
   i)   Departments shall not charge expenditures to incorrect funding strings
pending setup of the grant in the City’s accounting software;
   ii)   Departments may set up a new grant in advance of receiving the final
award notification, with the approval of the Grant Administrator and the OMB,
if:
      (1)   There is reasonable certainty of receiving the award (e.g. a grant
is awarded every year) and an alternative funding source is identified in the
event the award is cancelled; or
      (2)   The grant comes with pre-award spending authority;
b)   The Department will be notified of the approved grant budget plan (on the
City’s financial system) as follows:
   i)   Operating Grants: the Budget Office will approve the Budget Plan after
being notified by Accounting Division Grants Section that the grant has been
properly established;
   ii)    Capital grants: CIP will approve the Budget Plan for all Capital
grants;
c)   Departments and/or grant managers will inform the Accounting Division
Grants Section of the drawdown/reimbursement request procedures per the grant
and provide all necessary information to perform these procedures for operating
grants.
d)   Quarterly Federal Financial Reports (SF-425) will be prepared by the
grantee Department and submitted to Accounting Division Grants Section for
review and approval prior to submission to the grantor agency.
6.   GRANT FUNDS/ACTIVITIES
a)    All grant financial transactions must be recorded to exclusive grant
funds and project activities for both operating and capital grants, as assigned
by Accounting Division Grants Section/CIP.
b)   All City Departments shall use the City’s financial software to bill
grantors for funds due to the City; financial software billing must occur at
the time of grantor report preparation and request for reimbursement;
c)   Grant funds and project activities shall be structured to facilitate the
reconciliation of federal, state, local, and non-governmental grant
transactions to financial software billing and reporting required by the grant
award, the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (SEFA) and the City’s
Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR); City matching funds must be
appropriated within the grant project; depending on the specifics of the grant,
a separate activity ID may need to be used to segregate city match revenue/
expenditures from grantor revenue/expenditures.
7.   ACCOUNTING, REPORTING, MONITORING AND AUDIT REQUIREMENTS:
Accounting shall:
a)   Ensure that Journal Entries, Journal Vouchers, and Adjust Paid Entry
adjustments are reviewed and posted in a timely manner to facilitate grant
billing and reporting;
b)   Ensure that the general ledger is closed on a monthly basis so that
Departments may accurately bill and report on the financial status of their
grants;
c)   Provide assistance, guidance and training to Departments in order to
ensure they may timely and properly account, report, bill, reconcile and
closeout their grants; and
d)   Serve as the lead for the City’s annual audit, including the Single Audit.
Grantee Departments must:
a)   Oversee, monitor and administer grant compliance from acceptance to
closeout;
b)   Understand the administrative compliance and special terms and conditions,
if any, as well as laws and regulations related to the grant award;
c)   If the funding source is Federal, a grantee Department shall determine
whether vendors are subrecipients or contractors per Federal guidelines and
ensure that contracts with subrecipients and/or contractors comply with all
Federal requirements, including required clauses and compliance with the
Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act Subaward Reporting System;
d)   Monitor and oversee subrecipients, subrecipient reporting, audit results,
etc. as required by the grant award;
e)   Maintain accurate, current and complete disclosure of the financial
results of activities funded in whole or in part by the grant;
f)   Maintain records which adequately identify sources and applications of
funds, including authorizations, obligations, un-obligated balances, assets,
liabilities, outlays or expenditures and income;
g)    Upload into the accounting software all grant-related documentation
including, but not limited to: legislation, award letter, application,
contract/agreement, interim reports, final reports, and formal correspondence
with the grantor agency;
h)   Maintain effective control and accountability over the grant;
i)   Comply with City Procurement Code (City of Albuquerque Code of Ordinances,
Article 5) as well as Federal, State or grantor agency procurement requirements
as applicable;
j)   Submit financial reports to the grantor agency by the deadlines required
under the grant award; Federal Financial Reports (SF-425) reports must be
submitted to Accounting Division Grants Section for review and approval prior
to submission to the Federal agency;
k)   Comply with all requirements of and requests related to the Single Audit
Act of 1996 (2 CFR Part 200 Subpart F);
l)    Understand and provide to Accounting Division’s Grants Section of DFAS
information required to be presented on the Schedule of Expenditure of Federal
Awards (SEFA), as well as underlying audit and roll-forward schedules, by the
required due dates;
m)   Understand and provide to the Accounting Division Grants Section of DFAS
the grant’s line item budget including chart of accounts to be used related to
the grant;
n)   Monitor and record all revenue, including program income, related to the
grant and comply with all grant requirements related to the revenue;
o)    Maintain detailed support of in-kind services received and/or provided as
well as donations of property received in relation to the grant;
p)   Identify the type of financial transactions to be incurred and how to
properly record the transactions prior to incurring expenditures related to the
grant;
q)   Ensure that all expenditures charged to the grant are allowable per the
grant agreement, grant budget, and any special terms and conditions;
r)   Defer any advance grant payments until the revenue is earned by incurring
expenditures related to these advances;
s)   Maintain supplemental records related to assets purchased with grant funds
as required by the Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200.313(d)(1)) and grantor agency;
t)   Within 10 days of receiving an amendment, enter appropriate changes/
adjustments into the City’s financial software and notify Accounting Division
Grants Section to perform the amendment review, enter processing changes and
initiate budget finalization, as applicable;
u)   Comply with the City’s Conflict of Interest Policy (Sections 300 and 311.7
of the City Personnel Manual) and the City’s Code of Ethics (Charter of the
City of Albuquerque, Article XII, Section 4)
8.   GRANTOR COMMUNICATION AND AUDITS/REVIEWS:
a)   Any communication outside of normal program and/or fiscal communication
must be forwarded to Accounting Division Grants Section. Such communication
includes, but is not limited to, notifications of:
   i)   grantor agency review or audit
   ii)   violations of terms and conditions
   iii)   requirement to repay grant funds
b)   If a grantor provides notice of an official review or audit, follow the
requirements of Administrative Instruction 2-22 and forward the notice to the
Grant Administrator. At a minimum, the Grant Administrator will attend Entrance
and Exit Conferences, and Accounting Division’s Grants Section staff will be
available and involved in the review/audit to the extent necessary.
9.   GRANT REVENUE:
a)   DRAWDOWN: With the exception of the grant drawdowns prepared by the
Accounting Division Grants Section, the Department is responsible for and shall
drawdown through electronic funds transfers and/or request reimbursement of
expenditures no less than on a quarterly basis:
   i)   According to the terms and conditions of the grant;
   ii)   Upon billing the grant in the accounting software; and
   iii)   Upon receipt of signed Financial Status Reports from the Departments
for Federal grants, reconciled to the general ledger, and supporting
documentation.
b)   REQUEST FOR REIMBURSEMENT:
   i)   According to the terms and conditions of the grant;
   ii)   Upon billing the grant in the accounting software; and
   iii)   Upon completion of grantor agency required reports and supporting
documentation.
c) CIP managed grants: CIP will bill and drawdown/request reimbursement for
Capital projects they administer.
10.   CLOSE OUT: Grants are considered complete either when all work set forth
under the agreement has been performed or on the date grant support is
scheduled to end. If a grantee does not seek a supplemental grant or a no-cost
extension on or before the completion date, the grant is closed out with the
grantor agency by submitting all final performance, financial and other
required reports; adjusting the grantor agency share of costs, upward or
downward, if necessary; and settling any cash balances:
a)   Within 90 days of grant closing (having expired in term, expenditure and/
project), the recipient Department must provide a complete reconciliation to
Accounting and OMB/CIP. The reconciliation must include a copy of the Notice of
Termination or pay reimbursement marked final. If the grantor agency’s deadline
for final reporting and reimbursement is less than 90 days after the
expiration, the final reconciliation and reports will be submitted to OMB/CIP
on or before the grantor agency’s due date.
b)   Accounting will have the responsibility for ensuring all final
transactions are properly posted, disallowing any further transactions to be
posted to the grant and properly closing out the grant within the accounting
system.
11.    RECORD RETENTION: Program and financial records related to the grant are
required to be retained at least seven years and no more than ten years if
records are under audit, involving audit findings or involved in appeals or
litigation.
REFERENCES:   Budget Ordinance § 2-11-17 APPLICATION FOR FEDERAL AND STATE
GRANTS; BUDGETING FEDERAL FUNDS; City Procurement Code (City of Albuquerque
Code of Ordinances, Article 5); Federal Financial Reports (SF-425) reports;
Administrative Instruction 2-22 Internal and External Audits and Report
Responses; City’s Conflict of Interest Policy (Sections 300 and 311.7 of the
City Personnel Manual); City’s Code of Ethics (Charter of the City of
Albuquerque, Article XII, Section 4); Federal Conflict of Interest policies;
Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200); Administrative Instruction 2-1

AI NO: 2-27
SEGREGATION OF COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH COVID-19 (2020)
TITLE: Segregation of Costs Associated with COVID-19
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Finance and Administrative Services
BACKGROUND
The City of Albuquerque, the State of New Mexico and the United States have
declared an emergency due to the spread of the novel coronavirus. The City will
request financial aid from appropriate state and federal agencies to assist in
responding to the outbreak of COVID-19. This AI addresses the tracking of costs
related to COVID19 for all payroll and purchase transactions. Thus, to the
extent any request for reimbursement will require documentation, the City must
be able to accurately identify all costs associated with COVID-19.
Documentation includes the following: invoices, receipts, payroll timesheets,
etc.
A summary of allowable expenditures covered under Federal Guidelines is
attached in this link: https://tinyurl.com/CABQ-COVID-resources 
PAYROLL POLICY AND TASK PROFILES
Employees performing functions outside of their normal job duties should
segregate that time and charge it to the COVID19 funding string and identify
the COVID-specific work performed.
Employees performing their normal job functions should charge their hours as
regular hours worked (REG pay code).
If an employee is performing a function outside of his or her normal functions
directly related to COVID-19, the task profile dedicated to this work must be
utilized. Use task profile COVID19 and the proper pay code (REG, OCB, OPL,
ETC).
Kronos:
COVID19 task profile is available to all City departments.
   1.   Each employee performing a function outside of his or her normal
functions directly related to COVID-19 must submit by email a timesheet
identifying the time spent and specific activity so that for each day the
manager can input the time into Kronos related to COVID before payroll is
processed. Managers must send the timesheets to timekeepers as backup.
Timekeepers must also send the timesheets to covidrecoveryteam@cabq.gov as
backup for any potential grants. Comments must be added to identify the
specific assignment task and/or location related to COVID-19.
   2.   Managers must record the time to COVID19 before payroll is processed.
If the employee is unable to send their timesheet, they will be allowed to
submit it when they return to work.
Telestaff (APD/AFR):
Each employee performing a function outside of his or her normal functions
directly related to COVID-19 must enter the appropriate task profile/work code
identifying the time spent and specific activity.
Trapeze:
Time Schedulers will need to track hours for drivers who directly work on
COVID-19 related tasks and are required to submit a timesheet for each driver
that identifies the work assignment and description. Time Schedulers must also
send the timesheets to covidrecoveryteam@cabq.gov.
PAY CODES:  
Employees who are working from home as instructed by their Director should do
so in accordance with Administrative Instruction 7-30 TELECOMMUNITING/WORK FROM
HOME DURING THE COVID-19 OUTBREAK (2020). Use normal pay codes for the
position.
PEM:
Employees who have called in sick with the virus or have self-quarantined due
to travel or potential exposure, or taking care of a symptomatic family member,
he or she should be provided leave under the pay code “PEM.” Each employee will
be required to fill out a paper timesheet if they do not have access to the
system. The paper timesheet will need to be signed by the employee and manager
and sent to the time keepers and used as backup to the time paid. Send a copy
of the timesheet to covidrecoveryteam@cabq.gov.
PEW:
Employees that are able to work but are being sent home in accordance with AI
7-59, and cannot telework, he or she should be provided leave under the pay
code “PEW.” The employee will be required to fill out a paper timesheet if they
do not have access to the system. The paper timesheet will need to be signed by
the employee and manager and sent to the time keepers and used as backup to the
time paid. Send a copy of the timesheet to covidrecoveryteam@cabq.gov.
PEC: (EFFECTIVE 4/2/2020)
Per the Families First Coronavirus Response Act effective 4/2/2020: Employees
who are required to report to work but are unable due to child care issues
should code their time as “PEC”. The paper timesheet will need to be signed by
the employee and manager and sent to the time keepers and used as backup to the
time paid. Send a copy of the timesheet to covidrecoveryteam@cabq.gov.
Links:
Link to access the instructions on how to assign a task profile and enter pay
codes in
Kronos: https://tinyurl.com/CABQ-COVID-resources
Link to access the timesheet: https://tinyurl.com/CABQ-COVID-resources
 
PURCHASES POLICY
Procurements related to COVID19 must be in alignment with federal and city
guidelines and must utilize the funding string specific for COVID-19, with the
proper account number identified on the chart of accounts:
Fund          265
PCBU         PCDFA
Project         25_20_COVID19

TIME REPORTING AND APPROVAL POLICY
TITLE: TIME REPORTING and APPROVAL POLICY
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Finance & Administrative Services
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide work time reporting requirements for
all City of Albuquerque employees.
DEFINITIONS:
"Clock in" and "Punch in" (or out) means the method to register one's arrival
or departure from work by use of a time clock attendance system.
"Exception" based reporting for completing timecards means an employee is not
required to use the time clock to record hours worked. A standard total of work
hours is scheduled for payment each pay period and the employee records only
approved leave time.
POLICY:
1.   The City of Albuquerque requires all employees to accurately record work
hours and approved leave (annual leave, sick leave, educational leave, jury
duty, leave without pay, etc.). Federal and State laws require the City of
Albuquerque to keep an accurate record of time worked in order to calculate
employee pay and benefits. In addition, correct and complete timekeeping is
essential to:
   a.   Ensure employees are paid in a uniform and consistent manner in
accordance with applicable laws, rules, regulations, standards, and collective
bargaining agreements.
   b.   Provide accountability to the public. All City records, including
payroll and personnel records must be prepared factually and accurately. It is
the personal obligation of the employee completing such records as well as the
supervisor to ensure that such records are accurate and comply with federal,
state, and City record-keeping and accounting requirements.
   c.   Ensure compliance with Section 30-23-2 NMSA 1978 which makes it a
felony (timecard fraud) for public employees to receive public money for
services not rendered except for lawful remuneration to public employees for
vacation periods or absences from work due to sickness or for other lawfully
authorized purposes such as designated legal holidays.
2.   The City of Albuquerque utilizes an electronic timekeeping system, Kronos,
TeleStaff and Trapeze, as authorized timekeeping systems to report, approve,
and submit employees' work and approved leave to the Department of Finance and
Administrative Services (DFAS) for payment of wages at the end of each pay
period.
3.   Departments using other timekeeping systems that interface into Kronos are
responsible for ensuring time repo1ied is approved and accurate and for
maintaining a record.
4.   All employees must accurately record time off.
5.   Exempt employees may record their time worked on an exception basis.
Exempt employees are required to request and record approved leave in
accordance with City policies.
6.   It is the responsibility of each employee to ensure that their electronic
timecard is complete and accurate.
   a.   Employees are responsible for approving their own electronic timecard,
and by doing so, the employee is attesting that, to the best of his/her
knowledge, the information submitted is complete and accurate.
   b.   Regardless of who entered the time, employees are responsible for any
inaccuracy or omission of which the employee is aware at the time the
electronic timecard is approved and submitted.
   c.   Employees, Managers/Supervisors may not at any time share passwords to
any timekeeping systems.
   d.   Managers/Supervisors of employees are responsible for the review and
correction of missed clock in or out punches, and for making edits to
employees' time as needed.
   e.   Managers/Supervisors are responsible for approving work time submitted
by their employees at the end of each pay period by the date and time
designated by the Payroll Office.
   f.   By approving an employee's timecard, each Manager/Supervisor is
attesting that, to the best of his/her knowledge, the employee's electronic
timecard is complete and accurate.
7.   All overtime work must be pre-approved by the employee's supervisor. At
times, it may not be possible to receive prior approval before working overtime
due to emergencies or other unanticipated situations. In such cases, employees
must notify their supervisor of the overtime worked as soon as possible.
8.   If an employee works unauthorized ove1iime the appropriate compensation
will be made for all time reported as worked. However, the employee may be
subject to disciplinary action for failure to obtain the necessary supervisory
approval to work overtime.
9.   No leave accruals shall be advanced by the employer. Thus, no leave
balance shall ever result in a negative number.
10.   Nothing in this Administrative Instruction prohibits a Department from
establishing more specific or specialized policies regarding timekeeping or
overtime.
PROCEDURES:
1.   Requests for time off are completed through the Kronos, TeleStaff or
Trapeze systems. Time off must be requested in accordance with the City of
Albuquerque Personnel Rules and Regulations or the employee's applicable
collective bargaining union agreement.
2.   Employees may use only the amount of leave available. Requests for amounts
of leave in excess of available leave will be requested through Supervisors/
Managers.
3.   Approval or denial of leave requests by Supervisors/Managers will also be
completed through Kronos, TeleStaff or Trapeze.
REFERENCES:
§30-23-2 NMSA 1978
Fair Labor Standards Act
City of Albuquerque Personnel Rules and Regulations

STANDARD AGREEMENT PROVISIONS FOR ARCHITECTURAL, ENGINEERING AND LANDSCAPE
ARCHITECTURAL SERVICES FOR THE CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE
TITLE:   Standard Agreement Provisions for Architectural, Engineering and
Landscape Architectural Services for the City of Albuquerque
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Municipal Development
All procurement of engineering, architectural or landscape architectural
services made pursuant to the Selection Advisory Committee Ordinance shall
require any offeror submitting a proposal to perform such services to state in
the proposal that the offeror agrees, if selected, to enter into an agreement
with the City of Albuquerque which contains the standard terms and conditions
found in the model Engineering, Architectural and Landscape Architectural
Services Agreement dated October 1, 2001 as amended, which is incorporated
herein by reference.
The model Engineering Services Agreement, Landscape Architectural Services
Agreement and Architectural Services Agreement shall be the Agreement entered
into for all Architectural, Engineering or Landscape Architectural Services
that are exempt from the Selection Advisory Committee Ordinance except for
ancillary engineering, architectural or landscaping, architectural services
procured through construction contracts such as pre-engineered metal buildings,
manufactured shade structures, specific lighting design or similar services.
Changes in the provisions of the referenced model agreements shall be approved
by the City Attorney and the Department of Municipal Development Director or
their designees in advance of any requests for such services, and such changes
shall be contained in the model agreements made available to all those
responding to the solicitation.
REFERENCES:   Engineering, Architectural and Landscape Architectural Services
Agreement, dated October 1, 2001.

ACQUISITION OF AUDIT SERVICES
TITLE:   Acquisition of Audit Services
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
The acquisition of services for audits of the City's financial records, other
statistical and management information, or any agreed upon procedures which are
to be performed by external auditors shall be coordinated by the Department of
Finance and Administrative Services, Accounting Division. This administrative
instruction applies to all financial audits as well as grant compliance
financial and nonfinancial audits. Requests for such audits will be approved by
the Chief Administrative Officer upon recommendation of the Director of Finance
and Administrative Services.
At the time that a City department identifies the need for an additional
independent annual audit, it will formally transmit a request for such an audit
to the Accounting Division, identifying the need for and the scope of the audit
to be performed. This request shall indicate a desired completion date, cost,
distribution and any other requirements. If notified in a timely manner, the
Accounting Division will negotiate each year with the State Auditor, so that
each year the independent audit contract for the City's annual audit will also
include an amount for audits which may be performed in addition to the City's
annual financial audit (an umbrella contract that includes extra audit work).
The extra audit work is based on an estimate of the audit requirements.
If a City department identifies the need for an independent audit not
identified in the annual requirement, the Accounting Division, in conjunction
with the affected department, will discuss audit requirements with the
independent auditors of record and arrive at the cost to perform such work. If
the audit is identified as additional scope, the department will follow rules
set out in the Procurement Ordinance, which may require approval from City
Council. Should the estimated audit costs for an audit exceed the purchasing
ordinance limits, the Accounting Division will assist the affected department
in the preparation and circulation of an RFP.
REFERENCES:
Article 5: Public Purchases Ordinance, §5-5-28 Competitive Sealed Bids and 5-5-
30 Competitive Sealed Proposals

SMALL PURCHASES AND USE OF LOCAL VENDORS (2022)
TITLE: Small Purchases and Use of Local Vendors
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1.   Small Purchases
   A.   General
      (1)   The Small Purchase procurement methodology allows for purchases of
goods and services without competition or approval from the Central Purchasing
Division of the Department of Finance and Administrative Services (Purchasing
Division) when the total purchase price for all years that the product or good
will be purchased does not exceed the amounts set forth in the Public Purchases
Ordinance, Section 5-5-26.
      (2)   Except where funding of a program or operation is derived in whole
or in part from federal grant funding, purchases using the Small Purchase
procurement methodology shall be made from local vendors when feasible and not
cost prohibitive, as defined herein.
   B.   Application
      (1)   Each Department shall determine which City employees in that
Department are approved to make Small Purchase expenditures. Small Purchases
shall be made in accordance with the policies and procedures stated herein, the
Public Purchases Ordinance, and the Purchasing Rules and Regulations. All
purchases shall be made strictly for City business.
      (2)   Purchases made using the Small Purchase methodology shall be made
at the best obtainable price. For the purposes of this Administrative
Instruction, "best obtainable price" means the most competitive price at which
services or goods can be purchased, with consideration to other factors that
are important to the City, such as experience with a vendor, match to
specifications and customer service. Best obtainable price can be found by
obtaining quotes; based on research, experience, or purchase history; or other
appropriate methods to allow for a diligent review. The Department shall
maintain a record of the best obtainable price review in its procurement file
for the purchase.
      (3)   Employees shall not make Small Purchases of goods or services that
are available from pre-established, City-wide contracts or price agreements or
City punchouts.
      (4)   Employees shall not split purchases into two or more transactions
to bring the purchase amount below the Small Purchase transaction limit set
forth in the Public Purchases Ordinance, Section 5-5-26.
      (5)   Employees shall not use the Small Purchases procurement methodology
for repetitive purchases of the same item and/or the same item with the same
vendor. If a Department needs to make such repetitive purchases, those goods or
services must be procured by another authorized procurement methodology
established by the Purchasing Division.
   C.   Procedure for Payment
      (1)   Payments for Small Purchases may be made in one of the following
ways:
         (a)   Peoplesoft Accounting Quick Invoice entry up to small purchase
transaction limit set forth in the Public Purchases Ordinance, Section 5-5-26,
as may be authorized by DFAS Accounts Payable;
         (b)   P-Card use up to approved p-card limit; or
         (c)   Purchase Order up to the Small Purchase transaction limit set
forth in the Public Purchases Ordinance, Section 5-5-26.
      (2)   The Accounts Payable Division will conduct periodic audits of
entries made into the PeopleSoft Accounting Quick Invoice system.
      (3)   All purchases by P-card shall comply with the P-card regulations
set forth in the City's P-card Manual.
      (4)   For Purchase Orders, use the Small Purchase PO requisition type.
      (5)   Employees shall not purchase airline tickets or travel-related
expenditures through either the Quick Invoice or P-card programs. Employees
shall make travel-related expenditures in accordance with the City of
Albuquerque Travel Regulations located at https://partner.cabq.gov/CityTravel/
default.aspx. Travel for non-City employees is not addressed in the City of
Albuquerque Travel Regulations. Questions about purchasing travel for non-City
employees should be directed to a Department's Department Buyer.
      (6)   The payment of Small Purchases with Petty Cash is highly
discouraged. A Petty Cash account must be approved by the DFAS Treasury
Division.
   D.   Use of Local Businesses.
      (1)   Except where funding of a program or operation is derived in whole
or in part from federal grant funding, purchases shall be made from local
businesses, when feasible and not cost prohibitive, unless granted an exception
by a representative from the City's Buy Local Initiative.
      (2)   "Cost prohibitive" means the total cost is at least twenty percent
(20%) more than the total price for comparable goods or services.
      (3)   When deciding how to use local businesses for procurements, the
tier structure identified in the Procurement Rules and Regulations shall be
used to prioritize the order. In the Procurement Rules and Regulations, the
tiers for "Local" include those entities headquartered within the Greater
Albuquerque Metropolitan Area, as defined by the Public Purchases Ordinance,
Section 5-5-3 as well as those doing business locally and within the State of
New Mexico.
Questions with regard to any issue on Small Purchases are to be directed to a
Department's Department Buyer. Questions with regard to using local businesses
are to be directed to a representative from the City's Buy Local Initiative.
REFERENCES: City Ordinance Article 5 R.O.A. 1994 Public Purchases Ordinance,
Administrative Instruction 3-3; City of Albuquerque Travel Rules and
Regulations; 2 CFR Part 200.
This Administrative Instruction is effective immediately.

VENDOR AND CITY RELATIONS AND MANAGING VENDOR PERFORMANCE (2021)
TITLE: Vendor and City Relations and Managing Vendor Performance
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1.   Purpose and Scope
This Administrative Instruction sets forth the requirements for relationships
between the City of Albuquerque ("City") and vendors ("Vendors") and managing
Vendor performance. Pursuant to Section 5-5-25 of the City of Albuquerque
Public Purchases Ordinance, Section 5 of this Administrative Instruction,
Vendor Noncompliance, does not apply to Capital Improvement Projects (CIP).
2.   Vendor and City Relations
   A.   The following ethical conduct rules are applicable to all City
employees, officials, and Vendors engaged in procurement with the City:
      1   City of Albuquerque Charter: Article XII: Code of Ethics
      2   City of Albuquerque Public Purchases Ordinance, Section 5-5-22 ROA
1994
      3   City of Albuquerque Ordinance, Chapter 3, Article 3: Conflicts
oflnterest
      4   The State Governmental Conduct Act, NMSA 1978, Chapter 10, Article 16
   B.   Vendors shall not pay for City employees' travel expenses. This section
shall not apply to reimbursements for City employees' travel expenses incurred
as a result of active participation in presentations or workshops. Provided
however, that all such requests for approval of travel reimbursement shall be
submitted in advance of the proposed travel to the Department Director (or CAO
if the Director is the person proposing travel) and shall include the purpose
of the presentation or workshop, name of the Vendor or firm, names of
individuals traveling, and the benefit of the trip to the City and the
employee's City Department.
   C.   In order to ensure objective Vendor performance and eliminate unfair
competitive advantage, Vendors that develop or draft specifications,
requirements, statements of work, or requests for bids or requests for
proposals shall be excluded from competing for such procurements. For the
purpose of this Administrative Instruction, "develop or draft" shall mean all
active participation, by a vendor, in the drafting or development of
specifications, requirements, statements of work, or requests for bids or
requests for proposals following the City's decision to affirmatively move
forward on a competitive solicitation. This section shall not apply to problem
based competitive solicitations, in which the development or drafting of
specifications, requirements, statements of work, or requests for bids or
requests for proposals are conducted in a public setting and open to the
general public to participate. The participation of a vendor in a public
meeting, survey, questionnaire, town hall or similar event shall not be deemed
to be participation in development or drafting. Questions about the timing of
Vendor participation in development or drafting shall be directed to the Chief
Procurement Officer.
   D.   The City shall not draft specifications in such a way as to limit the
number of Vendors that would be eligible to submit responses.
3.   Department Responsibilities Relating to Vendor Performance
A statement of work or scope of services should provide the Department clear
direction for measuring Vendor performance. The goal of managing Vendor
performance is to ensure that contractual requirements are satisfactorily
performed and the responsibilities of both parties are properly discharged.
Effective management of Vendor performance helps to minimize problems and
potential claims and disputes. With regard to Vendor performance, the
responsibilities of the Department consist of the following:
   A.   Participate in the development of the solicitation or contract by
writing the specifications, statements of work, or scope of services, or by
providing a subject matter expert who can assist in the development of well-
defined specifications, statements of work, or scopes of services.
   B.   Notify the Department of Finance and Administrative Services Purchasing
Division ("Purchasing Division") if federal or other source grant funds will be
used to procure the goods or services, and identify all applicable federal or
other grant requirements associated with the funding agency or source.
   C.   Ensure the Department and Vendor have executed a contract and released
a Purchase Order before shipment of the goods or commencement of the services.
   D.   The Department, and a representative of the Purchasing Division, may
conduct a post-award conference with the Vendor to ensure that all parties
understand the terms of the contract and performance requirements. The post
award conference shall not change the terms of the solicitation or contract.
   E.   Monitor the Vendor's progress and performance to ensure that goods and
services conform to the contractual requirements.
   F.   Conduct a thorough inspection of all goods purchased to ensure that
they comply with contractual requirements. Inspections of goods shall be upon
receipt unless otherwise provided by contract or Purchase Order. The receiving
Department shall also inspect and validate that the services being performed on
behalf of the City by the Vendor have been performed and completed in
accordance with contractual requirements.
   G.   Coordinate with the Department's fiscal representative on submission
and approval of change orders and/or amendments to Purchase Orders and/or
contract terms. A Department shall not authorize a Vendor, either verbally or
in writing, to provide goods or services prior to execution of a fully approved
change order or contract amendment.
   H.   Maintain records that detail the history of the purchase, including but
not necessarily limited to, the following: Rationale for the method of
procurement, selection of contract type, contractor selection or rejection, and
the basis for the contract price, the original contract and all amendments.
   I.   Close out the contract to verify that both parties have fulfilled their
contractual obligations and there are no remaining contractual obligations to
be completed.
   J.   Report Vendor noncompliance to the Purchasing Division, using the
process set forth herein.
4.   Vendor Responsibilities to the City
   A.   Vendors shall comply with all Terms and Conditions of contracts
executed with and Purchase Orders issued by the City. Vendors shall not seek to
impose Terms and Conditions that have not been agreed to by the City, and
include in the Terms and Conditions of executed contracts or issued Purchase
Orders, or are otherwise against City policy.
   B.   Vendors shall reply to notices of noncompliance within the deadlines
set forth in the notice and comply with any corrective action plan that may be
established as provided herein.
5.   Vendor Noncompliance Reporting, Investigation, and Corrective Action
   A.   Departments are responsible for documenting vendor noncompliance with
contract provisions and any other performance issues related to business with
the City. To report noncompliance events, a Department shall complete and
submit the Vendor Noncompliance Form in Peoplesoft forms (or a successor form
provided by Purchasing) with supporting documentation explaining the
noncompliance, including dates and individuals involved, and the Department's
efforts in communicating the noncompliance to the vendor.
   B.   For purposes of this Administrative Instruction, noncompliance includes
but is not limited to: (i)   failure to deliver goods and services when
specified; (ii) noncompliance with the Terms and Conditions, technical
specifications, scope of work, or scope of services of the contract or Purchase
Order; (iii) being nonresponsive to requests for information or performance;
(iv) being non-responsible as provided in the City of Albuquerque Purchasing
Rules and Regulations; (iv) failing to obtain a Purchase Order prior to sending
goods or providing services; and (v) continued failure to properly and timely
invoice the City.
   C.   The Chief Procurement Officer or designee, upon receipt of a Vendor
noncompliance form, will investigate the issue. If required, the Chief
Procurement Officer or designee will schedule a meeting with the Department and
Vendor to establish a corrective action plan as quickly as reasonably possible.
The Chief Procurement Officer or designee will ensure that any required follow-
up action is tracked and, if necessary, appropriate other action taken, up to
and including termination of the vendor's contract and/or Purchase Order, and
possible suspension or debarment proceedings
This Administrative Instruction is effective immediately and valid until
December 31, 2021.

COMPREHENSIVE PURCHASING TRAINING PROGRAM
TITLE:   Comprehensive Purchasing Training Program
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1.   General
   The Central Purchasing Division of the Department of Finance and
Administrative Services (“Purchasing Division”) provides comprehensive
training, including training materials and pertinent notifications to its end-
users through the Purchasing Liaison User Group (“PLUG”). Training sessions are
conducted at a minimum on a quarterly basis at the PLUG meetings and
notifications are distributed electronically to all PLUG members via e-mail.
Training materials are posted on-line at the Purchasing SharePoint website for
all City employees.
2.   Definitions
   A.   Department Buyer- a City employee hired by a department or division to
assist with the purchasing functions in coordination with and approval by the
Purchasing Division.
   B.   Level 1 Buyers- designated City employees that issue Quick Quotes
through the Sicomm.Net system.
   C.   PLUG- the Purchasing Liaison User Group is a membership comprised of
City employees who have been identified from within their respective
departments and divisions to coordinate purchasing activities with the
Purchasing Division.
   D.   Purchasing Systems- the various software systems employed by the
Purchasing Division to carry out the purchasing functions of the City which
include, but are not limited to, the Enterprise Resource Program (ERP)
PeopleSoft modules; the online bidding program, Sicomm.Net and the Contract
Tracking System (CTS) which generates professional technical and other
agreements.
3.   Application
   A.   The Purchasing Division shall provide formal training materials,
including online courses called UPKs (User Productivity Kit), and other
relevant material at its Purchasing SharePoint website on pertinent purchasing
topics and purchasing procedures. In addition, the Purchasing Division shall
develop and offer purchasing training programs throughout the year at
reasonable intervals.
   B.   The Purchasing Division shall provide training materials or offer
training programs to new City employees regarding the Purchasing process.
   C.   Departments and divisions shall appoint Staff Designee(s) responsible
for generating purchasing requests and coordinating purchasing activities with
the Purchasing Division. Departments and divisions shall provide the Purchasing
Division with the names of these Staff Designee/s so that they may be included
in the PLUG membership by the Purchasing Division and provided notice of PLUG
meetings.
   D.   Staff Designees, Level 1 and Department Buyers are required to attend
all PLUG meetings. Failure to attend more than two (2) consecutive PLUG
meetings will result in a notification to the Department director and may lead
to the suspension of the designated staff member’s access to the Purchasing
Systems.
   E.   Staff Designees, Level 1 and Department Buyers are required to receive
training on the various Purchasing Systems prior to gaining a password and
access to the systems. Sharing of passwords or gaining access to a system
without proper authority is prohibited and may lead to the suspension of access
to the Purchasing Systems and disciplinary action, up to and including
termination from employment.
   F.   Department directors, deputy directors, associate directors, division
managers, supervisors, and fiscal personnel are encouraged to participate in
PLUG and attend PLUG meetings.
Questions regarding this process should be directed to the Chief Procurement
Officer.
REFERENCES:   None.

AI NO: 3-7 (2021)
PAYMENTS TO VENDORS DOING BUSINESS WITH THE CITY
TITLE:   Payments to Vendors Doing Business with the City
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
This Administrative Instruction supersedes the Administrative Instructions or
directives in previously issued versions of Administrative Instruction 3-7,
each of which is hereby rescinded in its entirety. This Administrative
Instruction does not supersede any review or approval authority that may be set
forth in any other Administrative Instruction not specifically identified in
this paragraph.
A.   Background
The City conducts business with a significant number of vendors and it is the
intent of the City to expedite payments to vendors when it is necessary and
practicable. It is also the intent of the City to maximize earnings on vendor
discounts.
On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared that the COVID-19
outbreak should be characterized as a pandemic. Also, on that date, New Mexico
Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham and the New Mexico Department of Health
announced the first confirmed cases of COVID-19 in New Mexico, and the Governor
issued Executive Order 2020-004: Order Declaring a State of Public Health
Emergency and Invoking the Powers Provided by the All Hazard Emergency
Management Act and the Emergency Licensing Act. As a result of the COVID-19
pandemic, supply chains for a wide range of essential items have now been
disrupted, requiring additional flexibility in the City's purchasing process.
To help the City of Albuquerque meet the challenges caused by the supply chain
disruption, Section 7 of Mayor Keller's first Declaration of Public Health
Emergency, issued on March 18, 2020, provides as follows:
Pursuant to §§ 5-5-19(B)(1) and 5-5-35, I find urgent and compelling reasons,
including the unforeseen and dangerous situation of the COVID-19 pandemic,
enabling the City to make emergency procurements to preserve the peace, health,
or safety of people or property within the jurisdiction of the City or to
prevent significant economic loss.
The exigent circumstances caused by the pandemic necessitate a revision to this
Administrative Instruction to address both current and future civil or public
health emergencies.
B.   Policy-Time of Payment
It is the policy of the City to pay all vendors in accordance with the terms of
the pertinent contracts, or within thirty days from the date of an invoice,
whichever is later. In the event of a declared civil or public health emergency
when it is necessary to expeditiously order or procure emergency goods or
services, the payment by the City may precede delivery of the goods or services
from the vendor when warranted by the circumstances. However, in the normal
course of procuring non-prepaid goods or services, and absent delays caused by
problems with the delivered goods or services, a thirty-day payment policy will
be achieved for the majority of payment obligations made by the City of
Albuquerque.
C.   Policy-Taxes on Purchases of Food
The City understands that there exists a gross receipts tax deduction for
receipts derived from the sale of tangible personal property to a government
entity, NMSA 1978, § 7-9-54, and that this deduction applies to the sale of
food in any form to the City. The City further understands that collecting,
applying deductions, payment, and reporting of the gross receipts tax to the
New Mexico Department Taxation and Revenue is the responsibility of the vendor.
It is a common business practice for a vendor to include gross receipts tax on
invoices to the City as a pass-through charge. However, the City, at a vendor's
request, will issue a Non Taxable Transaction Certificate for the vendor's use
in applying and reporting deductions.
The City purchases food from both local and national vendors, who as a matter
of course may include gross receipts tax on invoices to the City as a pass-
through charge. While acknowledging that the purchase of food is a nontaxable
transaction and that the pass-through amount could be deducted by the vendor,
the City must also balance the administrative costs and delay imposed on the
transaction should the City require that employees engaged in the purchase
stop, obtain all required paperwork, and negotiate with the vendor to require
the gross receipts tax be removed. To alleviate the impracticality of taking
such action, it is the policy of the City to waive the requirement that a City
end user seek the removal of the pass-through gross receipts tax charges by a
vendor.
D.   Responsibility
The Purchasing Division of the Department of Finance and Administrative
Services (DFAS), Operating Departments, and the Accounts Payable Section of the
Accounting Division of DFAS each share the responsibility for achieving an
expedient payment process.
These parties are charged with the following responsibilities:
Purchasing Division of DFAS:
   1.   Ensure that all Purchase Orders and City Contract Purchase Orders are
processed on a timely basis.
   2.   Ensure that change orders to Purchase Orders are expeditiously
processed or acted upon to avoid payment delays.
Operating Departments:
   1.   Ensure that all applicable individuals within the departments place a
high priority on processing and entering necessary purchasing information and
vendor information.
   2.   Ensure that department procedures for purchase/receipt/payment approval
are reviewed to eliminate bottlenecks and speed the payment process. The
emphasis should be on the proper and timely approval of the purchase prior to
receipt of goods or services, followed by verified receipt of the goods or
services. Prompt payment should be a natural outflow of these functions and
result in an expedient payment-approval process.
   3.   Ensure that goods or services are not acquired before a Purchase Order
is finalized.
   4.   Appoint department liaisons to be the contact persons for problem
resolution with the Accounts Payable Section and the Purchasing Division.
Furnish Accounting with the name of the appointed department liaisons when
initially appointed and also when turnover occurs.
   5.   Ensure that vendors are provided with proper information at the time of
purchase, i.e., Department/Division name, employee names and contact
information, and Purchase Order numbers, for inclusion on the vendor's invoice.
Accounts Payable Section of DFAS:
   1.   Ensure that all invoices are processed when received. Invoices will be
processed using the Purchase Order number referenced on the invoice. The
financial system will validate against open Purchase Orders and receipts. Where
there are exceptions identified by a match- exception process, the Accounts
Payable staff will work with the departments to resolve the issues. For
invoices submitted through the network hub Transcepta, the Accounts Payable and
Accounting staff will review information to ensure that the data is properly
loaded in voucher tables and ready for processing. Where there are exceptions
identified by a match-exception process, the Accounts Payable staff will work
with departments to resolve the issues.
   2.   Work with department liaisons to research and resolve any issues
regarding vendor invoices on a timely basis.
   3.   Work with departments to identify and review invoices older than 60
days for follow-up.
   4.   Ensure that original invoices are either directly mailed or e-mailed to
the Accounts Payable Section, or submitted through the network hub Transcepta.
Ensure that invoices sent directly to departments are redirected to the
Accounts Payable Section.
   5.   Ensure that appropriate training is provided to departments on the use
of the automated systems and on procedures to be followed.
   6.   Ensure that, in conjunction with the Purchasing Division of DFAS,
appropriate information and procedures are provided to all City vendors
periodically.

VENDING MACHINES AND VENDING STANDS ON CITY PROPERTY
TITLE:   Vending Machines and Vending Stands on City Property
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Municipal Development
General
This Administrative Instruction establishes City policy for the operation of
vending machines and vending stands on City property.
The following vending machines and vending stands are exempt from the
provisions of this Administrative Instruction:
1.   Restaurants or Concessions designated by the CAO to be awarded through a
formal competitive process.
2   Vending machines and vending stands which are operated by restaurants or
concessions in accordance with their contracts with the City.
3.   Vending machines and vending stands which are operated by citizen groups
sponsored by the City, e.g., Senior Centers and Community Centers.
Placement of vending machines or vending stands will not conflict with federal
law or other statutory or legal requirements.
Application
This instruction will apply to all facilities/properties owned by the City of
Albuquerque. This instruction does not apply to rental or lease properties.
Definitions
1.   Concession - The leasing of a portion of a property/facility for a
specific purpose in accordance with the City's Public Purchases and Real
Property ordinances.
2.   Restaurant - Any facility wherein food is prepared, cooked, heated and
served, and a seating area is provided for the consumption of food.
3.   Vending Machine - A money-operated machine designed for vending
prepackaged consumable products for a predetermined price.
4.   Vending Stand - A stand for the purpose of selling prepackaged consumable
products for the benefit of City employees and citizens conducting City
business at a City-owned facility. A vending stand may also include any number
of vending machines.
Procedure
The City Purchasing Officer will promulgate procedures for the application and
contracting of vending machines and vending stands. Such procedures will comply
with State Statutes 22-14-24 to 22-14-29 NMSA 1978 concerning preference for
the operation of vending stands by blind persons who are licensed by the New
Mexico Commission for the Blind.
Revenues
All revenues received by City departments from the operation of vending
machines and vending stands are City revenues. All revenues from these sources
shall be paid by a contractor's check made payable to the City of Albuquerque.
All revenues shall be deposited in accordance with Administrative Instruction
No. 3-4.
Inventory
All Departments shall respond to the Department of Municipal Development survey
of vending machines on or in City property. Departments shall report the name
of the vendor, identify where the machine is located and provide a copy of all
contracts or other agreements regarding revenue. DMD will compile a vending
machine master list.
REFERENCES:   State Statutes 22-14-24 to 22-14-29 NMSA 1978
         Administrative Instruction No. 3-4

PROCEDURES FOR RATIFYING PURCHASE VIOLATIONS (2021)
TITLE:   Procedures for Ratifying Purchase Violations
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1.   General
The Department of Finance and Administrative Services Purchasing Division
("Purchasing Division") has the authority and responsibility to administer the
City's Public Purchases Ordinance, the Purchasing Rules and Regulations, and
the Administrative Instructions in the Purchases Section ( collectively,
"Purchasing Rules").
2.   Definitions
   A.   A Purchase Violation occurs when an employee makes a purchase, either
knowingly or unknowingly, that violates any of the Purchasing Rules.
   B.   A Ratification is the way the Purchasing Division affirms a Purchase
Violation. A ratification has the effect of putting the Purchase Violation in
the same position as if it had been originally authorized. A ratification is
not a disciplinary action. Any disciplinary action shall be at the discretion
of the Department.
   C.   Purchasing Systems means the various software systems employed by the
Purchasing Division to carry out the purchasing functions of the City, which
include but are not limited to the Enterprise Resource Program (ERP) PeopleSoft
modules the online bidding program, and any other software systems that support
the purchasing functions.
3.   Procedure
   A.   When the Purchasing Division is notified of a Purchase Violation, it
shall initiate a Purchase Ratification Form and complete Sections I and II.
Section I is an explanation of why the purchase of goods or services was not in
accordance with the Purchasing Rules. Section II is the Purchasing Division's
recommendation on how to avoid a similar Purchase Violation in the future.
   B.   The Purchase Ratification Form will route to the employee who engaged
in the Purchasing Violation, who shall complete Sections III and IV. Section
III requires that that employee provide a complete explanation of the
circumstances of the Purchase Violation, including all applicable dates and
names of individuals involved with the purchase. Section IV requires the
identification of steps the individual and Department agree to take to ensure
future purchases are made in accordance with the Purchasing Rules.
4.   Approvals Required for Purchase Ratification Forms
Ratifications of Purchasing Violations require the approvals of the employee
involved in the Purchasing Violation, the Department Director, and the Chief
Procurement Officer.
5.   Consequence of Purchasing Violations
   A.   Any City employee who is found to have committed a Purchasing Violation
may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination from
employment.
   B.   Notwithstanding Section 5A, any City employee who is found to have used
any Purchasing System to purchase items for non-City use may be required to
reimburse the City for the unauthorized purchase.
   C.   Pursuant to Section 2-17-12(A) ROA 1994, all City officials, City
employees, and contractors shall promptly notify the Inspector General of every
known or suspected instances of: theft or other disappearance of cash, check,
or property; misuse of funds; improper governmental actions as defined in the
City's Whistleblower Ordinance; or non-compliance with federal law, state law,
or City ordinances or regulations.
   D.   Depending on the facts surrounding a Purchase Violation, the Chief
Procurement Officer may suspend the involved employee's access to any and all
Purchasing Systems. If the Purchase Violation involves the City's Procurement
Card ("P-card"), the P-card holder may be required to immediately surrender the
P-card to the Chief Procurement Officer.
REFERENCES: City Ordinance Article 5 R.O.A. 1994, Public Purchases Ordinance;
Inspector General Ordinance, Sections 2-17-1 et seq. R.O.A. 1994; City of
Albuquerque Purchasing Rules and Regulations; Administrative Instructions
Section 3, Purchasing.

ENCUMBRANCES AS BUDGET MANAGEMENT TOOL – POLICY & PROCEDURES
TITLE:   Encumbrances as Budget Management Tool – Policy & Procedures
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
Background:
An appropriation is the legal authority for a governmental entity to spend
funds for a specific purpose. Appropriations are established by adoption of
program or project level budgets by the City Council. During the course of a
fiscal year, the authority of an appropriation is used in part to acquire
necessary goods and services. An encumbrance represents a commitment to spend
some or all of an appropriation and reduces the amount available for other
encumbrances or expenditures. At any point in time, the sum of all expenditures
plus all encumbrances in place cannot exceed the available appropriation.
Policy:
Every department has an affirmative obligation to ensure that all encumbrances
are appropriate and valid at each month end, with particular attention required
at the end of each fiscal year. Failure to properly monitor the status of each
encumbrance may lead to negative consequences for the City. Failure of a
department to properly and accurately record all valid encumbrances at fiscal
year-end may have a negative impact on that department's operating budget for
the following fiscal year because valid obligations will have to be met out of
the subsequent year’s budget.
General Procedures:
A requisition to obtain goods and or services, approved by the department
director or his designee, must be prepared and submitted to the Purchasing
Division of the Department of Finance and Administrative Services (DFAS). The
requisition must include, at a minimum, the type and quantity of goods or
services to be obtained, the estimated amount to be paid, required general
ledger posting data, and the contract period or date(s) the goods or services
are required.
   1.   At the time that a purchase order is prepared by the Purchasing Office,
an encumbrance is also created. No encumbrance, when added to the current
fiscal year expenditures and encumbrances, can exceed the related
appropriation. If the estimated amount to be paid exceeds the sum of year-to-
date expenditures and existing encumbrances, the encumbrance will be limited to
the amount available for encumbrance.
   2.   Multiple year contracts are acceptable. However, the contract must
state that the commitment is for the current fiscal year appropriation only and
that renewals are contingent on future appropriations. Only amounts
representing commitments against current year appropriations will be
encumbered.
   3.   Purchase orders prepared by the Purchasing Division will include a
statement that contract extensions for subsequent periods beyond the close of
the current fiscal year are contingent on sufficient appropriations being
available. Only amounts representing commitments against current year
appropriations will be encumbered.
   4.   A contract period may span two fiscal years, if the contract period
differs from the City's fiscal year. Only the dollar value of that portion of
the contract to be performed in the current fiscal year will be encumbered. The
dollar value of the balance of the contract will not be encumbered, but will be
disclosed in the CAFR footnotes as a commitment of the following year's revenue
to the extent the data is available.
   5.   Departments are responsible for closing out purchase orders that are no
longer valid due to expired funding, inactivity, or expenditures ending lower
than anticipated.
   6.   In accordance with Section 2-11-12 (B) of the City's Budget Ordinance,
the reserve for encumbrances balance at the end of each fiscal year will be re-
appropriated to the next fiscal year provided there are sufficient reversions
in the respective program and subject to approval of the Office of Management
and Budget. The re-appropriated funds may be used only for the payment of goods
and services that were encumbered in the previous fiscal year. 
   7.   The reserve for encumbrances balance at fiscal year-end represents
amounts for goods or services ordered prior to fiscal year end, but not
received as of the last day of the fiscal year. Goods and services which were
ordered prior to fiscal year end, but were not received prior to fiscal year
end and for which there is an appropriation in the subsequent fiscal year will
be disclosed in the footnotes to the CAFR as a commitment of future revenues.
Exceptions to this Policy and Procedures
Open-ended contracts or agreements represent agreements for pricing only and do
not obligate the City to purchase goods or services. The estimated dollar
amount of purchases to be made under an open-ended contract or agreement will
not be encumbered at the time such a contract or agreement is entered into. The
dollar value of a purchase order release issued under the terms of an open-
ended contract or agreement will be encumbered at the time the purchase order
release is issued.
Questions may be directed to the Accounting Division, the Office of Management
and Budget Division, or the Purchasing Division of the Department of Finance
and Administrative Services.
REFERENCES:   Chapter 11: City Budget 2-11-12 (B); Chapter 5: City Property,
Purchases and Sales.
