PURCHASE OF GOODS OR SERVICES FOR USE BY EMPLOYEES
TITLE:   Purchase of Goods or Services for Use by Employees
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1.   General; Exceptions:
   A.   For the purposes of this Administrative Instruction, goods or services
for use by employees include, but are not limited to:
      I.   Food and beverage items; and related supplies or catering thereof;
      II.   Televisions computers, telephones and other electronics; microwave
ovens, refrigerators, or other appliances;
      III.   On premise gyms or athletic facilities for employees and their
spouses, domestic partners and dependent children;
      IV.   Achievement awards;
      V.   Items of clothing and uniforms; and
      VI.   Badges and side anns.
   B.   The City's Travel Regulations are applicable to goods and services
related to travel for City business and the payment of travel expenses.
   C.   Items purchased from the Mayor's discretionary fund or City Council
discretionary funds are not subject to the provisions of this Administrative
Instruction.
2.   De Minimus Purchases: The City adopts by reference Internal Revenue
Service guidelines, as existing or amended, with respect to the provision of
non-taxable employee benefits and achievement awards. A de minimis benefit is
any good or service provided to an employee that has so little value (taking
into account how frequently similar benefits are provided to employees) that
accounting for it would be unreasonable or administratively impracticable. Cash
or cash equivalents, regardless of the amount, are NEVER a de minimis benefit.
The Chief Administrative Officer ("CAO") or their designee may approve the
purchase of the goods or services under the de minimis benefit provision as
follows:
   A.   Food and Beverage Items:
      I.   Coffee, tea, soft drinks, juices, water, and other non-alcoholic
liquid refreshments or the catering thereof for board, commission and committee
members, and assigned staff, at a regularly scheduled or specially called
board, commission or committee meeting;
      II.   Pastries or other breakfast or snack items, or the catering
thereof, for board, commission, and committee members, and assigned staff, at a
regularly scheduled or specially called board, commission or committee meeting;
      III.   Food and beverages for employees furnished on-site at a City
facility as a convenience for the Department. A written or oral statement that
the meals are furnished for the Department's convenience is not sufficient
support for such a purchase. There must be a substantial business reason; for
example, sandwiches and cold drinks provided during a working lunch as part of
a training session or other group work activity would be evidence of a
substantial business reason;
      IV.   Food and beverages, at a cost of up to one hundred dollars, for
graduation ceremonies or retirement celebrations or open houses open to
employees, their families, and the public; and
      V.   All purchases pursuant to this section A. by employees other than a
Department director must be approved in advance in writing by the Department
director. All purchases pursuant to this section A. by a Department director
shall be approved in advance by the CAO or their designee.
   B.   Achievement Awards for Length-of-Service: A length-of-service
achievement award is limited to tangible personal property, such as a plaque,
watch, trophy, or similar item. The following items are not allowed as length-
of-service achievement awards: cash, cash equivalents, or gift certificates, or
other intangible property such as vacations, meals, lodging, tickets to theater
or sporting events, or stocks, bonds and other securities.
      I.   An achievement award for length-of-service is an item of tangible
personal property that meets the following conditions:
         a.   It is given to an employee for length-of-service;
         b.   It is awarded as part of a meaningful presentation; and
         c.   The award is not structured to result in disguised pay or any of
the unallowable items referenced above.
      II.   A length-of-service award may not be given to:
         a.   Any employee during the first five (5) years of the employee's
employment with the City; or
         b.   Any employee who received another length-of-service achievement
award from the City during the same year or in any of the prior four (4) years.
      III.   The recommended allowable costs for a length-of-service
achievement award are:
         a.   For five to nine (5 - 9) years of service, Fifty and  No/1 00
Dollars  ($50.00);
         b.   For ten to fourteen (10 - 14) years of service, Seventy-Five and
No/100 Dollars ($75.00);
         c.   For fifteen to nineteen (15 - 19) years of service, One Hundred
and No/1 00  Dollars ($100.00);
         d.   For twenty or more (20+) years of service, One-Hundred Fifty and
No/1 00  Dollars ($150.00).
      IV.   A Department director may approve a higher dollar amount for a
length-of-service award in advance and in writing, but in no case may a length-
of-service award exceed Two-Hundred and No/1 00  Dollars ($200.00).
      V.   All purchases pursuant to this section B. by employees other than a
Department director must be approved in advance in writing by the Department
director. All length-of-service awards for Department directors must be
approved in advance and in writing by the CFO or Director of Finance and
Administrative Services.
   C.   Annual Picnic or Party: With advance written approval from the CAO or
their designee, each Department may conduct an annual picnic or party for
Department employees and their guests. There may be no more than one (1) such
event in each fiscal year.
   D.   Other Allowable Purchases: City funds may be used to purchase goods or
services for use by employees if:
      I.   The Department director determines in advance and in writing that a
good or service is necessary for the health, safety or welfare of employees,
due to working conditions or the physical location of the workstation; or
      II.   The good or service is used in conjunction with a City-sponsored
training program that has been approved by a Department director in writing; or
      III.   The good or service is required to perform assigned Departmental
responsibilities or functions.
      IV.   All purchases pursuant to this section D. by employees other than a
Department director must be approved in advance in writing by the Department
director. All purchases under this section by Department directors shall be
approved in advance by the CAO, CFO, or Chief Operating Officer, as applicable.
   E.   Unallowable Purchases:
      I.   Except as provided in Section 2 herein, City funds may not be used
to pay for retirement lunches, dinners, parties, or receptions, or for
graduation or award ceremonies.
      II.   City funds may not be used to purchase goods or services for or on
behalf of a contractor.
      III.   City funds may not be used to purchase an item merely for the
convenience of one or more employees. For clarification, this section does not
apply to reasonable accommodation for the purposes of the Americans with
Disabilities Act.
      IV.   Under no circumstances should an employee use a City-based goods or
services contract for the employee's own personal use even if no City funds are
utilized in the purchase.
   F.   Items of Clothing and Uniforms.  When required by the Department, items
of clothing and uniforms with City or Department patches, printing, embroidery,
labels, or logos, with or without an employee's name, are not considered to be
goods for use by employees.
   G.   Badges and Sidearms: The City purchases badges and sidearms for certain
classes of employees. At retirement, the retiring employee may purchase from
the City that badge or sidearm assigned to them at the time of their
retirement. The Accounting Officer shall determine the fair market value of the
badge or sidearm, which shall be paid into the City treasury prior to the
employee's retirement.
REFERENCES: Public Purchases Ordinance Sections 5-5-1 et seq. ROA 1994;
applicable Internal Revenue Code; City of Albuquerque Travel Regulations.

NUTRITION STANDARDS FOR VENDING MACHINE BEVERAGES AND SNACK
TITLE: Nutrition Standards for Vending Machine Beverages and Snack
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Background:
The City of Albuquerque desires to provide a healthier food and beverage
vending program for vending machines located on all City property; and to
further promote the City’s commitment to improving the health of its employees
and visitors of all City of Albuquerque properties.
This instruction pertains to vending machines on City property, owned or
leased, and real property upon which City operations are conducted or is
occupied by City employees in their normal duties. City property includes but
is not limited to all buildings of any type, parking structures, parking lots,
and all other structures including the grounds of unenclosed space located on
City Property.
Policy:
In alignment with the U. S. Department of General Services Administration
document “Health and Sustainability Guidelines for Concessions and Vending
Operations”:
Calorie Labeling of Articles of Food in Vending Machines: The vending machine
operator shall provide a sign in close proximity of each article of food or the
selection button that includes a clear and conspicuous statement disclosing the
number of calories contained in the article when the Nutrition Facts Panel or
Calorie Content is not visible.
Trans fat: Only offer items that contain 0 grams trans fat per serving as
defined by the Unites States Food and Drug Administration.
Sodium:
   ∙  Only offer snack items that contain no more than 230 milligrams sodium
per serving (excludes refrigerated meals).
   ∙  Individual meal items must contain no more than 480 milligrams sodium per
serving.
In addition to meeting the menu labeling, trans fat, and sodium requirements
listed above, at least 25% of all packaged food choices must meet the following
criteria:
   ∙  Limit all snack (not refrigerated meals) items to no more than 200
calories per item (excluding nuts and seeds without added fats, oils, or
caloric sweeteners).
   ∙  Limit total calories from saturated fat to no more than 10% (excluding
nuts and seeds without added fats or oils).
   ∙  Limit calories from sugars to no more than 35% of total weight (excluding
fruits or vegetables without added caloric sweeteners).
Beverage requirements:
   ∙  At least 50% of available beverage choices (other than 100% juice and
unsweetened milk) must contain no more than 40 calories per serving.
   ∙  If milk is offered, only offer 2%, 1% and non-fat milk dairy-type
products.
   ∙  If juice is offered, offer at least one 100% juice with no added caloric
sweeteners.
   ∙  Vegetable juice must contain no more than 230 milligrams sodium per
serving.
REFERENCES:   Council Resolution R-16-52 (Enacted)

AI NO: 3-16
CREDIT CARD SECURITY
TITLE:   Credit Card Security
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Technology and Innovation
1.   Background
The number and type of credit cards accepted at City facilities continue to
increase. As more transactions are made with credit cards, including over the
internet, the City will remain vigilant and continue to earn the trust of the
public by ensuring credit card information is used in a secure and responsible
manner.
2.   Policy
The City will comply with the current version of the Payment Card Industry Data
Security Standards (PCI-DSS). In particular, the City will ensure:
   • All payment systems are PCI-DSS compliant
   • All payment systems are implemented in compliance with PCI-DSS
requirements.
   • All payment systems are maintained and operated in compliance with PCI-DSS
requirements.
In particular:
   • Unencrypted credit card numbers are not sent through end-user messaging
technologies such as, but not limited to, email, instant messaging (IM) or
chat.
   • Credit card numbers are not stored in paper form.
   • Card transactions processed by City personnel via telephone are entered
directly into the card processing system as the card information is relayed
from the constituent/customer. The card information is not written on paper or
keyed and is not stored on any application or database.
   • All employees involved in handling credit card information are trained to
securely handle credit card information.
   • In the event of a data breach, incident management will follow the
incident management guidelines laid out by the card company (companies)
impacted.

SENIOR LEVEL PURCHASING POSITIONS
TITLE: Senior Level Purchasing Positions
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
Except as otherwise provided by the Public Purchases Ordinance, the Central
Purchasing Office (also known as the Purchasing Division of the Department of
Finance and Administrative Services) is the central purchasing office for the
City. The Central Purchasing Office is staffed with several levels of
purchasing personnel to carry out this function. Although a Department may
decide it needs a dedicated buyer and is willing to fund its own senior level
purchasing personnel, all such employees shall be directly supervised by,
located in, and held accountable to the Purchasing Division and the Chief
Procurement Officer.
REFERENCES:   Public Purchases Ordinance Sections 5-5-1 et seq. ROA 1994,
applicable Internal Revenue Code.

GENDER PAY EQUITY REPORTING AND PREFERENCE POLICY (2020)
TITLE: Gender Pay Equity Reporting and Preference Policy
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Finance and Administrative Services
BACKGROUND
The City of Albuquerque encourages potential vendors and contractors to
prioritize gender pay equity by offering a preference to qualifying respondents
to requests for proposals. This administrative instruction is to provide
interpretation of Albuquerque City Ordinance ROA 1994, §§ 5-5-31 regarding the
City’s Gender Pay Equity policy. Organizations seeking contracts with the City
of Albuquerque through the submission of a bid or proposal will be required to
comply with the requirements of City Ordinance § 5-5-31, the New Mexico Fair
Pay for Women Act, NMSA Sec.28-23-1, et seq., and the federal Equal Pay Act, 29
USCA 206(d) and other federal gender pay equity laws. This preference shall not
be applied to bids or proposals submitted in response to solicitations for
federally funded projects. Federal procurement regulations prohibit the use of
statutorily or administratively imposed state or local geographical preferences
in the evaluation of bids or proposals.
POLICY
1)   Definitions:
   a)   Gender Pay Equity Initiative: Collaborative partnership between the
City of Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, and the Albuquerque Bernalillo County
Water Utility Authority.
   b)   Pay Equity Employee Data Form: The document in which a vendor enters
information.
   c)   Pay Equity Reporting Form: The document that is generated based on the
information submitted on the Pay Equity Data Form.
   d)   Pay Equity Certificate: The document certifying compliance with the Pay
Equity initiative as specified in section C.
   e)   Full Time: Employees working an average of at least 30 hours per week.
   f)   Part Time: Employees working an average of less than 30 hours per week.
   g)   Total Annual Compensation: The total monetary earnings for one full
year.
   h)   Job Category Titles: Job category classifications determined by the
U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, which categorizes jobs by title
in its EE0-1 Job Classification Guide (2010), which may be amended or updated
from time to time.
   i)   Technical Change: A technical change, as defined by the Gender Pay
Equity Initiative, consists of a missing component, flawed calculation, failure
to sign or date, or an incorrectly uploaded document. If one of these should
happen, the employer will be given 24 hours after the response deadline to
resubmit with the necessary correction to be considered responsive.
2)   Pay Equity Reporting Form
   a)   Structure
      i)   The Pay Equity Reporting Form is the document automatically
generated based on the data entered on the Pay Equity Employee Data Form. The
Pay Equity Employee Data Form can be accessed through the Gender Pay Equity
Initiative website: https://www.cabq.gov/gender-pay-equity-initiative.
      ii)   Individual pay data shall not be included in the Pay Equity
Reporting Form that is generated after completing the Pay Equity Employee Data
Form – only the organization’s summary pay equity information shall be included
on the Pay Equity Reporting Form that is submitted.
      iii)   Each Pay Equity Reporting Form is valid for one year from the date
it was signed.
      iv)   Sole proprietors are not required to enter pay information into the
Pay Equity Employee Data Form, but they must fill out the company information
section of the Pay Equity Employee Data Form and submit a signed Pay Equity
Reporting Form indicating they are a sole proprietorship.
      v)   Businesses that do not employ New Mexico residents are not required
to enter pay information into the Pay Equity Employee Data Form, but they must
fill out the company information section of the Pay Equity Employee Data Form
and submit a signed Pay Equity Reporting Form indicating they employ no New
Mexico residents.
   b)   Submission
      i)   A signed Pay Equity Reporting Form (or a valid Pay Equity
Certificate – see section 3) shall be submitted with all responses to requests
for bids and requests for proposals.
   c)   Processing
      i)   Pay Equity Reporting Forms and Pay Equity Certificates submitted in
bid or proposal packets shall be reviewed for technical compliance.
      ii)   If a technical change is necessary, Purchasing or CIP staff will
alert the bidder/proposer that they have 24 hours after receiving notification
to correct
the error.
      iii)   If an error on the Pay Equity Reporting Form or Pay Equity
Certificate is not corrected within 24 hours, that bid or proposal shall be
deemed nonresponsive.
3)   Pay Equity Certificate
   a)   Eligibility
      i)   To be eligible to receive a 5% pay equity preference on the bid
price or total proposal score, an organization must obtain a Pay Equity
Certificate and submit it with the bid or proposal. To obtain a Pay Equity
Certificate, the organization must meet two criteria:
         (1)   overall percent deviation between male and female pay must be
0.00%; and
         (2)   the position-specific deviations between any two gender
categories must be 0.00%.
      ii)   Each Pay Equity Certificate is valid for one year from the date of
issuance.
      iii)   Organizations that employ only one gender are not eligible for
certification.
      iv)   Organizations that only employ men and women in separate job
categories are not eligible for certification.
      v)   Organizations that employ no New Mexico residents are not eligible
for certification, although they must still comply with Section 2(a)(5) above.
      vi)   The pay equity preference shall not apply to bids or proposals
submitted in response to solicitations for federally funded projects. Federal
procurement regulations prohibit the use of statutorily or administratively
imposed state or local geographical preferences in the evaluation of bids or
proposals.
      vii)   Existing Certificates at the time this Administrative Instruction
becomes effective shall continue to be honored until the date of their
expiration. Certifications must be valid at the time of the solicitation close
date.
   b)   Submission
      i)   To be certified, an organization must submit a signed Pay Equity
Reporting Form, which will automatically be reviewed by the Gender Pay Equity
Initiative if the organization meets the eligibility criteria.
      ii)   Pay Equity Certificates issued by the Gender Pay Equity Initiative
are accepted by the City of Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, and the Albuquerque
Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority. To provide consistency, the City of
Albuquerque shall serve as the certifying agency for all three organizations.
      iii)   To be eligible for the pay equity preference, a valid Pay Equity
Certificate must be submitted with all responses to requests for bids and
requests for proposals.
   c)   Processing
      i)   The certifying agency will review all certification requests and
either issue a Pay Equity Certificate or communicate denial of the request
within two business days of receiving the Pay Equity Reporting Form.
4)   Verification of Submitted Data
   a)   The City reserves the right to request any organization provide a
third-party certification of data submitted to ensure compliance of
organizations seeking certification, claiming sole proprietorship, or claiming
to employ no New Mexico residents.
   b)   Gender identity categories are determined by the jurisdiction in which
the employee resides and are subject to verification by birth certificate or
other vital record.
   c)   Organizations found to have submitted inaccurate information in the Pay
Equity Reporting Form will have their bids/proposals deemed nonresponsive and
may be prohibited from bidding or proposing on future business with the City
according to Albuquerque City Ordinance ROA 1994, § 5-5-24.
5)   Reporting
   a)   The Gender Pay Equity Initiative will make organizational pay equity
data, but not individual pay data, available through a public-facing dashboard.
References: City Ordinance § 5-5-31; Women’s Pay Equity Task Force; New Mexico
Fair Pay for Women Act, NMSA 1978, §§ 28-23-1 to -6 (2013); Equal Pay Act, 29
USCA 206(d)

PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE AND SCHEDULING OF VEHICLE REPAIRS
TITLE: Preventative Maintenance and Scheduling of Vehicle Repairs
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:  Department of Finance and Administrative Services
Purpose:
City of Albuquerque owned vehicles and equipment require periodic maintenance
to ensure a safe, reliable, cost effective operation over its service life.
Each vehicle maintained by the Fleet Division has been assigned to a detailed
multi-tiered preventative maintenance (PM) program based on vehicle class and
application. Adherence to the PM program is mandatory. Failing to follow
preventative maintenance services according to the manufacturer guidelines
could void any claim to a warranty. All documentation of vehicle or equipment
repair or services will be kept through the life of the vehicle and recorded in
the City of Albuquerque’s fleet management system, Fleet Focus.
Policy:
It is the responsibility of the Fleet Division to maintain City owned vehicles
and equipment, and to ensure that they conform to specified conditions,
functions and safety standards. This instruction provides procedures that are
applicable for the repair and servicing of City owned vehicles and equipment.
The Fleet Division will send monthly PM and emission schedules to department
liaisons. It is the responsibility of the department liaisons and department
managers to ensure compliance with the schedules.
A follow up report will also be sent to department liaisons listing the
vehicles previously scheduled for PM and /or emissions testing that have not
complied with the schedule. Vehicles that fail to achieve compliance within 500
miles and/or 30 days of the schedule will have fuel privileges deactivated.
Procedures:
A.   The vehicle operator shall report with the vehicle or equipment to the
Fleet Division Service Writer office located at Pino Yards.
B.   The vehicle operator may submit a work request for repairs or maintenance
from any City issued computer prior to his/her arrival at the maintenance
facility. Otherwise a Fleet Division Service Writer will initiate a repair or
service order and either direct the vehicle operator to park the vehicle in the
appropriate repair line or direct the operator to the appropriate maintenance
area.
C.   All vehicle operators shall wait in designated waiting areas. At no time
will vehicle operators be allowed to wait in inspection bays, shops, or other
work areas. All equipment brought in for repairs or services will be moved at
the direction of Fleet Division personnel.
D.   Vehicles left for repairs or services will be locked and all valuable
items removed by the vehicle operator. The Fleet Division is not responsible
for items left in vehicles that are lost or stolen.
E.   Vehicle operators are responsible for contacting or delivering vehicles
and/or equipment with safety related issues. No appointment is necessary. If
the vehicle cannot safely be driven, contact Fleet Division Service Writer’s
for assistance.
F.   All City vehicles and equipment in need of service and under the
maintenance responsibility of the Fleet Division will be reported to the Fleet
Division’s maintenance facility, whether in-house or outside service is
required.
G.   Only the Fleet Division is authorized to initiate purchases for parts or
commercial repair for vehicles and equipment under its responsibility.
This Administrative Instruction excludes Aviation, Fire Department Heavy
Apparatus, Police Special Investigations Division, Transit vehicles, and Solid
Waste Management.
REFERENCES:   None.

VEHICLE IDENTIFICATION
TITLE: Vehicle Identification
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
This Administrative Instruction establishes the vehicle identification policy
for all City owned Vehicles. The Chief Administrative Officer must approve any
exceptions to this policy in writing.
1.    City owned vehicles shall display the City of Albuquerque logo as well as
the assigned vehicle number. All vehicles shall display the city logo on both
driver and passenger doors.
2.    All vehicles shall have the vehicle number displayed on the left and
right front fenders, and on the trunk lid or tailgate.
3.    Installation of all identification markings (including logos and
department/division names) shall be administered by the Fleet Division. As an
option, a department's name may be installed below the logo on each door.
4.    This Instruction excludes Aviation, Police, Fire, Transit, and Solid
Waste Management vehicles. Off-road landfill equipment is also excluded.
5.    Unless extenuating circumstances exist, there shall be no exceptions to
this policy. In the event there is such a circumstance, a formal request
identifying the reason for deviation from this policy, shall be submitted in
writing to the Chief Administrative Officer for approval. No vehicle
identification work shall begin until the request is approved.

VEHICLE ACQUISITION POLICY AND PROCEDURES (2024)
TITLE: Vehicle Acquisition Policy and Procedures
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:  General Services
Purpose:
To create an environmentally and fiscally responsible City of Albuquerque fleet
by ensuring that it is properly sized and fuel efficient, while still meeting
all intended uses. The Departments exempt from this policy are Solid Waste,
Transit, Fire, and Aviation. Not exempt are Fire non-emergency response
equipped vehicles and Solid Waste, Transit and Aviation light-duty vehicles.
Definitions:
a)   Zero emissions vehicle
   "Zero emissions vehicle" or "ZEV" is defined as a vehicle that does not
produce tailpipe emissions.
b)   Cost-competitive
   "Cost-competitive" is defined as a vehicle's total cost of ownership within
ten percent of the cost of a gasoline or hybrid vehicle, which includes the
costs of vehicle purchase, fuel, maintenance, and insurance, etc. Please see
Exhibit A: Attached cost of ownership Analysis
c)   Replacement Criteria
   "Replacement Criteria" is defined as the conditions that must be met to
replace an existing vehicle. Fleet vehicles must meet at least two of the
following three criteria to be considered for replacement:
      1)   More than 110,000 miles driven
      2)   More than 15 years old
      3)   The total repair over the life of the vehicle is more than 75% of
initial purchase price.
d)   Charging stations:
      a.   TYPES:
         i.   Level I Charging System- is a ZEV and EHV charging systems that
are low power electrical supply chargers that are the slowest to reach a full
charge. Level I chargers are typically supported by existing infrastructure.
         ii.   Level II charging - Is an ZEV and EHV charging system that can
require infrastructure improvements. Level II charging systems typically take
longer than level III to restore a full charge to ZEVs and EHV's.
         iii.   Level III -Is an ZEV and EHV charging system that requires more
electrical energy and typically requires infrastructure improvements/upgrades.
Level III Charging systems typically reach full charge in faster than level I
and level II.
e)   City Vehicles: Pool/ Assigned
   a.   City Vehicle - an automobile/passenger vehicle that is owned by the
City that is used as a conveyance to travel throughout the city while
conducting city business or directly providing services to the public.
      i.   City Vehicle Pool - a collection of vehicles managed by departments
to offer to department staff that is not specifically assigned to any one
person. Pool vehicles are issued or assigned to a variety of fleet users for
short time use.
         1.   Departments can have a pool of fleet vehicles that are specific
to the department however, General Services Department does have a pool of
fleet vehicles that other departments have access to.
      ii.   Assigned vehicles- Fleet vehicles that are assigned specifically to
one driver /user.
f)   Prepositioned City Vehicles-Vehicles that are positioned strategically at
publicly owned properties for City Staff that have approval for parking city
vehicles in strategic locations to provide efficiencies to the city.
Policy:
1)   It is the policy of the City of Albuquerque (COA) that all eligible new
vehicles and vehicles that meet the replacement criteria-purchased for the City
of Albuquerque's fleet will be:
   a)   Fuel-efficient with the lowest emissions within the vehicle class/type;
following a hierarchy from highest to lowest priority: (1) zero emissions
vehicles (ZEVs), (2) plug-in hybrid vehicles, (3) hybrid-electric vehicles
(HEVs),, and (4) internal combustion vehicles utilizing fossil fuels.
   b)   Commercially available, practical, and cost-competitive for the class/
type of vehicles needed for specific assignments.
   c)   Evaluated to determine if it is necessary to operate that class/type of
vehicle and if a suitable lower emissions vehicle would be sufficient.
2)   New vehicle requests for Sport Utility Vehicles (SUVs) or large trucks
that would increase the number of units to the COA fleet, will not be approved
unless justified based on a verified work assignment. Such work assignments
include: rough terrain/off-road travel, passenger/cargo requirements, and/or
trailer towing requirements on a routine basis. Requests shall be reviewed by
the Fleet Review Committee (FRC) and General Services Department (GSD) Director
and forwarded with a recommendation to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO)
for approval.
3)   The General Services Department (GSD) Fleet Division will work with City
departments to coordinate and support the replacement of fleet vehicles with
lower emissions and greater fuel-efficiency. Solid Waste, Transit, Fire, and
Aviation will coordinate their respective Department's replacement of vehicles
that are subject to this policy.
4)   When the GSD fleet division replaces eligible light-duty vehicles, the
standard budgeting approach involves replacing them with similar vehicles.
However, the division prioritizes the replacement of vehicles with ZEVs of the
appropriate vehicle class/type, in accordance with the policy stated in Item 1.
This approach underscores the division's commitment to sustainable and
environmentally friendly transportation solutions.
   a)   The General Services Department will also evaluate the assigned
location of the proposed replacement vehicle to determine the feasibility of
charging stations for ZEV's and EHV's at the site. The Facilities Management
Division, Energy and Sustainability Division, in some cases DMD, will work
collectively to make improvements for accommodations for charging the ZEV and
EHV Fleet.
5)   Exceptions to this policy may be approved on a case-by-case basis by the
FRC, GSD Director, and CAO based upon the intended use, application, vehicle
specifications, and/or overriding cost considerations. Fuel economy and vehicle
emissions are prioritized when requesting other vehicle types.
Fleet Review Committee (FRC) - Applicable to the GSD Administered Fleet
Purpose:
1)   Define vehicle utilization and allocation policies and procedures to
enhance the control, operation, cost effectiveness, and positive environmental
impact of the City of Albuquerque's Fleet.
2)   Provide guidance to City departments and divisions regarding vehicle
upgrades, additions, and replacements.
3)   Improve communication with vehicle users throughout the City of
Albuquerque.
4)   Serve as the final recommendation authority to the GSD Department Director
on vehicle upgrades, additions, and replacements.
Members:
1)   The FRC shall consist of a representative from each Department for which
the Fleet Management Division manages vehicle acquisition, appointed by the
Director thereof. All members will be considered to have equal rights and
responsibilities. All votes will be determined by majority rule, the requesting
department does not have a vote
2)   Members must make every effort to attend and actively participate in FRC
meetings. Members must also be knowledgeable about all activities occurring in
their respective departments that may impact the utilization and allocation of
vehicles. Each member shall have an alternate who will attend in his or her
absence.
3)   A member of the Fleet Management Division, appointed by the Fleet Manager,
will serve in a non-voting capacity to ensure compliance with policies and
requirements.
Responsibilities:
1)   Review, revise, and initiate, if required, City of Albuquerque policies
and procedures governing the control and operation of City-owned vehicles.
2)   Make recommendations regarding requests for vehicle upgrades,
replacements, or additions.
3)   Annually review Citywide standardized specifications for each class of
vehicle.
4)   Development and maintenance of City Fleet replacement and utilization
criteria.
5)   Development and maintenance of the Alternative Fuel Policy.
Fleet Management Division's Role - Applicable to the GSD Administered Fleet
Purpose:
1)   Provide policy guidance and support both the end user departments and the
FRC with fleet data and analysis.
2)   Serve as the facilitator of the FRC meetings.
3)   Administer the purchase, salvage of all approved equipment and vehicle
requests, and to assign under-utilized vehicles.
Responsibilities:
1)   Perform an annual fleet analysis, and make recommendations for vehicle
replacements to the FRC using the utilization and replacement criteria set
forth by the FRC.
2)   Fleet Management will work with the Purchasing Division to establish
contracts for the standard specifications that the FRC has set forth for each
class of vehicle.
3)   Assist the end-user departments with preparing requests to the FRC for
vehicle and equipment upgrades or additions.
4)   Order, track, receive, and prepare all approved vehicle purchases for the
end-user departments.
5)   Receive and prepare for salvage units submitted for replacement.
Procedure for Vehicle Additions, Upgrades, Replacements and ZEV Exemption:
1)   Vehicle Additions/Upgrades
   a)   Any department or division interested in upgrading or adding a vehicle
must contact and work with the Fleet Division to prepare a proposal to submit
to the FRC.
   b)   A representative from the requesting department or division will
provide a memo of justification to the FRC to include details on the need for
the requested upgrade or addition.
   c)   The Fleet Division staff will provide supporting documentation
including, but not limited to, the total number and usage of vehicles for the
department or division.
   d)   The FRC will make a recommendation on the need for the requested
upgrade or the addition based on the following criteria:
      i)   Whether the vehicle is required to continue providing excellent
customer service;
      ii)   Whether the vehicle required is due to an increase in staffing or
the addition of new programs;
      iii)   Whether the need can be met without a vehicle upgrade or addition;
      iv)   Whether the upgrade/addition/retention is in the best interest of
the City of Albuquerque;
      v)   Whether current department/division vehicles are used enough to
warrant this addition; and
      vi)   Whether this vehicle will help improve the sustainability of the
City fleet in a fiscally responsible manner.
   e)   The FRC will review the request based on the criteria above and provide
a recommendation to the GSD Director.
   f)   Department directors can appeal the GSD Director's decision to the CAO.
2)   Vehicle Replacements
   a)   The Fleet Management Division will annually perform an overall analysis
of the City fleet, make recommendations for vehicle replacements, and submit
such recommendation to the GSD Director for review.
   b)   The Fleet Management Division will critically assess vehicles due for
replacement to determine if the current vehicle is necessary to accomplish City
goals.
   c)   The Fleet Management Division will meet annually with department
directors or designee to discuss vehicles approved for replacement within their
respective departments.
   d)   Fleet Management and the FRC will determine if a fleet vehicle (whether
pool or assigned) will be replaced with either a ZEV or EHV if the following
criteria is met;
      i)   The pool vehicle is eligible based on existing criteria for fleet
disposal/surplus; and,
      ii)   The existing electrical charging infrastructure is in place where
the fleet pool vehicle will be parked either at the daily worksite or the
approved prepositioned location.
3)   ZEV Exemptions
   a)   The FRC may recommend an exemption from ZEVreplacement based on vehicle
criteria including, but not limited to: public safety vehicle capabilities,
emergency response functions, operating requirements, challenges due to
infrastructure access for charging or refueling, or no cost-competitive or
otherwise suitable ZEV replacement available.
   b)   When the FRC recommends an exemption to a ZEV procurement and the class
of vehicle has a ZEV option, the Fleet Management Division will select an
alternative vehicle pursuant to the following hierarchy: 1) plug-in hybrid
vehicles, 2) hybridelectric vehicles, 3) alternative fuel or other vehicle with
demonstrated lower emissions than the vehicle eligible for replacement.
Funding of Replacement Vehicles:
The Fleet Management Division on behalf of the FRC will request funding during
the annual budget process for all of the City vehicles that have been
identified as eligible for replacement.
Exemptions:
Written requests for exemption from this Administrative Instruction shall be
reviewed by the FRC and the GSD Director and forwarded with a recommendation to
the CAO for approval.

VEHICLE MAINTENANCE AND REPAIR RATES
TITLE: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Rates
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance & Administrative Services
Purpose:
To provide for the maintenance of all City owned vehicles and equipment
including both preventive and emergency maintenance to assure such equipment
can be utilized in the most productive and cost efficient manner.
The Fleet Management Division of the Department of Finance and Administrative
Services operates as an internal service fund. Revenue to support operations is
derived by directly billing user departments for services provided. All revenue
is offset by costs within each department as a result of charges for direct
labor, parts, fuel, commercial labor and parts.
The direct bill fees exclude maintenance service not considered normal wear or
required due to driver abuse, accident damage, vandalism, cosmetic (repaint and
detail), vehicle modifications, capitalization, vehicle repairs that are in
excess of the current book value, and glass replacement. These exclusions will
be charged based on actual maintenance costs to an accounting string provided
by the Department.
REFERENCES:

CITY VEHICLE USAGE POLICY
TITLE:   City Vehicle Usage Policy
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
I.   Background:
The City spends a significant amount of resources on acquiring and maintaining
a fleet of vehicles and equipment to enable employees to perform their duties.
The City and its employees have a fiduciary responsibility to use these
resources wisely, effectively, safely and in conformance with federal, state,
and City laws, statutes, ordinances, rules and regulations. This AI provides
general guidelines, policies and procedures, but cannot be read in isolation
from other relevant documents including, but not limited to, the City
Operator’s Permit (COP) program policies and procedures, other related
Administrative Instructions, and local, state and federal law.
The City reserves the right to deny any employee the use of a City vehicle. Any
City employee who fails to adhere to the policies and procedures contained in
this document may be subject to appropriate disciplinary action.
II.   Definitions:
   1.   “Assigned Take Home Vehicle” means a City vehicle which is used by a
City employee for City business and for regularly commuting to and from the
employee’s home and work station.
   2.   “Assigned Vehicle” means a City vehicle assigned to a department or
City employee for City business, but not for employee commuting to and from the
employee’s home and work station.
   3.   “Call–Out” means a directive to an employee to report to a work site
during off duty time or day, and to respond to emergencies, which require
immediate response to protect life and property.
   4.   "Designated Parking Area" means a City parking facility or lot which
has been identified by an employee's department director as an acceptable
overnight location for parking the employee's assigned City vehicle.
   5.   “Emergency Response" means an employee has primary responsibility for
immediate response, to protect life and property, and to maintain and enforce
law and order or an employee has primary City-wide custodial control of
resources used during emergency response.
   6.   "Motor Pool Dispatch Vehicle" means a vehicle issued from a central
motor pool for a single trip or motor pool policy.
   7.   Pre-positioned Vehicle means a vehicle assigned to a department and
parked in a designated parking area.
   8.   "Temporary On-Call Status" means an employee is directed by his or her
supervisor to be available to respond to emergency situations for a specified
and limited period of time.
   9.   "Work Station" means the office or site a City employee reports to
perform normally scheduled work.
III.   Policy:
For the purpose of this AI, “City vehicle” means all vehicles, regardless of
whether they are required to be registered under State law, made available by
the City, whether through purchase, lease, rental, or other means, to employees
to enable them to perform their duties and personal vehicles being operated for
city business.
   1.   City vehicles will be used exclusively to conduct official City
business.
   2.   Employees operating a City Vehicle are required to have a valid
driver’s license and City identification and be in compliance with the COP
program policies and procedures. If an employee is operating a City vehicle
that requires a Commercial Driver’s License (CDL), the employee must carry a
valid CDL and a valid medical card.
   3.   City vehicles are not to be used to conduct personal business
including, but not limited to, leaving City property solely for meals or
breaks, running personal errands to cleaners, banks, etc., going to medical
appointments unless based on a workers compensation claim, or visiting friends
or relatives. Personal errands in a City vehicle are only allowed if the
location of the errand is on the way to the employee’s Work Station and not
done during work hours.
   4.   City vehicles shall not be used to transport non-City employees except
for persons who have a working or other business relationship with the City, or
with advance CAO approval for special events such as parades. It is allowable
for employees to transport family members (e.g. children to school) if the
location of the school is on the way to the employee’s Work Station and not
done during work hours.
   5.   City vehicles shall not be used for commuting between the employee’s
residence and the place where the employee reports to work on a regular basis
and back, unless the employee has been an Assigned Take Home Vehicle.
   6.   City employees who are authorized the exclusive use of an Assigned Take
Home Vehicle will be subject to all pertinent Internal Revenue Services (IRS)
rules and regulations regarding taxation of that use. See the attached IRS
Fringe Benefit Form.
   7.   In the course of performing their normal duties while operating a City
vehicle, an employee may stop for regularly scheduled lunch or break periods at
establishments that sell food if that stop is otherwise incidental to their use
of the vehicle.
   8.   City vehicles, in general are not provided for the exclusive use of a
particular City employee.
   9.   Assignment of a City vehicle shall not be made based on employee merit
or employee status.
   10.   City employees operating City vehicles are required to obey all
traffic laws.
   11.   Any employee receiving a criminal or civil citation for violation of
state or City motor vehicle statutes or ordinances shall be personally
responsible for timely paying any assessed fine or penalty.
An employee is required to notify their supervisor of any criminal or civil
citation issued to them while operating a City vehicle. Failure to do so may
result in disciplinary action and is subject to review as an incident of
potential driver misconduct under the COP program. Fines or penalties charged
to a City vehicle and paid by the City shall be promptly reimbursed by the
employee operating the vehicle. City employees may be personally liable for
damages incurred during the operation of a City vehicle during official or
unofficial use, as well as during any misuse or abuse of a City vehicle. All
damages to and all accidents involving a City vehicle, no matter how minor,
must be reported in accordance with the Risk Management Procedures Manual.
   10.   Usage of mobile telephone by anyone operating any City vehicle shall
be incompliance with the City’s Traffic Regulations, specifically §8-2-1-24(E)
ROA 1994, as amended (“Ordinance”): “Except as otherwise provided below, no
person shall operate a motor vehicle upon a public highway while using a mobile
telephone to engage in a call or create, send or read text messages” while such
vehicle is in motion,” except in the hands-free mode.” As defined in the
Ordinance, drivers operating in an emergency situation and public safety
personnel use in the course of their employment are exempt. With Chief
Administrative Officer approval, Departments may enact more restrictive
policies regarding the use of cellular phones or other telecommunication devise
during operation of a City vehicle.
   12.   Wherever possible, assigned City vehicles shall be picked up and
dropped off at an approved Designated Parking Area, thereby avoiding the need
of an Assigned Take Home Vehicle.
   13.   Assigned Take Home Vehicle assignments must first be reviewed by the
Fleet Division and approved by the Chief Administrative Officer.
   14.   Emergency Response City vehicles may be taken home by designated City
employees who:
      a.   Are on Call-Out at least twelve (12) times per quarter, or
      b.   Forty-eight (48) times a year and have primary responsibility to
respond to emergencies which require immediate response to protect life or
property.
      c.   Cannot use alternative forms of transportation to respond to
emergencies; and
      d.   Cannot pick up City-owned Assigned Vehicles at designated sites
without impacting the employee's ability to respond to emergencies, which
require immediate response to protect life or property.
Emergency Response assignments should be supported by data demonstrating the
actual number and nature of Emergency Responses in the prior year, and
estimates of future Emergency Responses. There must be written justification as
to why an employee cannot use alternative forms of transportation to respond to
the emergencies or pick up City-owned Assigned Vehicles at Designated Parking
Areas.
IV.   Re-authorization of Assigned Take Home Vehicles: The Assigned Take Home
Vehicle assignment period shall not be greater than twelve (12) months unless
re-authorized by the Chief Administrative Officer or otherwise specified in a
collective bargaining agreement for represented employees.
No City employee shall operate a city vehicle outside the greater Albuquerque
metropolitan area without first submitted written justification and receiving
the required approval by both the Director of the user Department and Chief
Administrative Officer.
The City is not responsible for lost or damaged personal property. Valuables
should not be left in any City vehicles when parked overnight at an employee’s
residence. Unattended vehicles should be locked at all times. Employees shall
ensure parking is at a safe, secure, and legal location.
V.   Procedures:
The Fleet Division of the Department of Finance and Administrative Services
shall be the executive agency in charge of administering the provisions of this
AI.
Pre-positioned Vehicles:
   1.   Pre-positioned Vehicles shall be parked overnight at their Designated
Parking Areas and keys promptly returned to locations designated by the
Director of the user Department.
   2.   The Director of each user Department shall identify a fleet
administrator to ensure that all drivers (City employee) are accountable for
ensuring that each City vehicle is in proper operating condition daily
(checking tire pressure, fluid levels, etc.), receives preventive maintenance
according to schedule, is in compliance with vehicle emissions testing, and
reports vehicle problems and or damage.
   3.   Not less than annually, the Fleet Division will make recommendations to
the CAO for reassignment of City vehicles that appear to be underutilized. The
Fleet Division will serve as the facilitator of the Fleet Review Committee,
comprised of Department representatives who will be responsible for identifying
underutilized vehicles.
VI.   Motor Pool Dispatch Vehicles:
   1.   Shall be dispatched and maintained by the Fleet Division from
centralized locations accessible to City employees.
   2.   Motor Pool Dispatch Vehicles are to be returned to the lot from which
they were removed, the parking brake set and the vehicle locked.
   3.   The employee is to notify the Fleet Division immediately of any damage
or mechanical problems with a Motor Pool Dispatch Vehicle.
   4.   Employees shall follow all motor pool guidelines established by the
Fleet Division.
VII.   Take-Home Vehicles:
   1.   For the purposes of the this AI, and in addition to the Assigned Take
Home Vehicle definition, a “take-home” vehicle is one that is assigned
exclusively to an individual because of the nature of their job duties and that
they are authorized to operate outside of normal working hours. Absent union
contract provisions to the contrary, no employee shall be authorized to use an
Assigned Take Home Vehicle unless:
      a.   The employee’s primary residence is within the City limits; and
      b.   The employee must normally respond to after-hour Call-Outs or attend
after-hour meetings on an average of two (2) times per week; or
      c.   Call-Outs must be an operational benefit to the city and related to
the mitigation of public health and or safety emergencies, which require
immediate response to protect life and property.
   Department Directors have the authority to grant permission to allow a City
vehicle to be driven to an employee’s residence outside the take-home vehicle
boundaries, however, only after the employee submits special written
justification to the Department Director and the request is approved by the
Chief Administrative Officer. Formal notification of the permission must be
provided to the Fleet Division.
   2.   Department Directors are responsible for conducting annual reviews to
ensure employees with Assigned Take Home Vehicles are still qualified by
verifying there is no change in employment status or work assignment; those
reviews must be documented in writing and filed with the annual application
required in Section 3 below.
   3.   Applications for a “take-home” vehicle are available from the Fleet
Division. The employee must complete and sign the form certifying they have
read and understand the AI which governs the take-home vehicle policy. The
employee must deliver the application and any required documents therein to the
Department Director for their recommendation, prior to the employee being
assigned the vehicle.
   The Director shall submit the completed application upon initial assignment
of a take home vehicle or before January 1 st of each year, with their
recommendation, to the Fleet Division for review. The Fleet Division will in
turn submit the form to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) for final
approval or disapproval.
   If approved by the CAO, the original application will be forwarded back to
the Fleet Division and maintained on file by the Fleet Division who will be
responsible for appropriate billing to the approving Department. The Fleet
Division will provide the Department a copy of the approved application for
their files.
   4.   Authorization to operate an Assigned Take Home Vehicle is automatically
rescinded whenever an employee is transferred or promoted. If the employee
believes they still qualify for a “take-home” vehicle in their new position,
they must initiate the application process.
   Department Directors directly, or through their designees, are responsible
to notify the Fleet Division of any changes.
   Falsification or misrepresentation on the application may result in
immediate revocation of the “take-home” authorization, as well as other
disciplinary action.
VIII.   Temporary Rotating or Seasonal Use “Take-Home” Vehicles:
   1.   From time to time, a Director may determine that it is in the City’s
best interest for one or more employees, concurrently or sequentially, to have
the use of a “take-home” vehicle. For example, it may reduce response time if
employees whose job duties require them to rotate being on-call for emergencies
are provided with a “take-home” vehicle on those days they are in on-call
status. The criteria and application process for approval of rotating or
seasonal use of a “take-home” vehicle is the same as for a fulltime “take-home”
vehicle, as outlined above.
   2.   Occasional late night or early morning meetings are not justification
for requesting authorization of use of a “take-home” vehicle.
   3.   Department Directors directly, or though their designees, are
responsible for management, monitoring and enforcement of this policy. Within
thirty (30) days of the effective date of this AI, each Department Director
shall conduct a review of every employee currently operating a “take-home”
vehicle to determine that the authorization is still appropriate.
   4.   City employees found to be in violation of this AI will be subject to
disciplinary action.
REFERENCES:   IRS Regulations for Take-Home Vehicles (Available at
www.irs.gov); City of Albuquerque Personnel Rules and Regulations - City
Operator Permit Policy; City of Albuquerque Risk Management Manual; City of
Albuquerque Code of Ordinances F/S O-06-57, section 8-2-1-24 – Driver’s
Prohibited Acts; City of Albuquerque Motor Pool Guidelines

AI NO: 4-7
CITY VEHICLES PARKING IN METERED SPACES
TITLE:   City Vehicles Parking in Metered Spaces
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Municipal Development
This Administrative Instruction refers to City vehicles parking at metered
parking spaces throughout the city, especially in the downtown area, and in
some cases parking overnight at metered spaces. Parking meters are for use by
the general public and on occasion by city vehicles provided, in the case of
the latter, that the city employee utilizing the city vehicle is responsible
for the payment of any parking fee and subject to any time limitations. Metered
spaces are not to be used as daily, weekly or monthly parking.
City Departments are responsible for securing parking privileges for all
vehicles. Such privileges will normally be expected to be at City owned
facilities. Effective June 1, 1998, Parking Enforcement Officers will be
issuing violation citations to city vehicles parking in expired meter spaces or
any other parking violation. Unpaid tickets or failure to move vehicles will
result in towing and associated fines. Fines will be the responsibility of
vehicle operators and not the departments and may subject the employee to
discipline.

AI NO: 4-8
REPAIR TO VEHICLES THAT EXCEED BOOK VALUE
TITLE: Repair to Vehicles that Exceed Book Value
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
The City will not make repairs to vehicles in which the repair costs exceed the
book value of that unit. This policy spells out how the City will identify
which repairs will be made to vehicles, and which vehicles must be removed from
service because they are not economically viable to repair.
   1.   When any vehicle is brought to any Fleet Maintenance Facility for
extensive repair, a financial investment analysis will be performed. The Fleet
Division will evaluate whether or not it makes economic sense to repair the
unit. A predetermined set of criteria will be used to evaluate the vehicle,
including mileage, recent repair costs, book value, and current maintenance
needs.
   2.   The Fleet Division will not authorize further repair to a vehicle if
the cost of the repairs exceeds the value of the vehicle. This rule will apply
to all vehicles, with some flexibility taken into consideration for heavy,
specialized, or emergency type vehicles.
   3.   Fleet Division staff will prepare a detailed report on all such units
specifying the information listed in 1. A Surplus/Salvage Property form
containing a Director or Manager signature will be prepared by the department/
division that is assigned to the vehicle and submitted to the Fleet Division
for processing. Surplus/Salvage Property forms that are not submitted within 30
days of notification to the department/division will be signed, processed, and
moved to the Public Surplus for auction by the Fleet Division. The Fleet
Division will not repair units that cost more than the value of the vehicle
without written approval of the CAO.
REFERENCES:   None.

AI NO: 4-9
PROHIBITING SMOKING AND THE USE OF SMOKELESS TOBACCO PRODUCTS ON CITY PROPERTY
AND VEHICLES
TITLE:   Prohibiting Smoking and the Use of Smokeless Tobacco Products on City
Property and Vehicles
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Legal Department
This Administrative Instruction Governs Smoking and the Use of Smokeless
Tobacco Products on City Property and in and Around City Vehicles.
DEFINITIONS:
"City Contractor" means (1) anyone working under contract with the City at
times they perform the contract on City property or (2) anyone who is an
employee of a company providing labor to the City at the times they perform
services or labor on City property.
"City Employee" means all people employed in any manner by the City and receive
any compensation of any type from the City for their services.
"City Property" means all real property owned or leased by the City or real
property occupied by City employees in their normal duties. City property
includes but is not limited to all buildings of any type, parking structures
and lots and all other structures located on City property.
"City Vehicle" means any vehicle owned, leased or borrowed for the use by the
City. City vehicle also means any vehicle under the control of any City
employee. City vehicle does not mean a vehicle owned and operated by a City
contractor unless such contractor provides a vehicle to the City for use by
City employees.
"City Volunteer" means all volunteers for City programs who are under the
direction of a person employed by the City while providing their volunteer
services on or at City Property.
“Smokeless Tobacco Products” means loose leaf, pouch, pulverized or shredded
tobacco products that are chewed, snuffed, or placed in the mouth instead of
being smoked. Nicotine replacement therapies approved by the Food and Drug
Administration, including, but not limited to nicotine gum, lozenge, patch, and
nasal spray, are not smokeless tobacco products.
“Smoking” or “smoke” means inhaling, exhaling, burning, or carrying any lighted
or heated cigar, cigarette, or pipe, or any other lighted or heated tobacco or
plant product intended for inhalation, including hookah, whether natural or
synthetic, in any manner or in any form. “Smoking” or “smoke” also includes the
use of an electronic smoking device which creates an aerosol or vapor, in any
manner or in any form, or the use of any oral smoking device for the purpose of
circumventing the prohibition of smoking in this Administrative Instruction.
"Vehicle" means any device in, upon, or by which any person or property is or
may be transported or drawn propelled by a power other than human power, and
includes but is not limited to automobiles, trucks, trailers, motorcycles,
tractors, buggies, and wagons. The term "vehicle" includes all devices
regardless of the type or power, including but not limited to electric power
and any type of gas or gasoline power or any combination thereof and any
connected trailer or semi-trailer.
PROHIBITION:
No City employee, City volunteer or City contractor shall smoke or use
smokeless tobacco products in or within 30 feet of a City vehicle when such
vehicle is not located on City property.
No person, including but not limited to City employees, City volunteers or City
contractors shall smoke or use smokeless tobacco products within 30 feet of the
entrance to any structure located on City property. This prohibition applies to
all members of the public.
REFERENCES:   None

AI NO: 4-14
CITY OPERATORS PERMIT SUSPENSION/REVOCATION
TITLE:   City Operators Permit Suspension/Revocation
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administration Services
The City of Albuquerque has a vested interest in ensuring that City employees
operating City vehicles do not pose risks either to themselves or to the public
they serve. Accordingly, the City issues a City Operator Permit (COP) to
employees required to drive its vehicles or their personal vehicle on City
business.
Upon receiving notification of a suspended COP, the employee may not operate
any vehicle on city business until the COP is restored. Additionally, any
employee who, as a condition of employment must possess a COP to operate City
vehicles, will have ninety (90) days from the date of the suspension to either
have the matter adjudicated and present a valid state operator's license
without restriction, or to transfer to another position within the City that
does not require a COP. During this period and at the City's sole discretion,
the employee will either be assigned other job duties for which a COP is not
required, or will be allowed to take Annual Leave or Leave Without Pay during
this period. At the end of this time-frame, if the employee's COP has not been
restored or the employee has not been able to be selected for transfer to
another position, the employee shall be terminated for failing to meet the
essential functions of the position and the minimum qualifications for the
position. An employee selecting to transfer to another vacant position must
meet the minimum qualifications for the position, be selected as part of the
normal selection process and accept, if the position is at a lower salary
range, a reduction in pay as required by the Personnel Rules and Regulations.
Upon notification that an employee's COP has been suspended, the Director of
the Human Resources Department shall initiate a review of the affected
employee's position to validate that driving is an essential function of the
position and to assess if the department is able to transfer the employee to
another position in the same classification which does not require driving.
This review will consider the employee's duties as described in the relevant
job description and actually performed by the employee. Such review will be
completed as soon as is practicable but in no case shall the initiation of this
process exceed thirty (30) days from receipt of notice. The Director of Human
Resources shall provide the results of the review to the relevant Department
Director. If the Department Director disagrees with the results of the review,
the matter shall be submitted for a final determination by the Chief
Administrative Officer (CAO) within five (5) days. The CAO shall review the
matter and make a final determination.
If the final determination is that driving is not an essential function of the
position or that the department can laterally transfer the employee into a like
position that does not require driving, the employee will be returned to work.
REFERENCES: City Operator Permit Policy Section 1200 of the Personnel Rules and
Regulations

AI NO: 4-15
FUEL CONSERVATION POLICY
TITLE: Fuel Conservation Policy
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
Purpose
Adopting a policy that creates a uniform idle-reduction and fuel conservation
program will enable the City of Albuquerque to lead by example, control costs,
inspire the community and staff, and preserve the environment.
   I.   Policy
   This policy addresses major contributing factors such as, vehicle cold
starts, vehicle idling, hard accelerations, etc. Implementation of the policy
will reduce fuel and repair related costs, and mitigate the environmental
impact.
   II.   Responsibility
      A.   Reports of violations of mandatory procedures should be made
directly to the supervisor of the violating party, or if unknown, the
Department of Finance and Administrative Services Fleet Division (Fleet
Division) can be contacted.
      B.   It is the responsibility of each Division Manager to ensure
compliance with the policy and procedures.
   III.   Procedures
      A.   Mandatory
         1.   Vehicles shall not be left idling while tools, equipment or
passengers are loaded or unloaded;
         2.   Vehicles shall not be left idling while parked for the purpose of
keeping the cab cool or heated;
         3.   Start up for turbo-charged diesel engines shall not exceed three
minutes;
         4.   Cool down for turbo- charged diesel engines shall not exceed five
minutes, unless it is a heavy duty vehicle that has returned from a long
distance trip or was towing a sizeable load, or an Exemption set forth below
applies;
         5.   Drivers shall observe all posted speed limits, maintain a steady
speed, and anticipate traffic flows;
         6.   Ensure maintenance on vehicles and equipment is current;
         7.   Properly stock vehicles prior to leaving for the job work site to
avoid excessive return trips;
         8.   Drive the most fuel-efficient vehicle available when there are
options; and
         9.   Ensure tires are kept properly inflated, 10% under inflation can
decrease fuel economy by 3-4%.
      B.   Recommendations
         1.   Ensure daily, that job requirements are managed in an efficient
manner while reducing unnecessary travel;
         2.   Combine trips, when feasible; and
         3.   Carpool when attending meetings, trainings sessions or going to
work site. 
Exemptions
This policy does not apply to a vehicle or piece of equipment during the
following situations when:
      A.   Traffic conditions exist which a driver has no control over,
including but not limited to: stopped in a line of traffic, stopped at a
railroad crossing, or stopped at a construction zone;
      B.   Idling when necessary for testing, maintenance, repair or diagnostic
purposes;
      C.   Idling when necessary to ascertain that the vehicle and/or off-road
piece of equipment is in safe operating condition, and is equipped as required
by all provisions of law and established safety policies;
      D.   The vehicle is not expected to restart due to mechanical or
electrical problems;
      E.   Idling the engine is required to power auxiliary equipment other
than a heater or air conditioner, including but not limited to, hoist, lift,
computers, or safety lighting;
      F.   Idling is necessary to cool down a turbo-charged heavy-duty vehicle
that has been driven for a long period of time or used to pull heavy loads. The
cool down period for such vehicles is up to but, may not exceed 15 minutes in
accordance with the manufacturer’s recommendation;
      G.   Idling when necessary to perform an exhaust regeneration to clean
out soot build up from a diesel vehicle exhaust system, but only for the time
necessary to clean the system, which is typically 20 to 30 minutes; and
      H.   Severe weather conditions dictate the need to idle the vehicle for
ice and snow removal. Vehicle should only be left idling for the period
required to remove ice and snow, and should not be left unattended.
REFERENCES:   None.

AI NO: 5-1
SECURITY POLICY FOR CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE EMPLOYEE IDENTIFICATION BADGES
TITLE:   Security Policy for City of Albuquerque Employee Identification Badges
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Municipal Development
While on City of Albuquerque property personnel will have their identification
badges displayed on their person.
The following guidelines are established concerning the issuance of employee
identification badges.
   a. Employees will wear ID badges on the outer most layer of their clothing,
above the waist area at all times while at their work site or in any City of
Albuquerque owned or operated facility or property.
   b. The City of Albuquerque will issue a badge clip to each employee. Should
the employee choose to purchase a lanyard, it must be appropriate for use and
work environment. Employees are encouraged to use safety or break away
lanyards.
   c. Human Resources and City Security will be responsible for the issuance of
the identification cards, and each employee will sign for receipt of the ID
card.
   d. Loss of employee identification card must be immediately reported to the
employee’s supervisor. The loss of second and subsequent cards will result in a
replacement fee of $15.00 paid to City Treasury. This fee will be incurred by
the employee. Loss or misuse of the card could lead to disciplinary measures
being taken against the employee.
   e. Identification cards must be returned to their immediate supervisor in
the event of the following:
      i. Transfer to another department
         1. Employee will have 30 days to report to Human Resources to receive
a new identification card.
         2. Upon demand from the employee’s supervisor or appropriate Security
Personnel.
      ii. Suspension
      iii. Termination/Retirement
   f. Each department may be issued Visitor badges, which will be numbered for
accountability. Departments are encouraged to issue temporary badges when
Visitors are anticipated to be in a City owned facility for longer than one (1)
work day. It will be up to the issuing Department to implement procedures to
secure the return of the issued Visitor badge.
Temporary, contractor and/or seasonal employees will be issued an ID card if
their employment is anticipated to extend beyond 90 days.
   g. Identification cards will be color-coded for restricted access, and
Treasury purposes. The City Treasurer will determine the level of cash handling
authority and issue the appropriate color code. The Chief Administrative
Officer will determine the level of access for employees into restricted or
sensitive areas and issue a “Green All Access” color to the ID card.
This Administrative Instruction shall remain in effect until amended.

REAL ESTATE RECORDS
TITLE:   Real Estate Records
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Planning
The Real Property Division is required to keep current and complete records of
all real estate transactions involving leases, licenses, land use agreements,
memorandum of understanding documents, memorandum of agreement documents,
intergovernmental agreements, contracts, facility use agreements, easements,
purchases, sales, transfers, condemnations, donations and all other related
property documents and agreements. This includes property to be leased,
purchased or otherwise acquired by the City and property owned by the City to
be leased, sold or otherwise transferred to the private sector or any other
public sector entity.
It is the responsibility of each department director to involve the Real
Property Division in every real estate transaction, from the earliest possible
date. This includes sales, purchases, trades, leases, easements, donations, and
any other transaction involving real property. No transaction of any type
involving real estate in any department may be initiated or concluded without
the involvement of the Real Property Division. It is the responsibility of each
department director to provide the Real Property Division with all
documentation and information related to any and all transactions involving
real property that is required to complete the real property files.
A transmittal form available from the Real Property Division must be attached
to all real estate documents which are presented for the Chief Administrative
Officer's signature. This transmittal form must be signed by the Legal
Department and the Real Property Division Manager, or his/her designee, before
delivery to the Chief Administrative Officer for signature. These documents,
after approval and signature by the Chief Administrative Officer, will be
returned to the Real Property Division Manager who will forward the original to
the City Clerk/Recorder for filing.
In addition, all summary plats involving vacations, park dedications, or City-
owned property must be signed by the Real Property Division Manager or the Real
Property Division Manager's designee.
In addition to the information each department is required to provide to the
Real Property Division, as described above, and to further facilitate efficient
processing of transactions and effective management of City-owned or City-
leased property, the Real Property Division will also collect from all
departments, all property related data, including but not limited to utilities,
maintenance and cost information, and any information or records concerning
revenue generation or in-kind services received.
The Real Property Division may develop guidelines and procedures concerning the
use, property management roles and responsibilities, and maintenance of City
owned properties. The guidelines and procedures may also include instructions
for the process and forms to be used for providing real property documentation
(including the costs of ownership and maintenance, as well as the revenue
generated or in-kind services provided), the desired and required transaction
documentation for the purchase, lease or sale of City owned property, and the
property data and documentation requirements needed for the property management
software (e.g., location, managing department, use, floor plans/facility
plans).
Because the Aviation Department and the Metropolitan Redevelopment Agency
maintain their own real property functions, this instruction does not apply to
leases and agreements managed by the Aviation Department and the Metropolitan
Redevelopment Agency, except as to the requirement that each must still provide
the Real Property Division with copies of all documentation related to the
acquisition, trade, sale, lease, or donation of real property, or any easements
granted or acquired on their respective properties.

DISPOSITION OF VACATED STREETS
TITLE:   Disposition of Vacated Streets
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Planning
The following policy shall govern disposition of streets which are requested to
be vacated, pursuant to the City of Albuquerque Subdivision Ordinances, Section
7-11-42.C R.O. 1974, and pursuant to the extraterritorial platting and planning
jurisdiction of the City, Section 3-20-5 and 3-20-12 NMSA 1978. It should be
noted that the City may decide to dispose of the fee interest in the vacated
street, while retaining easements for utilities, drainage, or some other
municipal purpose.
A. Upon confirmation by Real Property that the City owns the right-of-way fee
simple, the Real Property Manager shall determine whether to retain all or part
of the vacated right-of-way for municipal purposes or to dispose of, at market
value as determined by Real Property, part or all of the vacated right-of-way
to abutting property owners.
Each abutting property owner is entitled to acquire up to the center line of
the nonessential right-of-way abutting the property owner’s land. However, if
one of the abutting property owners fails to notify the City of his or her
election to purchase the nonessential vacated right-of-way as provided in the
ordinance or does not wish to acquire the nonessential vacated right-of- way,
the other owner may acquire all of the adjoining nonessential right- of-way.
The City shall record a final plat of the vacated right-of-way retained by the
City as an independent lot, or incorporate the vacated right-of-way into
adjoining City-owned property, if applicable.
B. If an owner replats a subdivision that vacates all or part of a previously
dedicated right-of-way and dedicates a new, acceptable right-of-way which has
value equal to or greater than that of the vacated right-of-way as determined
by Real Property, and the same owner owns all property abutting the vacated
right-of-way, then the vacated right-of-way shall be conveyed to the property
owner without consideration due from the owner, except for a processing fee.
However, if the right-of-way to be dedicated is less valuable than the right-
of-way to be vacated, then the property owner shall be expected to pay an
amount representing the difference in value between the vacated right-of-way
and the right-of-way to be dedicated. The City shall pay no compensation for
dedicated right-of-way of greater value than the vacated right-of-way.
REFERENCES: City of Albuquerque Subdivision Ordinances, Section 7-11-42.C R.O.
1974
Section 3-20-5 and 3-20-12 NMSA 1978
