WATER, ELECTRIC AND NATURAL GAS UTILITIES CLEARINGHOUSE
TITLE:   Water, Electric and Natural Gas Utilities Clearinghouse
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Municipal Development
Background:
In order to ensure the proper management of water, electric and natural gas
utility accounts, a utilities clearinghouse was established for municipal
operations. The Utilities Clearinghouse was created by this Administrative
Instruction and adherence of responsibility from all City Departments/Division
and/or User Agencies (DDUA) will be monitored by the Facilities and Energy
Management Division (FEMD), Department of Municipal Development (DMD) located
at 1801 Fourth Street NW, Albuquerque, New Mexico 87102.
All Departments shall identify a Fiscal Manager to reconcile information and to
coordinate utility account information with FEMD. If at any time there is a
Fiscal Manager change, it must be communicated to FEMD in a written memorandum.
All City DDUA will be required to follow the procedures outlined below when
water, electric or natural gas utility services are needed:
Procedures:
Initiating Water, Electric and Natural Gas Service
1.   DDUA may initiate water, electric and natural gas service from the
appropriate utility.
2.   Upon initiation, the DDUA must complete and submit a Utility Account
Billing Information Form with the address, activity number, and description of
the service required to FEMD at 1801 Fourth Street N.W., Building B,
Albuquerque, New Mexico 87102. This form will also serve as the instrument to
ensure the proper assignment of this newly identified account to the monthly
COA utility billing with the identified address, activity number, and proper
rate structure.
Terminating Water Electric and Natural Gas Service
1.   DDUA may terminate water, electric and natural gas service from the
appropriate utility.
2.   Upon termination, the DDUA must complete and submit a Utility Account
Billing Information Form with the address, activity number, and description of
the terminated service to FEMD at 1801 Fourth Street N.W., Building B,
Albuquerque, New Mexico 87102. This form will also serve as the instrument to
ensure the proper termination/removal of the account from the monthly COA
utility billing.
Monthly Compliance
1.   The appropriate DDUA will be responsible for monitoring water, electric
and natural gas billing on a monthly basis, and reconciling these charges to
the general ledger. DMD will provide a monthly spreadsheet with billing
information. Training information on utilizing composite billing is available
by contacting FEMD at 768-5310.
2.   Any DDUA that begins a new construction, renovation or building/facility
demolition project, must submit Utility Account Billing Information Form to
FEMD prior to initiating services.
3.   If there is a seasonal facility or seasonal meter, the DDUA must notify
FEMD of this type of service by completing and forwarding a Utility Account
Billing Information Form. The FEMD will ensure the proper rate schedule and
billing information for the seasonal account is reflected in the monthly COA
utility billing.
4.   If there are any changes to the utility accounts such as name, activity
number, seasonal usage or ownership at any time during the year, the DDUA will
be responsible for providing this information to FEMD immediately using the
Utility Account Billing Information Form.
Annual Update
1.   At the beginning of each fiscal year, FEMD will provide each DDUA with a
comprehensive list of City water, electric and gas utility service accounts for
annual verification by City DDUA.
2.   If there are any changes to the utility accounts such as name, activity
number, seasonal usage, account status or ownership, the DDUA will be
responsible for providing this information to FEMD with a new Utility Account
Billing Information Form with verified and correct information for each
account. Failure to submit the updated form could result in disconnection of
service.
3.   If there are no changes identified during the Annual Update, the Fiscal
Manager must return the list of accounts with a written formal memo to FEMD
stating that all information is verified and all account information is
correct.

AI NO: 6-11
ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT OF REAL PROPERTY ACQUISITIONS
TITLE:   Environmental Assessment of Real Property Acquisitions
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Planning
The following policy shall govern the acquisition by purchase of all real
property by the City. This policy shall not apply to the acquisition of real
property by eminent domain or by plat dedication.
For all purchases of real property, the City, through the Real Property
Division, shall obtain the following environmental assessments of the real
property by qualified licensed environmental consultants.
1. A Phase I Environmental Assessment.
2. A Phase II Environmental Assessment if the Phase I Environmental Assessment
recommends a Phase II Assessment.
3. Further environmental assessments, including those recommended by a Phase II
Environmental Assessment, if performed.
4. The City shall require the completion of the recommendations set forth in
any of the environmental assessments, if any, as either a precondition to the
closing of the real estate contract, or as a condition subsequent to the
closing of the contract as determined by the City.
Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the City may purchase real
property that is determined to be contaminated so long as the environmental
condition of the property will not prevent the planned use of the property by
the City, and the purchase is approved by the Chief Administrative Officer.
Additionally, the requirement to obtain any or all of the Environmental
Assessments and the completion of any recommendations may be waived, as is
reasonably determined by the Real Property Division Manager, and approved by
the Chief Administrative Officer, based upon factors including, but not limited
to, the location of the property, the size of the property, the cost of the
property, the intended use of the property, and the necessity of the property
to the City.

ENSURING CPOA COMPLAINT FORMS AND RECRUITING BROCHURES
ARE AVAILABLE AT LIBRARIES AND COMMUNITY CENTERS
TITLE:   Ensuring CPOA Complaint Forms and Recruiting Brochures are Available
at Libraries and Community Centers
PRIMARY DEPARTMENTS:   APD; Family and Community Services; Cultural Services;
Senior Affairs
1.   General
The City must "make complaint forms and informational materials, including
brochures and posters," regarding making a complaint or commendation about an
officer, available at City locations, including libraries and community
centers, as agreed to in the Court Approved Settlement Agreement in the case of
United States v. City of Albuquerque, 14-CV-1025. In addition, the City must
recruit "qualified applicants from a broad cross section of the community'' to
the police academy, and thus, as part of the City's recruitment strategy, the
City will make APD recruitment brochures available at libraries and community
centers.
This Administrative Instruction defines the process by which the City will
ensure that such documents are available at libraries and community centers and
restocked as necessary.
2.   Application
   a.   APD must refill out-of-stock and low stocked complaint forms,
informational brochures and materials at each library, community center, and
senior center.
   b.   Each library, community center, and senior center must:
      I.   On the first of each month or the first subsequent business day,
ensure that the following documents are stocked, visible to the public, and
easily accessible to the public: Albuquerque Police Department Complaint or
Commendation Form (in both English and Spanish: Civilian Police Oversight
Agency Informational Brochure (in English and Spanish); and APD recruitment
brochure.
      II.   If there are less than ten APD recruitment brochures in stock,
contact Sergeant Deanne Otzenberger at (505) 228-2559 or Drush@cabq.gov to
request additional recruitment brochures.
      III.   If there are less than ten Complaint/Commendation forms or CPOA
Informational Brochures in stock, call Kathy Roybal-Nunez at 768-2880 to
request additional forms or brochures.
      iv.   Ensure that the "Let's put 'COMMUNITY' into APD COMMUNITY POLICING"
poster, in English and Spanish, is posted in a location visible to the public
and is not torn, tattered or worn in a way that interferes with legibility.
      v.   If the poster needs to be replaced, call Kathy Roybal-Nunez at 768-
2880 and ask that APD replace the poster.

Personnel
AI NO: 7-1
SIGNATURE AUTHORITY FOR PERSONNEL MATTERS (October 2023)
TITLE: Signature Authority for Personnel Matters
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Human Resources
Background:
The City of Albuquerque acknowledges that appropriate delegation of authority
is required for efficient processes associated with the signing of
documentation for personnel matters.
This AI provides general guidelines for delegation of signature authority. For
items not covered in this Administrative Instruction, reference State statute,
City Ordinance, City Resolution, City Rules and Regulations, the Merit System
Ordinance, or City policies. This AI supersedes all other personnel related
AIs.
Definitions:
   A.   Chief Administrative Officer (CAO)
   B.   Department Director- Director of the designated department
   C.   Executive Administrator (EA) – Assigned administrator of the Mayor’s
executive team with administrative oversight for assigned department(s). The
assigned Executive Administrator shall be designated by title through approved
and posted organizational chart.
   D.   Human Resources Director (HRD)
   E.   Middle Management- Employment of individual where the job description
contains the essential function of directly supervising others. These middle
management level positions are levels of management below Deputy Director and
Associate Director.
General Policy:
The City of Albuquerque CAO hereby delegates signature authority associated
with the following personnel workflows:
   I.   Creation, re-classification or release of positions
      A.   Newly-created, non-funded positions; reclassifications requiring
additional budgetary funding; and non- routine requests must be approved by the
HRD, Budget Officer and EA.
      B.   Reclassifications not requiring additional budget or release of
funded positions must be approved by the Department Director(s) associated with
the reclassification, Budget Analyst(s), HRD and EA.
   II.   Hiring
      A.   Hiring of the CAO, any deputy administrative officers, Chief of
Police, Fire Chief, City Clerk, and the City Attorney require approval of
Council as provided in Article IV, Section 4 of the City Charter.
      B.   Unclassified Employees
         1.   All Unclassified Directors, Deputy Director and Associate
Director Employees must be approved by the CAO.
         2.   All unclassified Middle Management employees must be approved by
the Department Director and EA.
         3.   All other unclassified staff level positions must be approved by
the Department Director, Budget Officer and EA.
      C.   Classified Employees
         1.   All Middle Management employees in titles of Assistant or
Associate Director must be approved by the Department Director and EA.
         2.   All other Middle Management and staff level positions must be
approved by the Department Director.
      D.   Positions identified as Difficult to Recruit must be approved by the
HRD and EA. Hiring Incentive limits have been established through AI 7-44.
   II.   Compensation
      A.   All wage adjustment requests to base pay must be submitted to the
Human Resources Department, Classification and Compensation Division for
appropriate benchmarking.
      B.   All permanent wage adjustment requests must be approved by the CAO.
      C.   Temporary Upgrades
         1.   Temporary Upgrades for Director or Deputy Director Positions must
be approved by the CAO.
         2.   Temporary Upgrades for Middle Management and staff level
positions must be approved by the Department Director and EA.
   III.   Leave
      A.   With Pay
         1.   Accrued vacation, sick, and injury time approval
            a)   Time off request of Directors must be approved by EA.
            b)   Time off requests of Deputy Directors and Associate Directors
must be approved by Department Directors
            c)   Time off requests of Middle Management and staff are approved
by their designated supervisor
      B.   Without Pay
         1.   Time off requests of Directors must be approved by CAO
         2.   Time off requests of less than 2 weeks of Deputy Directors and
Associate Directors must be approved by Department Director and EA.
         3.   Time off request of more than 2 weeks of Deputy Directors must be
approved by CAO
         4.   Time off request of less than 2 weeks of Middle Management and
staff as approved by Department Director and EA.
         5.   Time off requests of more than 2 weeks of Middle Management and
staff must be approved by CAO.
      C.   Leave Donations
         1.   Leave donations requested from employees within a Department must
be approved by the Department Director
         2.   The Department Director, HRD and EA must approve leave donations
requested from employees within other departments.
      D.   All other leave requests must be approved by the CAO.
   IV.   Resignation acceptance or Termination
      A.   Director or Deputy Director position resignation acknowledged or
termination approved by EA.
      B.   Middle Management and staff position resignations acknowledged or
termination approved by Department Director
   V.   Temporary Assignment of Signature Authority- Temporary signature
authority may be delegated in writing by the official who holds the applicable
position.
      A.   Temporary signature authority delegated for less than a 2-week
period must be approved by EA.
      B.   Temporary signature authority delegated for more than a 2-week
period must be approved by CAO.
   VI.   Notice of Delegated Action
      A.   Signatory actions taken as a result of the delegated authority
included and/or referenced to Administrative Instruction No. 7-1 must be
documented and communicated to the Chief Administrative Officer with 5 days of
action. The Chief Administrative Officer must also document and communicate
signatory actions taken on behalf of the Executive Administrators or department
staff to the applicable department(s) Executive Administrator within 5 days of
action.
REFERENCES: Executive Instruction No. 2 Signature Authority; City Charter;
City's Merit System Ordinance; City Personnel Administrative Instructions; and
the City of Albuquerque Personnel Rules and Regulations.

AI NO: 7-2
INJURY TIME ADMINISTRATION, INJURY REPORTING, INITIAL HEALTH CARE PROVIDER
DESIGNATION AND CHANGE OF HEALTH CARE PROVIDER
TITLE:   Injury Time Administration, Injury Reporting, Initial Health Care
Provider Designation and Change of Health Care Provider
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administration Services
The Risk Management Division within the Department of Finance and
Administrative Services is responsible for administering the City’s Workers
Compensation program and the Injury Time benefit, and therefore has established
procedures to assure compliance with City policy and the Workers’ Compensation
Act. This instruction further clarifies those procedures:
   ∙  Employees and supervisors are required to follow the current reporting
requirements of the Risk Management Division. These requirements are available
from the Risk Management Division and are posted on Risk Management Division’s
internal webpage.
   ∙  Department Directors are to ensure that a “City of Albuquerque,
Supervisor’s Injury Investigation Report” is completed immediately after the
injury and submitted to the Risk Management Division within two workdays.
   ∙  The Risk Management Division will verify and approve Injury Time. The
Payroll Office will not release an employee’s Injury Time check until it
receives verification from the Risk Management Division.
   ∙  When a City employee is injured in the course of and arising out of his/
her employment, the City shall provide the worker with reasonable and necessary
health care services. Per the Workers’ Compensation Act (52-1-49 NMSA 1978),
the City shall initially select the health care provider for the injured
worker.
   ∙  Pursuant to NMSA 1978 Section 52-1-49 of the Workers’ Compensation Act,
the worker may elect to change the healthcare provider after 60 days from
initial treatment. Should a worker intend to change from the City’s designated
health care provider, the worker shall complete the “Notice of Change of
Healthcare Provider” and submit it to the Risk Management Division. The form is
available Online at www.workerscomp.state.nm.us.
Injury Reporting and Initial Treatment
The City provides health care services by/through the City Employee Health
Center. City workers shall abide by the following instructions:
   ∙  If EMERGENCY MEDICAL TREATMENT IS NECESSARY CALL 911. Subsequent to the
emergency situation, call the Telephonic Nurse Triage number to report the
injury.
   ∙  For non-emergencies call the Telephonic Nurse Triage number to report the
injury and receive instructions for treatment. If instructed to seek medical
treatment outside of the Employee Health Center, the injured employee must
report to the Employee Health Center prior to returning to work and for any
follow up evaluation or care.
   ∙  Detailed instructions for this procedure are available at the Risk
Management office or on the Risk Management internal webpage. http://
sharepoint.cabq.gov/dfas/risk/WC/default.aspx
REFERENCES:   Workers’ Compensation Act (Section 52-1-49 NMSA 1978) and
Personnel Rules and Regulations Section 401.10 Injury Time.

AI NO: 7-3
HUMAN TRAFFICKING AWARENESS TRAINING FOR CITY EMPLOYEES
TITLE: Human Trafficking Awareness Training for City Employees
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:Human Resources   
Purpose of Administrative Instruction:
This Administrative Instruction serves to implement Council resolution R-24-42
and establish mandatory anti human trafficking awareness training.
Background:
Human Trafficking is a crime wherein someone exploits another person
using force, fraud, or coercion for the purposes of compelled
labor or commercial sex. Human Traffickers operate in every country, state,
city, and town. It’s happening right now in Albuquerque, New Mexico, maybe even
in your community. It’s difficult to realize, because human trafficking often
goes unrecognized, or it’s underreported because victims are afraid, or they
don’t understand what is happening.
Traffickers find vulnerable people and exploit them. Circumstances like
poverty, an unstable living situation, lack of support, social and cultural
inequalities, addiction or substance use, or previous trauma or victimization
are a few of the contributors that can put someone at risk.
The city of Albuquerque is committed to empowering our employees to be aware
and diligent in recognizing, identifying and helping to report Human
Trafficking in our community and help build a safe and sustainable environment
for our residents.
General Policy:
The Employee Learning Center, Albuquerque Fire and Rescue, and Transportation
Departments have collaborated to provide training to all City employees for
Human Trafficking awareness.
This training is mandatory for all City employees on an annual or biennial
basis depending on department specific training requirements.
All new employees will receive Human Trafficking awareness training during
their New Employee Orientation. This training must be completed within two
weeks of the employee’s hire date.
Options for employee trainings will include the following:
Mandatory biennial online training for all Regular and Part-Time employees in
non-public safety or aviation departments. This training is offered online
through the City of Albuquerque Employee Learning Center in the Human Resources
Department.
Mandatory annual online department specific Human Trafficking awareness
training as provided by AFR and APD for all first-responder or Public Safety
Employees.
Mandatory annual Human Trafficking Awareness training as provided by the
Transportation Security Administration through the Aviation Department for all
Aviation employees.
Employee training records will be monitored and managed by the City of
Albuquerque Human Resources Department, and the HR staff in the AFR, APD, ACS
and Aviation departments.
References:
R-24-42

AI NO: 7-5
PRE-EMPLOYMENT MEDICAL EXAMINATIONS
TITLE:   Pre-Employment Medical Examinations
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Job applicants for City employment may be required to submit to and pass
employment medical examinations and alcohol and illegal drug testing.
The medical examination shall be conducted only after a contingent offer of
employment has been made to the job applicant. An alcohol and illegal drug test
shall be conducted in conjunction with the medical examination for SAFETY
SENSITIVE positions as identified by the Director of Human Resources
Department. The medical examination and the alcohol and illegal drug test shall
be completed prior to extending the final approved offer of employment. The
medical examinations shall be conducted by/through the City Employee Health
Center. The medical examinations shall be requested through the Human Resources
Department Director or his/her designee. The results of the medical
examinations shall be identified as pass/fail in the approval process.
A job applicant who passes all other prerequisites for employment but does not
pass the medical examination, alcohol, or drug testing will be notified
pursuant to Personnel Rules and Regulations Section 1100 Substance Abuse
Policy.
The City shall test for alcohol and illegal drugs in conjunction with medical
examinations. However, such tests are not medical examinations, and their
results are not subject to the appeals process contained in Personnel Rules and
Regulations Section 1100 Substance Abuse Policy.
The City prohibits the use of alcohol and illegal drugs at the workplace by all
employees, and the City requires that employees not be under the influence of
alcohol or illegal drugs in the workplace. The City requires that all employees
be in compliance with the requirements of the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988.
The application process shall be terminated for a job applicant who tests
positive for alcohol or an illegal drug pursuant to Personnel Rules and
Regulations Section 1100 Substance Abuse Policy.

AI NO: 7-6
MULTILINGUAL DIFFERENTIAL PAY POLICY
TITLE: Multilingual Differential Pay Policy PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Human Resources
Purpose of Administrative Instruction: This Administrative Instruction
implements a policy for allocating pay incentives for multilingual capable
employees in accordance with R-23-103.
Background: The City of Albuquerque acknowledges that bilingual City employees
help make government services and resources more easily available and
understandable to the diverse residents of Albuquerque, including non-English
speakers and those who use American Sign Language. This AI supersedes all other
Multi or Bilingual Pay related AIs.
Definitions:
1.   CAO – Chief Administrative Officer
2.   Department Director – Director of the designated department
3.   Human Resources Director (HRD)
4.   Safe Harbor Languages
   i.   Spanish
   ii.   American Sign Language (“ASL”)
   iii.   Dine (Navajo)
   iv.   Vietnamese
   v.   Mandarin Chinese
   vi.   Arabic
   vii.   Swahili
5.   Collective Bargaining Agreement(s) CBA
General Policy:
I.   Eligibility:
Eligibility shall include all classified and unclassified positions within the
City. The City emphasizes the importance of using various languages across our
workforce. This list provides a prioritization hierarchy for providing
bilingual pay consideration:
   1)   Emergency Services:
      i.   Albuquerque Police Department
      ii.   Albuquerque Fire Rescue
      iii.   Albuquerque Police 911 Communications
      iv.   Albuquerque Community Safety Department
      v.   Aviation Emergency Communications
   2)   Positions with citizens with special needs/circumstances:
      i.   Senior Affairs Department
      ii.   Department of Youth & Family Services
      iii.   Department of Health, Housing & Homelessness
      iv.   Civil Rights Office
      v.   Violence Intervention Program (VIP)
      vi.   Civilian Police Oversight Agency
      vii.   Transit Department
   3)   Positions or Departments which have daily bilingual citizen contact:
      i.   311 Contact Center Employees
      ii.   Mayor’s Office
      iii.   Animal Welfare Department
      iv.   General Services Department
      v.   Parks & Recreation Department
      vi.   Planning Department
      vii.   Solid Waste Department
   4)   Positions or Departments which have occasional bilingual citizen
contact:
      i.   Arts & Culture Department
      ii.   Aviation Department
      iii.   City Clerk’s Department
      iv.   City Council
      v.   Office of Consumer Protection
      vi.   Economic Development
      vii.   Emergency Management Office
      viii.   Environmental Health Department
      ix.   Equity & Inclusion Office
      x.   Human Resources Department
      xi.   Inspector General’s Office
      xii.   Internal Audit Department
      xiii.   Legal Department
      xiv.   Management & Budget Office
      xv.   Metropolitan Redevelopment Department
      xvi.   Municipal Development
      xvii.   Technology & Innovation Department
I.   PRIORITIZATION
The Department Director of each Department shall prioritize each position to
receive Bilingual Differential Pay within their respective Department
considering the following:
   A.   All roles within the organization are eligible; limited by the
organizations ability to provide appropriate testing;
   B.   Employees demonstrating fluency in Safe Harbor Languages shall be
prioritized over employees who speak other languages;
   C.   Staff positions shall be prioritized before leadership positions;
   D.   Non-Probationary employees shall be prioritized over Probationary
employees;
   E.   Eligible Jobs require individuals to utilize a different language more
than 10% of the time;
   F.   Temporary Employees shall be eligible for Bilingual Differential Pay
only after all full time employees who qualify;
   G.   Employees who assist co-workers with Bilingual Language (10% or more
their time) shall be eligible for Bilingual Differential Pay;
   H.   Any employee may lose their Bilingual Differential Pay if they change
their job classification into a position or Department with a lower
prioritization.
   I.   Language pay will be provided when an employee has certified for their
first language; no additional pay consideration shall be provided for multiple
languages;
   J.   A maximum of 377 employees may qualify for Bilingual Pay Differential;
   K.   Employees who utilize Bilingual Interpretation Services shall not be
eligible for Bilingual Pay Differential;
   L.   Employees who receive Bilingual Differential Pay shall be required to
use their Bilingual Language to the best of their ability and shall become
ineligible for Bilingual Pay Differential should they become unable or
unwilling;
   M.   Employees who qualify for Bilingual Differential Pay but do not receive
Bilingual Pay Differential due to budgetary limitations shall not use their
Bilingual proficiency.
   N.   Employees who receive Bilingual Differential Pay shall be required to
assist other Departments with their Bilingual skills as needed;
II.   TESTING:
   A.   Human Resources will oversee the bilingual examination, certify exam
results, and determine effective date of the bilingual pay.
   B.   Testing resources shall be determined by Human Resources in
collaboration with the Office of Equity and Inclusion.
   C.   The City will only fund testing for any employee once per year.
   D.   If an employee would like to retest in the same year, the individual
may self-pay for retesting using City approved testing resources.
   E.   The City will only pay for testing for the same individual 2 times over
a 5-year period.
III.   CERTIFICATION/RECERTIFICATION OF BILINGUAL ABILITY
   A.   The supervisor of an employee who receives Bilingual Differential Pay
shall be required to certify that the position requires the employee to use
their bilingual skills at least 10% of the time on an annual basis;
   B.   Supervisors are required to notify the Human Resources Department
immediately if a qualifying position no longer uses bilingual skills the
required 10% of the time.
   C.   The Human Resources Department shall confirm that the supervisor of an
employee who receives Bilingual Pay Differential has certified/recertified on
an annual basis. An employee will cease receiving Bilingual Pay Differential
should they not be certified/recertified on an annual basis.
IV.   DIFFERENTIAL PAY
A salary differential allowance shall be paid to employees in positions
requiring bilingual proficiency that qualify and shall be designated as
follows:
   A.   $.75 per hour applied to regular hours/hours worked for employees
certified in performing both listening/speaking and reading/writing proficiency
or
   B.   For employees who are not certified in both listening/speaking and
reading writing:
      i)   $.30 per hour for listening/speaking proficiency
      ii)   $.20 per hour for reading/writing proficiency
References:
R-23-130
 
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/35cea8d42b9362d804e1add43109a67648282f64/
IMAGES/0-0-0-2654.jpg]

AI NO: 7-7
CITY PAYROLL DEDUCTION POLICY - NON-CITY SPONSORED ACTIVITIES OR INSURANCE
TITLE:   City Payroll Deduction Policy - Non-City Sponsored Activities or
Insurance
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
It shall be the policy of the City to make payroll deductions only for official
City- sponsored activities. The City shall not make deductions for non-City
sponsored organizations or employee recreation funds.
Payroll deductions for existing non-City-sponsored life insurance, which
currently are the only payroll deductions for non-City sponsored activities,
will be continued as a convenience for City employees.
Every July 1, the service charges to the insurance companies will be reviewed
and revised if necessary. The service charges will be billed each July 1 and
will be due in 30 days. Any charges paid after the due date will be deducted
from any distributions to the companies. Failure of companies to pay the
service charge may result in the elimination of payroll deductions for that
firm. The service charges are as follows:

CITY EMPLOYEES HOLDING ELECTIVE OFFICE
TITLE:   City Employees Holding Elective Office
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Background
At the municipal election on October 3, 1989, the voters of Albuquerque
approved Proposition No. 8, which added a new §3 to Article XI (now renumbered
as Article X) of the City Charter. Section 3 prohibits City employees from
holding an elective office of the State of New Mexico or any of its political
subdivisions. The effective date of the prohibition is January 1, 1993.
However, those City employees who held such elective offices as of October 3,
1989, were allowed to continue to serve in such elective offices and to
continue to be elected to the same office while serving as City employees.
Also, since the prohibition did not become effective until January 1, 1993, any
City employee who was elected to such an elective office after October 3, 1989,
but before January 1, 1993, was able to remain in elective office until January
1, 1993.
The effect was to create three classes of City employees:
1.   City employees who were employed by the City and were holding elective
office on October 3, 1989. These employees were to be allowed to continue to
hold elective office, so long as they are elected to the same elective office.
2.   City employees who were first elected and held office after October 3,
1989, but before January 1, 1993. These employees were permitted to remain in
office and City employment until January 1, 1993.
3.   City employees who did not hold any elective office on or after January 1,
1993.
As of the Effective Date of this Administrative Instruction No. 7-8 (2016), the
Human Resources Department is not aware of any current city employee who would
fall within the first two classes of employees described above.
Policy
Effective January 1, 1993, it is the policy of the City of Albuquerque that all
City employees are prohibited from holding an elective office of the State of
New Mexico or any of its political subdivisions while employees of the City.
The foregoing prohibition does not apply to an employee of the City of
Albuquerque who was employed by the City on October 3, 1989, and who at that
time held elective office of the State of New Mexico or any of its political
subdivisions. That employee may continue to hold that same elective office
while serving as a City employee.
REFERENCES:
City Charter Article X, §3 (adopted at Regular Municipal Election on October 3,
1989, as Proposition No. 8.)
City of Albuquerque Ordinances, § 3-1-21(B), Political Activity (recommended
reference on this topic)
City of Albuquerque Personnel Rules and Regulations, Section 311.3(B) –
Political Activities (recommended reference on this topic)

EMPLOYEE LEAVE PURCHASE PROGRAM
TITLE: City of Albuquerque – Employee Leave Purchase
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Human Resources
Purpose of Administrative Instruction:
The purpose of this Administrative Instruction is to outline the guidelines and
procedures for the purchase of additional leave by eligible City employees.
This program aims to provide employees with greater flexibility in managing
their work-life balance, while ensuring that City services continue to function
effectively and efficiently.
SCOPE:
This program applies to all full-time and permanent part-time City employees
who are eligible to purchase additional leave under the terms outlined herein.
Employees must adhere to the guidelines and procedures as specified in this
document.
ELIGIBILITY:
Employees are eligible to purchase additional leave if they meet the following
criteria:
• Must be a full-time or permanent part-time employee.
• Employees who have been placed on unpaid suspension in the previous year are
not eligible to participate in the leave purchase program.
LEAVE PURCHASE LIMITS:
• Full-time employees may purchase up to 40 hours of additional leave per
fiscal year; part-time employees may purchase up to 20 hours of additional
leave per fiscal year.
• Leave must be purchased in increments of 8 hours for full-time employees and
in increments of 4 hours for part-time employees.
• During initial and subsequent open enrollment, employees may purchase up to
100% of the purchase limit.
• Newly hired employees and existing employees purchasing leave after initial
and open enrollment, may purchase leave based on the following schedule:
   o Full-time:
      40 hours if purchased during the first quarter of the fiscal year.
      32 hours if purchased during the second quarter of the fiscal year.
      24 hours if purchased during the third quarter of the fiscal year.
      16 hours if purchased during the fourth quarter of the fiscal year.
   o Part-time:
      20 hours if purchased during the first quarter of the fiscal year.
      16 hours if purchased during the second quarter of the fiscal year.
      12 hours if purchased during the third quarter of the fiscal year.
      8 hours if purchased during the fourth quarter of the fiscal year
• Employees may not purchase leave in excess of vacation leave limits.
HOW TO PURCHASE LEAVE:
• All leave purchase requests are subject to approval by the employee’s
director, and departmental financial officer based on departmental needs and
operational coverage.
• Employees may only submit one purchase request per fiscal year.
• Employees shall provide the leave purchase requests to their departmental
payroll and human resources coordinators.
• The cost of purchased leave will be deducted in equal amounts from the
employee’s salary throughout the remainder of the fiscal year.
USAGE OF PURCHASED LEAVE:
• Purchased leave will be coded as Vacation Leave Buy (VCBUY) upon purchase for
tracking and reporting. Employees shall use the code Vacation Purchase Taken
(VPT) when submitting payroll after using the purchased leave.
• Employees should request to use leave in accordance with their departmental
policy.
• Purchased leave can be taken in conjunction with other types of leave (such
as vacation leave or sick leave), subject to supervisor approval.
• Supervisors must review the request and ensure there is sufficient leave
balance.
LEAVE BALANCE AT END OF ENROLLMENT PERIOD:
• If an employee has a remaining balance of purchased leave at the end of the
enrollment period, the cash value of the purchased leave balance shall be
refunded to the employee during the first full pay-period after the enrollment
period ends.
The amount refunded shall not exceed the amount actually deducted from the
employee’s pay during the enrollment cycle.
LEAVE BALANCE UPON SEPERATION:
• If an employee owes a remaining balance for leave taken, but not repaid to
the City, the employee shall be fully responsible for repaying the balance and
the full amount shall be deducted from the employee’s final paycheck.
• If an employee leaves City employment before the full purchased leave amount
is utilized, the balance of the leave purchase will be credited to them on
their final paycheck.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES:
• Transfers: If an employee transfers to another department, any unused leave
purchased under this program will be transferred to the new department and the
granting of any additional requested purchased leave will be up to the new
department.
• Promotions and Demotions: Employees who are promoted or demoted will have
purchased leave paid out at their rate of pay at the time the leave is taken.
• Usage with Other Types of Leave: Employees may use purchased leave in
conjunction with other types of approved leave. The purchase and usage of
additional leave does not alter and will not extend the eligibility for other
leave entitlements under relevant personnel rules and labor laws.
• FMLA: Employees who are actively on FMLA and have exhausted paid leave should
consult with their department director and the Employee Relations Division of
Human Resources to determine eligibility of purchasing leave.
RECORDKEEPING:
• Payroll, and the employee’s department will maintain records of all leave
purchases, including the employee's request form, repayment schedule, and any
adjustments to the leave balance.
• Employees are responsible for ensuring that they are aware of their remaining
leave balance and the status of their repayment.
PROGRAM REVIEW AND MODIFICATION:
• This leave purchase program is subject to periodic review and may be modified
or terminated at the discretion of the City.
• Employees will be notified in writing of any changes to the program’s terms
or conditions.
COMPLIANCE:
Employees must comply with all relevant laws, regulations, and employment
agreements concerning leave. Any violation of this policy may result in
disciplinary action, including the denial of future leave purchase requests.

AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT (ADA) GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE
TITLE:   Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Grievance Procedure
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Background:
Title II of the ADA prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability by
public entities in all services, programs and activities (including employment)
provided or made available to the public.
Disability means, with respect to an individual, a physical or mental
impairment that substantially limits one or more of the major life activities
(caring for one's self, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing,
speaking, breathing, learning, working, etc.) of such individual; a record of
such an impairment; or being regarded as having such an impairment.
The U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division, has adopted regulations
at 28 CFR Part 35, entitled “Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in
State and Local Government Services”. 28 CFR §35.107(b) provides that:
      "A public entity that employs 50 or more persons shall adopt and publish
grievance procedures providing for prompt and equitable resolution of
complaints alleging any action that would be prohibited by this part."
ADA GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE:
A.   POLICY
    The City of Albuquerque, in maintaining a policy of Equal Employment
Opportunity and equal access, will afford to all employees, applicants for
employment, and users of public services, programs and activities, the right to
file a complaint or grievance on any discriminatory action, procedure or
practice in selection, employment and access. However, this Grievance Procedure
only applies to employees employed by the City of Albuquerque or citizens
applying for advertised positions posted by the City of Albuquerque.
   The Human Resources Department, located in Old City Hall, shall be
responsible for investigation of all such complaints and grievances as it
relates to employment with the City of Albuquerque. The purpose of the
grievance procedure is to provide an avenue for the resolution of disability
discrimination complaints, verbally or written, equitably and in a timely
manner. The procedure shall be utilized only for complaints based on
discrimination or alleging noncompliance with the ADA. The grievance procedure
outlined in the City's Merit System Ordinance shall be used for grievable
issues not alleging discrimination based on disabilities covered under the ADA.
   Investigation of complaints regarding accessibility to City government
programs, services and activities, reasonable accommodation or discrimination
in employment, may be initiated by filing a charge with the Human Resources
Employee Relations Manager (Human Resources Manager), or his or her designee.
B.   PRE-INTAKE PROCEDURE
     When investigating claims of discrimination in employment practices other
than hiring, prior to accepting and investigating a complaint of
discrimination, the grievant will be encouraged by the Human Resources
Department to discuss the complaint with his or her supervisor or department
head to attempt to resolve the issues at the department level. If the grievant
does not receive a satisfactory resolution of the complaint at that level, he
or she may file a charge and initiate an investigation into the matter by
contacting the Human Resources Manager, or his or her designee.
C.   INTAKE PROCEDURE
     The following procedure will be used by the Human Resources Manager, or
his or her designee, in investigating and attempting to resolve ADA complaints:
   1. The grievant must notify the Human Resources Manager, or his or her
designee, of the grievant’s complaint either in person or in writing within 30
calendar days from the date the alleged discriminatory action took place. The
complaint shall include:
      a.   the name and phone number of grievant, and department of grievant,
if internal;
      b.   the date, description and/or location of alleged discriminatory act;
      c.   the name(s), if known, of person(s) responsible for alleged
discriminatory act; and
      d.   the nature of remedial action sought.
   2. The Human Resources Manager, or his or her designee, will meet with the
grievant to review and clarify the issues and explain the complaint procedure,
including the availability of alternative dispute resolution procedures.
   3. The complaint will result in a thorough investigation conducted by the
Human Resources Manager or his or her designee. The Human Resources Manager, or
his or her designee, will submit investigative findings and recommendations to
the Department Director for review and a final decision will be rendered within
ten (10) working days of the completion of the investigation. The Human
Resources Manager, or his or her designee, may recommend such interim relief as
may be appropriate.
D.   APPEAL PROCEDURE
   1.   If the response by the Human Resources Manager or his or her designee
does not satisfactorily resolve the issue, the grievant may appeal the decision
within ten (10) working days after the receipt of the response from the Human
Resources Director, or his or her designee.
   2.   Within ten (10) working days after the receipt of the appeal, the Human
Resources Manager, or his or her designee, will meet with the grievant to
discuss the complaint and possible resolutions. Within ten (10) working days
after the meeting, the Human Resources Manager, or his or her designee, will
respond in writing, and where appropriate, in a format accessible to the
grievant, with a final resolution to the complaint.
   3.   Anyone wishing to file a complaint alleging discrimination on the basis
of disability in the provision of services, activities, programs, and/or
benefits offered by the City of Albuquerque, should utilize the grievance and
appeal procedure outlined in the following link:
https://www.cabq.gov/humanrights/americans-with-disabilities-act-ada
E.   NONRETALIATION
   No individual, applicant for employment or user of public services, programs
or activities will be discriminated against, harassed, intimidated, retaliated
against or suffer reprisal as a result of filing a complaint or participating
in the investigation of a complaint by providing information, testimony or
assisting in the investigation in any way.
   Nothing in this section shall preclude any individual from filing a formal
charge with the appropriate local, state or federal civil rights enforcement
agency at any stage of the procedure.
   All written complaints received by the City of Albuquerque and responses
will be retained by the City of Albuquerque for three (3) years.
REFERENCES:
Americans with Disabilities Act Title II, 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.;
28 CFR Part 35, as amended and effective October 11, 2016 (81 FR 53203).

AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT (ADA) 1990
TITLE:   Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) 1990
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Background:
The ADA prohibits discrimination against people with disabilities in
employment, transportation, public accommodation, communications, and
governmental activities. The Act guarantees protection comparable to that
previously afforded other groups on the basis of race, color, sex, national
origin, age, and religion.
Policy:
The Administrative Instruction affirms the dedication of the City of
Albuquerque to honor the spirit and promote the purpose of the ADA as well as
to adhere to the letter of the Act.
Therefore:
   PART I
   The following clause shall appear on all printed material prepared for
public dissemination:
   The City of Albuquerque does not discriminate on the basis of race, color,
national origin, ancestry, sex, religion, age or disability in the provision of
services, programs, and activities.
   PART II
   The City of Albuquerque shall not discriminate on the basis of disability in
contracting for the purchase of goods and services. It may not directly or
through contractual or other arrangements, use criteria or methods of
administration that have the effect of subjecting qualified individuals with
disabilities to discrimination on the basis of their disability. Further, in
the selection of procurement contractors, the City shall not use criteria that
subject qualified individuals with disabilities to discrimination on the basis
of such disability.
   To comply with these provisions and to ensure that City contractors and
subcontractors also comply, the following provision shall be inserted in all
contracts to which the City of Albuquerque is a party:
   The contractor shall comply with all applicable provisions of the Americans
with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. §12101) and federal regulations
promulgated thereunder (28 C.F.R. Parts 35, 36 and 37).
   PART III
   The City of Albuquerque shall not administer a licensing or certification
program in a manner that subjects qualified individuals with disabilities to
discrimination on the basis of disability, nor will it support the programs or
activities of licensees or certified entities that subject qualified
individuals with disabilities to discrimination on the basis of disability.
REFERENCES:   Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. §12101) and
federal regulations promulgated thereunder (28 C.F.R. Parts 35, 36 and 37)

ADA COMPLIANCE FOR PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS, PROMOTIONS AND BROCHURES
TITLE:   ADA Compliance for Public Service Announcements, Promotions and
Brochures
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Mayor’s Office
The Americans with Disabilities Act requires the City of Albuquerque to ensure
that its communications with persons with disabilities are as effective as
communications with others.
All public service announcements and promotions produced by or for the City of
Albuquerque which are prepared for television shall be open or closed
captioned.
All such announcements which are prepared for radio broadcast or to appear in
print shall say that the announcement is also available in alternate formats,
upon request.
All such public service announcements and promotions produced by or for the
City shall contain a statement that the City of Albuquerque is relay-friendly
and will accept calls from constituents calling through text or video relay.
All public service announcements and advertisements of City-sponsored programs,
services, and events previously produced must be modified as set forth above
before they may be broadcast or distributed. Existing brochures shall be
withdrawn and either reprinted or modified (for example, by adding the required
information using stick-on labels or inked stamps).

RETURN TO TEMPORARILY RESTRICTED DUTY AND PERMANENTLY MODIFIED WORK ASSIGNMENTS
RESULTING FROM WORK RELATED INJURY
TITLE:   Return to Temporarily Restricted duty and Permanently Modified Work
Assignments resulting from work related injury.
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
It is the policy of the city of Albuquerque to fully utilize its employees and
to maintain a productive, equitable and positive work environment. To
accomplish this goal and to comply with the Workers' Compensation Act this
policy encourages the return of employees injured on the job to productive work
as soon as medically appropriate after the injury. The Policy also includes
provisions for providing appropriate assignments for those employees who have
permanent work restrictions as the result of a work related injury or illness.
Participation in the Program is required by all employees returning from a work
related injury or illness. All Departments will participate and provide full
cooperation with the Risk Management Division of the Department of Finance and
Administrative Services in the effort to identify and develop appropriate
assignments and to place these returning employees in them. If an appropriate
assignment is unavailable in the employee’s home department temporary or
permanent reassignment to another department may be considered. In the case of
a Temporary Restricted Duty reassignment the employee’s payroll status will
remain with the home department.
The Risk Management Division shall administer the program, which will include
the following components.
   1.   Temporary Restricted Duty
This component is intended to return an employee who has sustained an on- the-
job injury to a productive level of work in preparation for return to his/her
pre-injury position. The maximum duration of temporary restrictions shall be 45
calendar days. Extension of restricted duty will be determined by Risk
Management based on medical information from the authorized provider.
The employee's department in collaboration with Risk Management shall be
responsible for identifying Restricted Duty assignments. The Restricted Duty
assignment will be temporary in nature to assist the employee and the operating
department during the employee's temporary inability to return to normal duty.
   2.   Permanently Restricted – Modified Duty
When the Employee Health Center or other authorized medical provider places
permanent restrictions, the Risk Management Division, in conjunction with the
Human Resources Department, the department, and employee will work to identify
modification of the current job or permanent reassignment to a position for
which the employee is qualified. If no such modification or reassignment is
identified, the appropriate leave and physical layoff positions in the
Personnel Rules and Regulations shall be utilized.
REFERENCES: New Mexico Workers' Compensation Act (52-1-25.1 and 52-1-50.1 NMSA
1978)

HARASSMENT/SEXUAL HARASSMENT POLICY (2020)
TITLE:   Harassment/Sexual Harassment Policy (Revised April ______, 2020)
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
The City of Albuquerque is committed to providing a work environment free from
all forms of harassment. Harassment in the workplace includes, but is not
limited to, sexual harassment. Harassment is any verbal or physical conduct
including displaying or forwarding any visual material, that denigrates or
shows hostility or aversion toward an individual because of his or her race,
color, religion, gender, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, medical
condition, sexual orientation or gender identity, or hair types, textures, and
styles commonly associated with race, gender, or religion; that has the purpose
or effect of creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment;
and has the purpose or effect of unreasonably interfering with an individual's
work performance; or otherwise adversely affects an individual's employment
opportunities or ability to obtain public services. Harassment based on any of
the foregoing statuses is a form of discrimination which is unlawful under
local, state and federal civil rights laws. This policy applies to all forms of
harassment, including sexual harassment.
The City of Albuquerque, as a public employer and a provider of services, WILL
NOT TOLERATE OR CONDONE HARASSMENT IN ANY FORM from any employee, regardless of
his or her employment status, nor from a provider of services who is under
contract with the City. All employees, supervisors and managers are responsible
for maintaining a work environment free of any form of harassment, and will be
held fully accountable in complying with this policy and taking appropriate
measures to ensure that such conduct does not occur. Applicants for employment
are entitled to employment consideration without being subjected to sexual or
other forms of harassment. Any employee found to have engaged in prohibited
harassment will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including
termination.
This policy supersedes all previous policies with the City of Albuquerque
addressing harassment including sexual harassment and is made in accordance
with City Council Bill No. C/S R-158, regarding sexual harassment. Departments
may reinforce this policy with an additional departmental policy consistent
with this policy and with the signature of the Chief Administrative Officer.
MANDATORY TRAINING
Training on harassment/sexual harassment is mandatory each year for all City of
Albuquerque employees and is essential for our organization to ensure employees
experience a safe, fair and healthy work environment. The City of Albuquerque
will make training available to all employees on an annual basis. Initial
training will be provided in person and thereafter annually, utilizing the
City's on-line training.
DEFINITION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, in conjunction with the Equal
Employment Opportunity Commission's guidelines for defining sexual harassment
prohibits unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and verbal
expression or physical conduct of a sexual nature.
Sexual harassment is defined as any unwelcome sexual advances, requests for
sexually motivated physical contact, or other verbal expression or physical
conduct or communication of a sexual nature when:
   1.   Submission to that conduct or communication is made a term or
condition, either explicitly or implicitly, of obtaining employment or public
services; or
   2.   Submission to or rejection of that conduct or communication by an
individual is used as a factor in decisions affecting that individual's
employment or obtaining public services; or
   3.   That conduct or communication has the purpose or effect of unreasonably
interfering with an individual's employment or obtaining public services or
creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive environment in which to work or
obtain services.
The following criteria will be looked at to determine if sexual harassment
exists:
   1. The frequency of the conduct.
   2. The severity of the conduct.
   3. Whether the conduct unreasonably interferes with work performance.
Unwelcome verbal or physical conduct, even if it does not rise to the level of
sexual harassment, may be a violation of City policies and is prohibited.
Examples of Sexual Harassment
The following are examples of conduct which may be considered sexual
harassment. Conduct which is not on this list can also be sexual harassment if
it meets the above definition.
A.   Physical Assaults of a Sexual Nature, such as:
   1.   Rape, sexual battery, molestation, or attempts to commit the foregoing;
   2. Intentional physical conduct, such as touching, pinching, patting,
grabbing, brushing against another employee's body, or poking another
employee's body that is sexual in nature.
B. Unwanted Sexual Advances, Propositions, or Other Unwanted Sexual Comments,
such as:
   1.   Threatening adverse actions in order to have a sexual favor performed;
   2.   Suggesting a desire for sexual relations or physical contact;
   3.   Propositions of sexual nature;
   4.   Continued requests for dates after being informed that such requests
are unwelcome;
   5.   Use of any offensive or demeaning terms which have a sexual connotation
such as:
      a.   Verbal abuses of a sexual nature;
      b.   Graphic commentaries about a person's body;
      c.   Use of sexually degrading words to describe a person;
      d.   Telling jokes or making remarks of a sexual nature to, or in the
presence of, persons who find such jokes or remarks offensive.
      e.   Making offensive remarks about someone's sexual orientation or
gender identity.
   6.    Whistling or calling another in such a manner as to attract unwelcome
attention to another person, i.e. "wolf whistling" "cat calls";
   7.   Initiating unwanted discussion of one's personal sex life.
   8.   Non-verbal gestures such as:
      a.   Looking or staring at a person up and down;
      b.   Winking, throwing kisses, or licking lips;
      c.   Making sexual gestures with hands or through body movements.
C.   Sexual Displays or Publications Anywhere in Workplace by Employees, such
as:
   1.   Displaying pictures, posters, calendars, graffiti, cartoons, objects,
promotional materials, reading materials, or other materials that are sexually
suggestive, sexually demeaning or pornographic, or bringing into the work
environment or possessing any such material to read, display, or view at work;
or
   2.   Reading or otherwise publicizing in the work environment materials that
are in any way sexually revealing, sexually suggestive, sexually demeaning, or
pornographic.
DEFINITION OF HARASSMENT
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, in conjunction with the Equal
Employment Opportunity Commission's guidelines defines harassment as unwelcome
conduct that is based on membership in a protected class.
Harassment is unlawful and prohibited where:
   l.   Enduring the offensive conduct becomes a condition of continued
employment or a condition of obtaining employment or public services, or
   2.   The conduct is severe or pervasive enough to create a work environment
that a reasonable person would consider intimidating, hostile, or abusive.
   Examples Which May Constitute Harassment
   1.   Epithets;
   2.   Slurs;
   3.   Negative stereotyping;
   4.   Threats;
   5.   Hostile acts;
   6.   Ridicule or mockery because of a person's protected class;
   7.   Denigrating or hostile written or graphic material posted or circulated
in the workplace.
Retaliation for Harassment/Sexual Harassment Complaints is prohibited, such as:
   1.   Disciplining, providing inaccurate work information to, or refusing to
cooperate or discuss work- related matters with any employee because that
employee has complained about or resisted harassment, discrimination, or
retaliation; and
   2.   Intentionally pressuring, falsely denying, lying about or otherwise
covering up or attempting to cover up any conduct that meets the definition of
harassment, as provided above.
The above is not to be construed as an all-inclusive list of prohibited acts
under this Policy.
Any form of harassment, including sexual harassment, is prohibited, hurts other
employees, and contributes to a general negative atmosphere in which all
employees suffer the consequences. Any of the prohibited conduct described
here, if found to constitute harassment/sexual harassment, has no legitimate
business purposes. Accordingly, the employee who engages in harassment/sexual
harassment should be and will be made to bear the full responsibility for such
conduct.
REPORTING HARASSMENT
Employees and applicants for employment who believe they have been subjected to
sexual or other harassment are encouraged to tell the person responsible for
the behavior that his or her actions are offensive and unwelcome. Employees and
applicants for employment have an obligation to report the matter as soon as
possible to a supervisor, the Department Director, or to the Human Resources
Director. An employee may also exercise his/her rights to pursue an action
through any local (City of Albuquerque, Human Rights Office), state (Human
Rights Commission of New Mexico) or federal (Equal Employment Opportunity
Commission) regulatory agency responsible for enforcement of anti-
discrimination laws. This policy does not extend the time limits to file any
discrimination action.
ANY DEPARTMENT DIRECTOR, MANAGER OR SUPERVISOR WHO OBSERVES OR HAS KNOWLEDGE OF
HARASSMENT, MUST IMMEDIATELY BRING THE MATTER TO THE ATTENTION OF THE
DEPARTMENT DIRECTOR OR THE HUMAN RESOURCES DIRECTOR. FAILURE TO DO SO MAY
RESULT IN DISCIPLINARY ACTION.
The City will investigate all reports of alleged harassment. To the extent
possible, the City will keep the information confidential, consistent with its
obligation to provide a prompt, impartial, and thorough investigation. If the
City determines that harassment or other violations of City policy have
occurred or that counseling, training, disciplinary measures or termination are
appropriate, it will take appropriate measures to correct the problem.
No employee will be retaliated against in any way for reporting in good faith
any allegations of harassment or assisting, testifying, or participating in an
investigation. Such retaliation in and of itself may result in disciplinary
action, up to and including termination.
All employees are required to cooperate with any investigation undertaken by
the City in response to an allegation of harassment. Department Directors are
responsible for assuring cooperation with investigations. Refusal to cooperate
in an investigation may result in disciplinary action, up to an including
termination.
Each Department Director shall adhere to and enforce the procedures established
by the City of Albuquerque which provides work sites free of harassment
including sexual harassment, so that instances of harassment including sexual
harassment will be detected soon after their occurrences, and to provide for
prompt resolution of complaints within the department.
ALL EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE HAVE THE RIGHT TO AN EQUITABLE WORKING
ENVIRONMENT.
The Human Resources Department is available to discuss incidents, investigate
whether the conduct appears to be harassment, including sexual harassment, and
explain the options for dealing with harassment. Any activity that may be
harassment should be reported immediately to determine if any corrective action
should be taken.
For more information contact the Human Resources Department at 768-3700.
Effective Date
This Administration Instruction is effective immediately.
REFERENCES: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Age Discrimination
in Employment Act of 1967, (ADEA), and the Americans with Disabilities Act of
1990, (ADA), Equal Employment Opportunity Commission guidelines, the New Mexico
Human Rights Act, 28-1-1, et. al.

POLITICAL ACTIVITIES OF CITY EMPLOYEES AND USE OF CITY PROPERTY FOR POLITICAL
ACTIVITIES
TITLE:   Political Activities of City Employees and Use of City Property for
Political Activities
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   City Clerk
Every city employee has the right to support the Candidates and ballot
questions of their choice; however, the credibility and the integrity of our
service demands that City employees obey the laws and regulations governing
political activity and prevent the appearance of governmental involvement or
bias.
1. Definitions
Candidate or Candidates shall mean a person who is a prospective candidate or a
person who has filed as a candidate or their representative or anyone promoting
or opposing any ballot proposition or the election of anyone seeking public
office in any election.
Public Meeting Space means a City owned or leased area inside or outside of a
structure that is used as a meeting area for general public on an ongoing basis
throughout the year and shall not include meeting rooms and conference rooms or
other areas used only for government business.
2. Conduct of City Employees
The following activities are permitted or prohibited for all City employees
with respect to all elections.
   A. Activities Permitted - Any City employee may:
   1) Register and vote;
   2) Express an opinion about Candidates or on issues;
   3) Assist in voter registration drives;
   4) Display political pictures, stickers or posters in homes or on private
vehicles;
   5) Become politically active in connection with any question or issue on the
ballot;
   6) Attend a political rally, fund raising function or other political
gathering; or
   7) Participate in the following activities while not on duty.
      a. Sign nominating petitions;
      b. Make voluntary contributions to Candidates or issues committees; or
      c. Wear political buttons or badges while not on duty or in City uniform.
   B. Activities Prohibited - No City Employee Shall:
   1) Become a Candidate for any elective City office;
   2) Actively campaign for or against a Candidate for any elective office
while on duty or represent a Candidate while on duty. Volunteers assisting in
City functions under the supervision or direction of City employees shall not
campaign for a Candidate while performing such duties for the City;
   3) Receive, disburse or account for assessments, contributions or other
funds for any Candidate;
   4) Receive or offer to receive any money, gratuity or benefit from any
candidate;
   5) Wear on one's person political badges or buttons while on duty or while
in a City uniform at any time;
   6) Take either a position for or against any Candidate for elective office
while representing either that such position is an official City position on
such Candidate or that such position is taken in one's official capacity as a
City employee;
   7) Circulate nominating petitions within or on City property while on duty,
at the place of one's employment or at any time or any place while in City
Uniform;
   8) Serve as an election judge or clerk in a City election;
   9) Use any City-owned properly, equipment, supplies, vehicles or space
either to campaign for or against a Candidate.
   10) Display or distribute any political stickers, posters or materials on or
from City-owned vehicles or City property;
   11) Display or distribute any political stickers, posters or material for or
against any Candidate while on duty or at the City employee's work place, other
than bumper stickers displayed on the employee's private vehicle, including
vehicles parked in City owned parking lots; or
   12) Use the employee's position or status to influence the support of other
City employees or City officials for or against any Candidate or issue.
   C. Hatch Act - Any City employee whose principal employment is in connection
with an activity which is financed in whole or part by loans or grants made by
the United States or a Federal agency is subject to the provisions of the Hatch
Act in addition to the prohibited activities set forth in this memorandum. Each
City Employee is responsible for determining if Hatch Act prohibitions apply to
his or her employment with the City.
3. Facility Tours.
City employees who are authorized to conduct tours of City facilities may guide
Candidates through City facilities provided that such employees do not campaign
for or against any Candidate while conducting such tour. Tours shall not
disrupt or otherwise interfere with ongoing City programs, activities, or
meals.
4. Public Meetings.
Candidates may attend meetings of advisory councils or other similar
organizations that are authorized by the City to conduct activities at a City
facility as well all City boards and commissions. Candidates may be introduced
to the public at the meetings of such organizations. Candidates shall be
entitled to make public comment on agenda items that are open for public
comment.
5. Petition Signatures.
Candidates may ask members of the public at City facilities to sign nomination
or other petitions to qualify to be on the ballot. Candidates shall not solicit
such signatures from City employees during the employee's working hours.
Solicitation of petition signatures shall not interrupt ongoing City
activities, programs, or meals and shall not block the orderly flow of traffic.
6. Campaign Materials.
Candidates may wear campaign logos, clothing, buttons, name tags and other
similar campaign materials while at City facilities, as may members of the
public, whether or not they are actively campaigning. City employees and
volunteer staff under the direction of City employees shall not wear, carry or
distribute such campaign materials while on duty.
7. Use of City Property.
City Property may be used for political activities only through compliance with
the following:
   A. Candidates shall be allowed access to Public Meeting Space for campaign
events through written request at least two weeks prior to the planned event.
The manager of the facility the Candidate designates for use shall make the
determination of availability of the requested facility. Any previously
scheduled use of the location or conflicting on going uses for a City-sponsored
activity shall take precedence over the request. Campaign events consist of the
use of part or all of a facility for a meeting or program by the Candidate and
do not include activities described previously in this administrative
instruction. In the event more than one Candidate requests use of Public
Meeting Space on City property for the same day and time, the request first
received shall be allowed if the Public Meeting Space is otherwise available.
No City equipment, materials, or labor of City employees on duty shall be
provided to Candidates related to their use of a Public Meeting Space.
   B. A Candidate may distribute campaign materials, greet employees and
solicit contributions and petition signatures at entrances or exits to City
property as well as at any place open to the general public but only in a
manner that does not disrupt the orderly flow of traffic or interrupt City
activities, programs or meals.
   C. Campaign materials may be placed in a manner and at locations as
designated by the manager of the City facility. The manager shall provide
locations accessible to the public. The manager shall be entitled to limit
space available for each Candidate in order that all Candidates may have space
for their materials and to limit the number of locations for such materials to
ensure the public safety.
   D. Candidates and their representatives shall not contact City employees at
their work sites while the City employee is on duty other than to make
arrangements for the use of City facilities as allowed in this administrative
instruction.
REFERENCES:   Hatch Act

CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE SUBSTANCE ABUSE REVIEW AND HEARINGS PROCESS - RULES OF
PROCEDURE FOR CONTESTING THE DESIGNATION OF POSITIONS AS "SAFETY SENSITIVE"
TITLE:   City of Albuquerque Substance Abuse Review and Hearings Process -
Rules of Procedure for Contesting the Designation of Positions as “Safety
Sensitive”
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1. Statement of Purpose. The purpose of these rules is to implement and clarify
the City of Albuquerque (hereinafter the “City”) policies regarding the
designation of certain positions as “safety sensitive” for purposes of
substance abuse and alcohol and drug testing, as required by Section 2(B) of
Resolution R-237 of the City Council for the City of Albuquerque, and to
establish fair and expeditious procedures for employees to contest the
designation of their positions as “safety sensitive” as required by said
Resolution.
2. Authority. These rules are enacted pursuant to powers stated in Section 2(B)
of R-237.
3. List of “Safety-Sensitive” Positions. The City Human Resources Department
shall promulgate and cause to be circulated to each City Department a list of
all “safety-sensitive” positions within City government.
4. Notification of Employees. The Human Resources Department shall notify each
“safety-sensitive” employee of such designation. Such notification shall be in
writing, and shall state that the employee’s position has been designated as
“safety sensitive”, that the employee’s Department has been notified of such
designation, and shall advise each affected employee of their right to contest
such designation. Employees newly hired or transferred into a “safety-
sensitive” position shall be promptly notified of such status by the Director
of the Human Resources Department.
5. Employee’s Notice of Protest. An employee whose position has been designated
as “safety sensitive” may contest such action by submitting a notice of protest
to the Director of the Human Resources Department within thirty (30) calendar
days of his or her notification that his/her position has been designated as
“safety sensitive”. The notice of protest shall state:
   a.   The employee’s name;
   b.   Social security number;
   c.   Job classification, or other information identifying the employee’s
position; and
   d.   The reasons for the employee’s claim that his or her position is not
“safety sensitive”, including information relating to the employee’s daily job
duties together with any supporting documents.
   The rights of protest set forth in these rules shall not apply or be
available to employees whose positions are defined in United States Department
of Transportation Regulations as “safety sensitive” nor to the designation of
“safety-sensitive” positions held by police officers, corrections officers or
firefighters.
6. Department Inquiry. The Director of the Human Resources Department shall
review the information submitted by the employee, along with any information
provided by the employee’s department, and shall notify the employee in writing
of a determination within fifteen (15) calendar days of the employee’s
submission. The Director of the Human Resources Department shall simultaneously
forward the employee’s claim and the notification of determination to the City
Hearing Officer.
7. Notification of Hearings on Protesting a Safety-Sensitive Designation. If
the determination of the Director of the Human Resources Department is to deny
the employee’s claim, the Hearing Officer shall set the employee’s hearing as
expeditiously as possible, and shall notify the employee, or his or her
representative, the employee’s Department Director, and the Director of the
Human Resources Department of the date, time and place of the hearing. In the
event the employee fails to appear at the time and place specified, the
employee may reapply for a hearing within ten (10) calendar days of the hearing
date by submitting another notice of protest to the Director of the Human
Resources Department, as provided in Section 5, above, and, in addition, the
employee shall state the reasons for his or her failure to appear at the
earlier scheduled hearing. It shall be within the Hearing Officer’s discretion
to grant or deny the employee’s renewed request for a hearing.
8. Conduct of Hearings. In all hearings conducted under this regulation, the
employee shall have the right to be represented by a person of his or her
choosing. The proceedings shall be recorded either by means of stenographic or
audio tape by a certified reporter or monitor. Neither the rules of evidence
nor of civil procedure shall apply, but, the employee and the Director of the
Human Resources Department, shall each be accorded a full and fair opportunity
to examine witnesses and to present any relevant evidence to the Hearing
Officer so as to establish a complete record.
9. Standard of Review. In deciding whether a position should be classified as
“safety sensitive”, the Hearing Officer shall apply the criteria set forth in
Personnel Rules & Regulations Section 1100, and shall apply the designation, at
a minimum, to employees with access to Controlled Substances and to those
employees who are required by their job descriptions to hold a commercial
driver’s license, and who actually drive commercial vehicles. In determining
whether the designation should apply to additional positions, the Hearing
Officer shall consider the extent to which the job responsibilities impact upon
the safety of the public, the extent to which the job responsibilities expose
the employee or co-workers to hazardous conditions, and the extent to which the
job requires responsibility for the safety of others.
10. The Hearing Officer’s Decision. The Hearing Officer shall issue a written
decision within thirty (30) calendar days of the completion of the hearing to
either uphold or to reverse the determination of the Director of the Human
Resources Department. The Hearing Officer shall state the reason for its
decision, and shall transmit its decision to the Chief Administrative Officer.
Copies of the Hearing Officer’s decision also shall be provided to the
employee, or his or her representative, the employee’s Department Director, and
to the Director of the Human Resources Department. The Hearing Officer’s
decision on the matter shall be the City’s final administrative step, and shall
not be subject to further review or appeal.
REFERENCES:   Personnel Rules and Regulations Section 1100 Substance Abuse Part
I
