INCENTIVE PROGRAM FOR POSITIONS WHICH ARE
"DIFFICULT TO RECRUIT" (Revised January 2023)
TITLE: Incentive Program for Positions which are "Difficult to Recruit"
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Human Resources
The City has established an incentive program to help address the challenges
faced by the City in recruiting highly qualified, performance-orientated
candidates for specific classifications that have been identified as "difficult
to recruit." "Difficult to recruit" classifications are defined as:
   a)   Positions which are highly competitive in the labor market due to
specialized skills and/or certifications, or
   b)   Positions influenced due to unusual market demands, or
   c)   Positions that experience high turnover making it difficult to maintain
adequate staffing levels to provide critical City services.
All recruitment incentives, and the classifications to which they will apply,
must be approved in advance in writing by the Human Resources Director as
delegated by the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) prior to discussion with
any candidate or recruiting effort proposing to offer one or more of these
incentives. Recruitment incentives may be discontinued at any time at the sole
discretion of the CAO. The CAO will exercise final authority regarding the
implementation and administration of this incentive program.
The following recruitment incentives may be offered in appropriate
circumstances with the written concurrence of the CAO:
HIRING INCENTIVE:
The Addendum to this Administrative Instruction will provide a comprehensive
list of positions eligible for a hiring incentive, effective dates, and amount
of the applicable incentive. In addition, each job title includes an exclusion
for individuals who have been previously employed by the City. Individuals who
are rehired within the exclusion timeframe are not eligible for the Hiring
Incentive.
For the purposes of this Administrative Instruction, successful completion of
any period of time required for the payment of a hiring incentive must be
evidenced by the completion of a Performance Evaluation showing that
performance expectations were met.
SICK LEAVE TRANSFER:
Unclassified employees who leave another employer to accept a "difficult to
recruit" position in the City may be credited with up to 96.2 hours (bi-weekly
accrual of 3.7 hours for 26 pay periods) of sick leave. The actual amount to be
credited may not exceed the maximum of 96.2 hours and shall be based on
documentation provided by the employee indicating the sick leave balance in
effect, net of any "payout" or "conversion" of sick leave, at the date of the
employee's termination of their previous employment. The sick leave shall be
credited to the employee's City sick leave bank after the completion of one
full pay period.
Police Officer Laterals: Each lateral hire, upon completion of the officer's
academy training, shall be credited with forty ( 40) hours of sick leave.
VACATION ACCRUAL RATE:
Unclassified employees hired into "difficult to recruit" positions in the City
will accrue vacation leave at the rate applicable to employees with five years
of experience with the City provided they have at least five years of
experience with one or more previous employers in a position comparable to the
one into which they are hired. The enhanced accrual rate shall go into effect
at the completion of six (6) months of employment. The enhanced accrual rate
will remain in effect until the employee reaches ten (10) years of service with
the City.
Police Officer Laterals: Upon completion of the officer's academy training, and
for each year of prior service recognized by the Albuquerque Police Department
for purposes of lateral credit, each lateral hire shall be credited with
vacation leave as follows:
   40 hours for 2-4 years
   70 hours for 5-14 years
   100 hours for 15 or more years
FINDER'S FEE:
Any City employee who has referred a candidate not currently or previously
employed by the City within the last eight (8) years for employment into a
"difficult to recruit" classification may be paid a finder's fee of up to
$2500.
   a)   Incentive payments for difficult to fill positions will be made only
after the referred candidate is hired and successfully completes six months of
City service with a "meets expectations" or higher evaluation rating and may be
paid a finder's fee of up to $500, or
   b)   Incentive payments for police officer cadets and laterals will be made
once the referred candidate is hired and successfully completes their OJT with
a "meets expectations" or higher evaluation rating and may be paid a finder's
fee of up to $2500, or
   c)   Incentive payments for Albuquerque Fire Rescue 3/Class will be made
only after the referred candidate is hired and successfully completes their
probationary year with a "meets expectations" or higher evaluation rating and
may be paid a finder's fee of up to $1000.
The following conditions apply for a City employee to be eligible to receive
the finder's fee:
   •   The referring employee must be identified on the candidate's original
application for employment; and
   •   The candidate cannot have been a City employee within the last eight (8)
years.
Executives, Directors, Deputy Directors, Associate Directors, Assistant
Directors, Human Resources, and leadership positions with oversight over a
finder's fee eligible job are excluded from receiving a Finder's Fee. No
finder's fee will be payable with respect to a candidate who has retired from
the PERA or ERA system.
The determination of whether a finder's fee is to be paid and the amount to be
paid will be made by the Director of the department that hired the candidate.
Any finder's fee may be subject to applicable collective bargaining agreement
(s).
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE:
Candidates for "difficult to recruit" classifications may be eligible for a
relocation assistance of up to $5000. Relocation assistance shall be included
with the applicable individual's offer letter and is payable the pay period
following completion of the employee's first full pay period worked.
CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO INCENTIVE PROGRAM:
Any incentive to be paid under the terms of this program shall be payable from
the existing fiscal year budget of the Department proposing to offer the
incentive. No budget line item shall be proposed or approved to accommodate
this incentive program.
All payments to candidates or employees under this Administrative Instruction
shall be treated as taxable income on the date paid, and subject to all normal
withholdings and deductions.
Department Directors may request additions and deletions from the list of
recruitment incentives by emailing CentralHR@CABQ.gov.

AFR PARAMEDIC NEW HIRE SUPPLEMENT (Aug. 2020)
TITLE: Incentive Program for Paramedic New Hires with Albuquerque Fire Rescue
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Albuquerque Fire Rescue
Definitions:
A new hire is a person who is offered and accepted a position with AFR and who
possesses all of the qualifications and certifications listed in the job
posting. Each individual must complete the traditional cadet program.
Individuals with NM State or National Registry Emergency Medical Technician
(EMT) license at the basic level or higher are preferred.
COMPLETE INCENTIVE PACKAGE FOR PARAMEDIC NEW HIRES:
   HIRING BONUS:
   A hiring bonus of $15,000 shall be offered to a new hire with an EMT-
Paramedic license only, payable as follows: $5,000 at the successful completion
of the first two weeks of the AFR Training Academy, $5,000 at the successful
completion of the AFR Training Academy and the remaining $5,000 payable
following the successful completion of the one-year probationary period.
   Training Program Duration:
   All AFR new hires must complete an eighteen (18) week Training Academy.
While in the Academy, all members will be assigned to a forty (40) hour work
week. Following completion of the Training Academy, all members shall be
assigned to a fifty-six (56) hour work week and subject to Department policies
regarding overtime.
   CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO INCENTIVE PROGRAM:
   The incentives offered under this program shall be delineated in a written
agreement signed by the candidate, the Department director, and the CAO, in
advance of, or concurrently with, the Recommendation of Hire.
   EFFECTIVE DATE; TRANSITION RULE; EXCEPTIONS:
   This Administrative Instruction is effective the date the document is signed
by the CAO and valid until December 31, 2021. This Administrative Instruction
will apply only to prospective City employees for the purpose of new hires for
the Albuquerque Fire Rescue who possess an EMT Paramedic license. Any person to
whom an offer of employment has been made on or before the effective date of
this Administrative Instruction, as revised, is not eligible for any hiring
incentive under this program. Individuals previously employed by Albuquerque
Fire Rescue are not eligible to participate in the Incentive Program for
Paramedic New Hires.
REFERENCES: AI Number 7-44 (Incentive Programs for Positions which are
"Difficult to Recruit" 2016)

TRANSIT MOTORCOACH OPERATOR SUPPLEMENT (2021)
TITLE: Incentive Program for Motorcoach Operators with the Transit Department
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Transit Department
BACKGROUND:
As result of high turnover of the Motorcoach Operator position within The
Transit Department, the department has been approved to utilize a recruitment
incentive (i.e. finder's fee) and hiring bonus initiative for this position.
DEFINITIONS:
A new hire is a person who accepts a Motorcoach Operator position with the
Transit Department and who possesses the minimum education, experience, and
additional requirements as listed in the job posting. A transfer is a current
City employee who accepts a Motorcoach Operator position with the Transit
Depaitment and who possesses the minimum education, experience, and additional
requirements as listed in the job posting.
CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO INCENTIVE PROGRAMS:
The incentives offered under this Administrative Instruction shall be
delineated in a written agreement signed by the candidate, the Department
Director and the CAO, in advance of or concurrently with the Recommendation for
Hire. Transfers will be eligible for the hiring bonus as follows: Transfers
that have not completed probation will be considered a new hire; Transfers that
have completed probation will be eligible for a hiring bonus as outlined below.
HIRING BONUS:
Motorcoach Operators (New Hires):
A maximum incentive of $1,000 will be offered, payable as follows:
   •   At completion of probation - $250.00
   •   At nine (9) months of employment - $250.00
   •   At one (1) year of employment - $500.00
Motorcoach Operators (Transfers - Probation Completed):
A maximum incentive of $500.00 will be offered, payable as follows:
   •   At one (1) year of employment with Transit - $500.00
FINDER'S FEE:
Motorcoach Operator:
A maximum incentive of $100 will be offered as outlined and payable as follows:
Any City employee that has completed probation who has referred a candidate not
currently or previously employed by the City for employment into a "difficult
to recruit" classification will be paid a finder's fee of up to $100. Incentive
payments for such referrals will be made only after the referred candidate is
hired and successfully completes their respective probationary period with a
"meets expectations" or higher evaluation rating. The following conditions
apply for a City employee to be eligible to receive the finder's fee:
   •   The referring employee must be identified in the candidate's interview
for employment; and
   •   The candidate cannot have been a City employee within the last eight (8)
years .
No employee whose regular job duties include recruiting, hiring or training of
new employees will be eligible for the finder's fee. Finder's fees will be
limited to three (3) per calendar year per employee. No finder's fee will be
payable with respect to a candidate who has retired from the PERA or ERA
system. The determination of whether a finder's fee is to be paid, will be made
by the Transit Department Director.
EFFECTIVE DATE & TRANSITION RULE:
This Administrative Instruction is effective the date the document is signed by
the CAO and valid until December 31, 2022. This Administrative Instruction will
apply only to prospective City employees for the purpose of Motorcoach
Operators in the Department of Transit. Any person to whom an offer of
employment has been made on or before the effective date of this Administrative
Instruction, is not eligible for any hiring or finder's fee incentive under
this program. Individuals previously employed by the City of Albuquerque
Transit Department, may be able to participate in the Incentive Program for New
Hires contingent upon the Department Director's approval, which will be
reviewed on a case by case basis. All payments to candidates or employees under
this Administrative Instruction shall be treated as taxable income on the date
paid, and subject to all normal withholdings and deductions.
All other hiring processes and procedures are in effect.

TEMPORARY UPGRADES FOR EMPLOYEES OTHER THAN SWORN POLICE AND FIRE
TITLE: Temporary Upgrades for Employees other than Sworn Police and Fire
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Temporary upgrades will be permitted in accordance with the following
requirements:
A. Upgrades for 10 working days or less.
   1. Upgrades of 10 working days or less will be handled by the individual
departments based on short-term critical business needs.
   2. Employees upgraded under this section will automatically cease performing
the duties of the upgraded position at the conclusion of the need for the
temporary upgrade or upon expiration of the 10 working days, whichever occurs
first.
   3. If an employee is required to serve in an upgraded position for more than
10 working days, the department will be required to comply with section B. of
this policy.
B. Upgrades for more than 10 working days.
   1. Human Resources Department must approve upgrades for more than 10 working
days. The employee to be upgraded must possess the minimum qualifications for
the upgraded position, as specified in the job description of the upgraded
position. The department requesting the temporary upgrade under this section
will provide documentation of the qualifications of the employee to be upgraded
prior to an employee being placed in the upgraded position.
   2. In recommending employees for upgrade, departments are required to comply
with the provisions of any applicable collective bargaining agreement in
upgrading employees, including rotation of upgrades among qualified employees.
   3.    Departments may provide the Human Resources Department a list of
employees eligible to be upgraded for the position to be filled with
documentation of their qualifications. The Human Resources Department will
review the qualifications of each employee whose name is provided. The
department seeking to upgrade will be able to rotate employees to the upgraded
position without submitting the names again to the Human Resources Department.
C. Upgraded employees will be required to perform all of the duties of the
upgraded position as well as the duties of their regular position.
D. Only fully qualified individuals will be upgraded. An employee who is
upgraded will be paid in accordance with the respective collective bargaining
agreement for the time served in an upgraded capacity. E and I series employees
will receive compensation as approved by the Chief Administrative Officer.
E. If a license is required for performance of any upgraded position, no
employee who lacks the required license may be upgraded to that position,
regardless of the length of the upgrade.
F. Employees who are upgraded to safety sensitive positions must be designated
safety sensitive within the same safety sensitive category as the position to
which he or she is upgraded.
G. An FLSA non-exempt employee will be upgraded only if an FLSA exempt employee
is not available to perform the duties of the position. A non-exempt employee
who is upgraded for less than ten (10) days will be entitled to overtime
compensation in the upgraded position. An employee upgraded for more than ten
(10) days will be entitled to overtime compensation if he or she is performing
duties considered to be non-exempt under the provisions of the FLSA. The Human
Resources Department will make the determination whether an employee upgraded
for more than 10 days is entitled to overtime compensation at the time that the
Human Resources Department qualifies the employee for upgrade.
H. No employee will be upgraded for less than an eight hour period.
I. No employee will be upgraded during lunch or other similar work periods.
J. The maximum number of hours an employee may be upgraded will be in
accordance with the respective collective bargaining agreement for union
employees. The maximum number of hours E and I series employees may be upgraded
will be in accordance with the Personnel Rules & Regulations.
K. Supervisors who fail to adhere to this instruction will be subject to
disciplinary action.
REFERENCES:   Personnel Rules & Regulations

LONGEVITY PAY FOR NON-BARGAINING UNIT EMPLOYEES
TITLE: Longevity Pay for Non-Bargaining Unit Employees
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
Background:
On November 21, 2001, the City began awarding longevity pay of $85.00 per pay
period to M series employees who had twenty years of continuous City service.
At that time, “M series employees” referred to employees who were not members
of a bargaining unit and thus not otherwise eligible for the longevity pay that
had been negotiated for members of the bargaining unit represented by AFSCME
Local 3022.
Policy:
It is the policy of the City that employees in the classified service shall be
granted longevity pay of $85.00 per pay period in the first pay period when
they reach 20 years of continuous City service, excluding service in a
temporary or seasonal position or any other position identified as “non-
benefited time”.
It is the policy of the City that employees serving in unclassified positions
who are not identified as members of any existing bargaining unit shall be
granted longevity pay of $85.00 per pay period in the first pay period when
they reach 20 years of continuous City service, excluding service in a
temporary or seasonal position or any other position identified as “non-
benefited time”. Examples of employees who may be eligible under this paragraph
include assistant City Attorneys, City Council staff, and Deputy Directors of
departments.
It is the policy of the City that the granting of longevity pay as described
above is not a right and may be rescinded with sixty days written notice. An
employee who is promoted or transferred from a position receiving longevity pay
under this Administrative Instruction will cease to be eligible to receive that
longevity pay although he/she may be eligible to receive longevity pay under
the pay plan governing his/her new position.
Any longevity pay allowable under the provisions of this Administrative
Instruction shall be prorated for half-time and three-quarter time employees.
Procedures:
Employees who are promoted or transferred from a position in a bargaining unit
where they were receiving longevity pay to a position that is not included in a
bargaining unit may be granted longevity pay in their new position only if they
are eligible under the provisions of this Administrative Instruction.
REFERENCES:   none

ASSIGNED DUTIES WHILE ON ADMINISTRATIVE LEAVE
TITLE: Assigned Duties While on Administrative Leave
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
The Personnel Rules and Regulations ("PRR") provide that an employee may be
placed on administrative leave status during an investigation. Pursuant to PRR
402.6(C), the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) may assign City employees to
duties and responsibilities that are of benefit to the City while on
administrative leave. Work accomplished by the Clean City Task Force ("CCTF")
benefits the City.
All employees placed on administrative leave under PRR 402.6(C) will be
assigned to the CCTF unless the CAO, in his or her sole discretion, determines
the employee should be assigned different duties and responsibilities. The CAO
may also determine, in his or her sole discretion, that an employee should be
relieved of all duties during an investigation.
The Chief of Police and the Fire Chief have the authority to re-assign Public
Safety employees as appropriate.
REFERENCES:   Personnel Rules and Regulations 402.6 (C) Administrative Leave

PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources

EMPLOYEE SELF-SERVICE PAYROLL DELIVERY
TITLE: Employee Self-Service Payroll Delivery
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Department of Finance and Administrative Services
1.   Purpose
The citizens of the City of Albuquerque expect and deserve efficient and
effective local government. A component of delivering services most efficiently
and effectively is enabling City employees to spend as much of their employment
time as possible providing direct services to our constituency by reducing the
amount of time spent performing administrative tasks.
The following options are available in Employee Self-Service in the PeopleSoft
ERP system.
a)   View Paycheck
b)   Benefits Summary
c)   View W-2’s
d)   1095 Consent form
e)   View 1095-C form
f)   Direct Deposit
g)   Personal Information Summary
h)   Paycheck Modeler
i)   My Current Profile
j)   W-4 Tax Information
k)   Voluntary Deductions
l)   Life Events
With respect to pay delivery, the City mandated direct deposit as a condition
of employment effective January 1, 1999. At that time and subsequently,
employees exempted from this mandate have been encouraged to adopt direct
deposit for pay delivery.
2.    Policy
Payroll delivery is accommodated only via one of the following options:
   A.   Employees with a commencement date of January 1, 1999, or later:
      1. Direct deposit to a financial institution account or accounts of the
employee’s choice, as designated in the City Payroll Policies and Guidelines;
      2. Application of net pay amount to a Pay Card, administered by the
City’s designated Pay Card provider.
Employees with a commencement date prior to January 1, 1999:
   B.   These employees may choose either option 2(A)(1) or 2(A)(2) above, or
if currently receiving pay via paper paycheck, continue to receive pay via a
paper check that will be postmarked and mailed to the employee’s home mailing
address as recorded in the PeopleSoft system and on file with the City’s Human
Resources Department on the pay date. (The cut-off date to effect a change of
the designated mailing address shall be at least 30 days prior to the pay day
on which the paper check will be mailed).
With respect to remittance advices:
   C.   The City has enabled electronic payroll remittance advice access via
the PeopleSoft ERP Employee Self-Service (ESS) functionality. Effective
November 1, 2012, paper advices will no longer be centrally printed and
distributed by the City. Advices may be accessed via the employee’s City-issued
work computer, smartphone, or tablet, or any other such personal device with
web access. Employees with no access to these ESS tools may request and receive
advice view/print capability from the designated Department representative.
REFERENCES:   Administrative Instruction 2-16 – Direct Payroll Deposit

HIRING AND TEMPORARY COVERAGE PROCEDURES FOR FISCAL, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY,
RISK MANAGEMENT/SAFETY, AND HUMAN RESOURCES POSITIONS
TITLE: Hiring and Temporary Coverage Procedures for Fiscal, Information
Technology, Risk Management/Safety, and Human Resources Positions
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Human Resources
Purpose of Administrative Instruction:
The purpose of this Administrative Instruction (AI) is to provide general
guidelines for advertising and interviewing positions in the Fiscal,
Information Technology, Risk Management/Safety, and Human Resources
professions. In order for the City to hire the best qualified applicant in
these specialized occupations, departments are directed to employ the expertise
of the Department of Finance and Administrative Services (DFAS), the Department
of Technology and Innovation (DTI) or the Human Resources Department (HR).
Similarly, Fiscal, Information Technology, Risk Management/Safety, and Human
Resources positions often hold critical roles in their Departments’ day-to-day
administration, and maintaining appropriate coverage is essential. Moreover,
coverage through the temporary upgrade or assignment processes may not always
provide the competencies necessary because these positions frequently require
specialized knowledge or skills that their supervisors or lower level positions
may not possess. This AI creates a way to facilitate coverage of high-level
Fiscal, Information Technology, Risk Management/Safety, and Human Resources
positions to maintain critical administrative functions.
HIRING POLICY
All departments are required to contact DFAS, DTI or HR in accordance with the
specific position to appoint an interview panel member when hiring for these
positions. The hiring department should advertise the vacant position both
internally and externally to obtain a larger pool of applicants.
Procedures
Below are procedures set in place for departments to follow when a position
becomes vacant in these professions:
   1.   When a department has a vacancy in the above mentioned professions, the
hiring department must contact DFAS, DTI or HR as appropriate. Requests for
hire may be rejected if these steps have not been followed.
   2.   Fiscal positions - DFAS will assist in the following:
      a.   Fiscal Manager E18 –The DFAS Director or designee will appoint a
staff member from Budget or Accounting to participate in the interview panel
and the hiring department will assign one (1) staff member of their own.
      b.   Fiscal Officer or other fiscal positions at a level of E/M16 - DFAS
will appoint a Budget or an Accounting staff member to participate in the
interview panel and the hiring department will assign two (2) staff members of
their own.
      c.   Fiscal Positions at a level of E/M15 – the hiring department will
notify DFAS of the appointees for the interview panel and obtain DFAS’s
concurrence to ensure the appropriate individuals participate in the interview
panel. The interview panel for all other lower level fiscal positions are at
the discretion of the hiring department to obtain the appropriate interview
panel.
DFAS will generate technical questions for an E/M16 through E18 and the hiring
department will generate other relevant questions. Positions at an E/M15 level,
the hiring department will generate the interview questions.
   3.   Information Technology Positions - Departments wishing to create a new
Information Technology position shall consult with DTI Director (or designee)
before creating the position. DTI will also assign one (1) IT staff member or
an IT specialist from another department to participate in the interview panel
and the hiring department will assign the remaining panel members. DTI will
generate technical questions and the hiring department will generate other
relevant questions.
   4.   Risk Management/Safety Positions – DFAS will appoint a Risk Management
Safety staff member to participate in the interview panel and the hiring
department will assign the remaining panel members. Risk Management/DFAS will
generate technical questions and the hiring department will generate other
relevant questions.
   5.   Human Resources Positions - the HR Department will assign one (1) staff
member or an HR specialist from another department to participate in the
interview panel and the hiring department will assign the remaining panel
members. HR will generate technical questions and the hiring department will
generate other relevant questions.
   6.   The interview panel will make a recommendation for the proposed
employee or candidate to the hiring Department Director and that Department
Director will submit the request for hire through the NEOGOV system.
By following this AI, the City will ensure departments hire the best qualified
and suitable candidate to fit the needs of the department as well as the City
of Albuquerque.
COVERAGE POLICY
Any department confronted with a vacancy in a Fiscal, Information Technology,
Risk Management/Safety, Human Resources position of E-16 grade or higher that
it reasonably anticipates will last more than 30 days or that cannot otherwise
be met by temporarily upgrading a lower level employee is directed to consult
with DFAS, DTI, or HR as appropriate to develop a coverage plan. The coverage
plan should at a minimum identify the department’s needs, some candidates to
meet those needs, and an estimated duration. Examples of applicable situations
include, but are not limited to the creation of a new department, a Fiscal
Manager vacancy during a critical period, or an applicable vacancy when its
subordinate staff has less than one year with the City and does not meet the
qualifications of the vacant position. The resulting plan should be presented
to the CAO or designee for review and approval.
Available options include the following:
   1.   Temporarily upgrade or assign a lower level employee from a different
department who meets the minimum qualifications or who has the necessary
competencies;
   2.   Enlist the assistance of an employee in an equivalent position from the
same or another department for a maximum of six (6) consecutive pay periods for
which that employee may be eligible for additional duty pay by the requesting
department based on the additional effort they must expend. Alternatively, the
employee that is assisting can earn compensatory time (hour for hour) for any
additional hours they work up to 10 hours per week when providing support to
the requesting department.
Guidelines for Additional Duty Pay or Paid-leave-other:
   1.   Covering employees must be exempt from overtime under the FLSA.
   2.   Covering employees are expected to maintain high performance in their
current role.
   3.   Covering employees may be eligible for additional pay or paid-leave-
other (PLO) to be used at a later date based on the additional effort or
responsibility they take on.
      a.   Additional Duty Pay may vary but shall not exceed 15% of an
employee’s annualized salary. (For example: if an employee annualized salary is
$60,000, 15% of the salary is $9,000 annually.) Additional Duty Pay can only be
awarded for a maximum of six consecutive pay-periods per assignment, with a
maximum of three assignments per year or until the 15% of the annual salary is
reached.
         i.   The requesting director and relevant advisor from DFAS, DTI, or
HR will assess the additional effort or responsibility required by the
covering-employee to determine the rate of additional pay. Minor increases
should be valued at 5%, moderate at 10%, and major at 15%.
      b.   In lieu of additional pay, the covering employee may elect to
receive up 60 hours of PLO. This PLO time can only be awarded for a maximum of
six consecutive pay-periods per assignment, with a maximum of three assignments
per year or until the 60-hour maximum is reached. The amount of PLO may vary
from one assignment to another, but shall not exceed 30 hours per assignment.
         i.   The requesting director and relevant advisor from DFAS, DTI, or
HR will assess the assess the additional effort or responsibility required by
the covering employee to determine the rate of PLO accrued. Minor increases
should be valued at 2 and one-halve hours per pay-period, moderate at three and
one-third hours per pay-period, and major at 5 hours per pay-period.
      c.   Factors to consider in assessing effort or responsibility
undertaken:
         i.   How much will the employee’s workload increase?
         ii.   Will the employee have to undertake additional supervisory
responsibility?
         iii.   Are the covered tasks routine or particularly complex?
         iv.   Will the employee be responsible for a larger work-force,
budget, system, or similar metric than in their normal position?
         v.   Are there other elements that bear on how hard the employee will
have to work or the impact their actions will have on the organization?
   4.   The additional duties assigned can be completed during or beyond the
employees’ regularly scheduled hours, but should not interfere with their
regular duties or exceed twenty additional hours per week. Covering employees
must be exempt from overtime under the FLSA, therefore, and not eligible for
overtime for additional hours worked.
   5.   The requesting Director or their designee will provide a project plan
to the covering-employee with expected deliverables and outline of additional
duties. The project plan will also encompass who will be monitoring the
covering-employees progress toward goal and how it will be reported.
If these solutions do not meet the requesting director and DFAS, DTI, or HR
advisors needs, they may propose an alternative approach to the HR Director,
who will in either approve or deny in consultation with the CAO or designee.

BREAK TIME FOR LACTATION
TITLE:   Break Time for Lactation
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources Department
The City of Albuquerque recognizes the health benefits of breastfeeding and
supports accommodation of mothers who choose to utilize their own breast pump
to express breast milk upon returning to work after maternity leave of absence.
This Administrative Instruction is in compliance with the break time
requirement for nursing mothers in the Patient Protection and Affordable Care
Act (PPACA), which took effect on March 23, 2010 (P.L. 111-148). PPACA also
amended Section 7(r) of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) which regulates
break time for nursing mothers.
This Administrative Instruction also aligns with New Mexico state law [NMSA
1978, Section 28-20-2 (Amended 2007)] which requires employers to provide
flexible break time and a clean, private space, not a bathroom, in order to
foster the ability of a nursing mother who is an employee to use a breast pump
in the workplace.
Policy
A.   Flexible Scheduling
   1.   A nursing employee is allowed to use a breast pump to express milk
during the work day using her regular break and meal periods. Since the
frequency and duration of lactation breaks will likely vary throughout the
nursing period, a nursing employee shall be allowed a reasonable flexible break
schedule for lactation with her own breast pump. The time allowed for milk
expression breaks each work day will not exceed the combined total amount of
time for regular employee break and meal periods. For time above and beyond the
combined total amount of time for break and meal periods, the employee may
request a lactation break schedule that includes the use of available vacation
or sick leave accruals. An employee who does not have sufficient vacation or
sick leave accruals must request the use of Personal Leave Without Pay.
   2.   Under no circumstances will the employee be paid overtime pay to
complete their work due to the time required to express milk.
   3.   In order to prepare a work schedule and coverage for a nursing employee
who provides uninterrupted city services, the employee must provide to her
supervisor at the beginning of each pay week a proposed schedule for expressing
milk with a breast pump.
   4.   All flexible lactation break schedule requests are subject to approval
by the department based on reasonableness of the request. Supervisors will
consult with the employee to identify a flexible break schedule that considers
parameters of the employee’s job description and the service being provided.
B.   Designated Lactation Space
   1.   Each department will provide a sanitary, lockable, private room or
other space where an employee can express milk with her own breast pump in
privacy, shielded from view, and free from intrusion from coworkers and the
public. This room or space may be used by other on-duty city employees when the
room is not being used to express milk.
   2.   Where possible, the room will be located near a sink with running water
for washing hands and rinsing out breast pump parts, and have an electrical
outlet. Where possible, the room or space will be in close proximity to the
employees' work area. The room may not be a toilet stall or bathroom. If
employees prefer, they may express milk in their own private office or other
comfortable locations agreed upon in consultation with the employee's
supervisor.
   3.   It is the employee's responsibility to keep the location clean after
each use and remove any personal items.
   4.   Nursing employees who do not work in an office setting but provide
uninterrupted city services may be required to use a room or space established
by this Administrative Instruction at a city facility that is not operated by
the department in which the employee works. The employee would be required to
use this room or space in order to minimize travel time to and from the
employee’s work location to the room or space.
   5.   Some departments may elect to provide transportation for the employee
from the field to the building in which the lactation space is located.
   6.   Twice a year, in January and in July, the Human Resources department
will distribute a list of each city facility that has or may have a private
room or space for expressing milk. This list will provide the following
information: Name of facility or complex, street address, days and hours of
operation, location of the room or space, parking information, any restrictions
for the use of the room or space, contact name, phone number, and email
address. Department representatives may use the list to identify facilities
that meet the needs of their department. Each department is responsible for
making lactation space arrangements.
C.   Storing Breast Milk
   1.   Nursing employees will provide their own containers and storage unit
such as small ice chest or thermos from home if these accommodations are not in
place.
   2.   If breast milk is stored in a common refrigerator, the expressed milk
container must be placed in a clean, closed container, which has the mother's
name and date on it. It is the employee's responsibility to remove expressed
milk at the end of each day.
D.   Employee's Responsibility
   1.   Employees need to inform their supervisor as early as possible of their
intention to continue breast pumping following maternity leave of absence. At
least two (2) weeks' advance notice should be given. This provides the
department time for all necessary arrangements to be made.
   2.   At the beginning of each pay week, provide the supervisor a proposed
break schedule for expressing milk with a breast pump.
E.   Supervisor's Responsibility
   1.   Upon receiving an employee’s advance notification of her intention to
express milk during the work day, the department must take necessary steps to
ensure schedule and room arrangements are made prior to an employee's return to
work.
   2.   Retaliation is prohibited against an employee who files a complaint,
institutes a proceeding, or testifies in a lactation break time investigation
(Section 15(a)(3) of the FLSA).
F.   Human Resources Department Responsibility
   1.   Provide list identified in section B-6 of this Administrative
Instruction.
   2.   As part of the procedure for applying for maternity leave under the
Family and Medical Leave Act, mothers shall be provided this Administrative
Instruction.
G.   Maximum Time Frame for Schedule Adaptation
   1.   The flexible lactation break schedule and space accommodations for
employees will expire one year from the date of birth of the child.
   2.   If the employee discontinues breast pumping before the child’s first
birthday, the employee is obligated to inform her supervisor of the date she
will discontinue breast pumping. Failure to inform the supervisor upon
discontinuing breast pumping and continuing to utilize the space accommodations
or schedule adaptation would be considered a policy violation subject to
appropriate disciplinary action.
H.   Scope
This Administrative Instruction applies to all current employees, classified
and unclassified, including but not limited to interns, volunteers and seasonal
employees.
REFERENCES:
Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA)
Section 7(r) of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA)
NMSA 1978, Section 28-20-2 (Amended 2007)
Section 15(a)(3) of the FLSA

MANDATORY ETHICS AND CODE OF CONDUCT TRAINING
TITLE:  Mandatory Ethics and Code of Conduct Training
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
BACKGROUND
Upholding public confidence in the integrity of government requires that public
officials and employees maintain their conduct at the highest standards.
Employees are required to serve the public in an ethical manner with respect,
concern, courtesy and responsiveness, recognizing service to the public is the
reason for their employment. As such, it is important to ensure that all City
of Albuquerque ("City") employees are aware of, and properly trained on, the
City's ethics and Code of Conduct requirements.
Council Resolution R-2016-032 established a Public Service Ethics and Code of
Conduct training program for the City. However, the Resolution only applies to
senior officials and employees. Expanding training to all employees would
promote professional excellence throughout city government.
POLICY
The Mandatory Ethics and Code of Conduct Training is established as a resource
to the public servants of the City of Albuquerque and to reaffirm that City
officials and employees must maintain their conduct at the highest standards to
retain the confidence and trust of the public.
Effective January 1, 2019, all regular City employees shall be required to
complete the Ethics and Code of Conduct Training provided by the City every two
years. All newly hired employees shall be required to complete the training
within 30 days of hire.
RECORD OF TRAINING
The City will record all Ethics training through the People Soft Enterprise
Learning Management (ELM) System and report training in the learner profile for
each employee.
REFERENCES
City of Albuquerque, New Mexico, Charter art. XII (Code of Ethics); City of
Albuquerque, New Mexico, Code of Ordinances §§ 3-3-1 to -13 (as amended through
1985) (Conflict of Interest); City of Albuquerque Personnel Rules and
Regulations, § 301 (Code of Conduct)

PAID PARENTAL LEAVE
ADMINISTRATIVE INSTRUCTION NO:   7-55 (2019)
TITLE:   Paid Parental Leave
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
   The City of Albuquerque is committed to a productive and healthy work
environment for all employees. The City strives to provide competitive benefits
that are flexible, and when possible, responsive to the needs of our employees
in order to continue to attract and retain a qualified, engaged and diverse
workforce. Paid Parental Leave, as established by Ordinance No. 0-18-37,
Enactment No. 0-2018-036, recognizes family and work-life balance as important
to the success of the City of Albuquerque. In accordance with this commitment,
the City provides employees with Paid Parental Leave to spend with a child
newly added to their family through birth, adoption, or foster care. The Paid
Parental Leave benefit supports parents by having additional flexibility and
time to bond with their new child and to balance professional obligations.
Eligibility:
   ∙   An employee must have worked for the City a total of twelve (12) months
(or fifty-two (52) weeks if the work is intermittent); and
   ∙   Must have worked one thousand two hundred and fifty (1,250) hours in the
twelve (12) months preceding the date the Parental Leave will begin.
   FLSA-exempt employees who have worked full-time for twelve (12) months are
presumed to meet the hourly requirement. Paid and unpaid absences used in the
twelve (12) months preceding the date the FMLA leave will begin are not counted
toward the one thousand two hundred and fifty (1,250) hour total.
Qualifying Event:
The Parental Leave Benefit begins with the following qualifying events:
   ∙   On the date of the birth of the child; or
   ∙   On the date of placement for adoption of a child age eighteen (18) years
or younger; or
   ∙   On the date of placement for foster care of a child (excluding the
adopting of a stepchild or partner's child) age eighteen (18) years or younger.
Entitlement:
The City provides eligible employees with the following Parental Leave
benefits:
   ∙   The parental leave must run concurrently to the Family Medical Leave
Act, ("FMLA"), if the employee is eligible for FMLA.
   ∙   Up to twelve (12) standard work weeks of paid time off used within six
(6) months of the qualifying event;
   ∙   If both parents work at the City, each employee is entitled to twelve
(12) weeks of parental leave;
   ∙   For events that occurred prior to the enactment of Ordinance No. 0-18-
37, retroactive parental leave benefits may be deemed qualified where an event
occurred within the FY19 Fiscal Year, (July 1, 2018 -June 30, 2019);
   ∙   Employees receiving Parental Leave may not simultaneously receive sick
or vacation time pay, however, will accrue sick and vacation time while on paid
parental leave;
   ∙   Approved parental leave must be taken in a continuous block of time
unless an intermittent schedule has been pre-approved and pre-scheduled by the
Department Director and the Human Resources Director. If approved, the
intermittent schedule must be consistent and taken in increments of four (4)
hours;
   ∙   Employees may be eligible for other types of leave that occur prior to
or after Parental Leave under other applicable administrative policies or
contracts;
   ∙   During the Parental Leave, medical coverage will continue to be
available for the employee and any dependents under their current group
insurance policy in existence at the time ofleave. While on paid leave, the
continued coverage will be provided on the same basis as available to the
employee during the course of employment.
Procedures:
Employees must request Parental Leave and obtain approval:
   ∙   An employee must give at least thirty (30) days written notice to Human
Resources and his/her Department Director before leave starts. If thirty (30)
days' notice is not possible, notice is expected as soon as practical. "As soon
as practical" means at least verbal notice within two (2) business days of
learning of the need for leave followed by written confirmation. If an employee
fails to give thirty (30) days' notice for foreseeable leave with no reasonable
excuse for the delay, the Human Resources Director (or Department Director, as
applicable) or designee may delay the taking of Parental Leave until at least
thirty (30) days after the date the employee provided notice based upon the
business needs of the Department.
   ∙   Request for leave must be submitted on a Parental Leave Request Form,
concurrently with a Family Medical Leave Certification Form.
   ∙   Any FMLA-qualifying absence will be designated as FMLA leave by the
Human Resources Department and will be applied to the twelve (12) weeks paid
leave entitlement, even if not requested by the employee.
   ∙   The Human Resources Department will notify the employee within two (2)
workdays , if feasible, of the approval or disapproval of their Parental Leave
request.
   ∙   The City may make a preliminary designation ofleave as Parental Leave
pending receipt of documented proof of event certification.
   ∙   To address the retroactive activity of the Ordinance, the City may
designate another type leave, which has already been taken, as Parental Leave
if the leave was taken within six
(6) months of the qualifying event.
   ∙   Where Parental Leave is foreseeable and thirty (30) days' notice has
been provided, an employee must provide documented proof of qualifying event
before leave begins. The employee is responsible for any expense connected with
the supporting documentation to prove the event. Failure to provide the
required documented proof of the event may result in a delay or denial of
Parental Leave.
   ∙   For birth or placement, documentary proof to support the date of the
qualifying event must be received within 30 calendar days.
Timekeeping:
Employees approved for paid parental leave will be entered and coded as
"Parental Leave" (PLF or PLY) in the City's time keeping system.
Effective Date:
This Administrative Instruction is effective immediately.
REFERENCES:   Family and Medical Leave Policy.

AFR ANNUAL PHYSICAL POLICY
ADMINISTRATIVE INSTRUCTION NO: 7-56 (2019)
TITLE: AFR Annual Physical Policy 
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Albuquerque Fire Rescue
BACKGROUND:
All members of AFR will be given an annual physical consistent with the NFPA
1582 Standard on Comprehensive Occupational Medical Program for Fire Department
v. 2018 and OSHA 29 CFR 191 0.134 - Respiratory protection. Cancer reduction
best practices for firefighters include having an annual exam. This document
will explain the agreed upon interpretation of NFPA 1582, AFR member
responsibilities, and Employee Health responsibilities.
ANNUAL PHYSICAL TWO-TIER PROCESS:
All AFR members will receive a physical annually, which will increase the
number of exams required. The annual physical will be a two-tier process: Blood
draws, which will occur while a member is on duty, and the actual physical
exam/ doctor's visit, which will be conducted while a member is off duty, with
appropriate compensation as enumerated below. With the increase in the number
of physicals needed to be scheduled, it will be imperative that members
communicate with the Department Health and Safety Officer when they need a
schedule change. Failure to appear for a scheduled physical without notifying
the HSO may lead to progressive discipline.
Tests included in a physical exam include: physical exam, fasting blood draw,
audiogram, vision, pulmonary, urinalysis, spirometry, EKG, chest x-ray as
indicated and treadmill stress test as indicated.
Base line physicals, previous physicals, any exposures, and TB testing results
will be included in what the physician reviews for each exam. By including the
exposure and TB results in the physical, this will now become a part of a
member's medical file, which will ensure they are kept and are accessible for
at least 60 years from a member's separation from the city.
SCHEDULING:
The AFR-HSO will schedule the member for their blood draw at Employee Health.
The member will be given a 4 week window for their physical to be scheduled.
The physical will be scheduled at the time of the blood draw at Employee
Health; members are reminded to schedule their clinic visit for their OSHA
physical on a day they are in an off-duty status. All communications with the
AFR-HSO will be done with an email for scheduling issues, even if a call has
been made.
All follow up testing is to be scheduled off duty; at no time will field units
be placed “Out of Service” for follow up testing for an annual physical. Once
scheduled, the date of the examination will be considered a "Special" day and
the member is required to go, barring emergent circumstances. It will be the
responsibility of the Member to contact the AFR-HSO prior to their blood draw
being taken if they need to have their physical window rescheduled.
COMPENSATION:
Members will be compensated 5 hours of CTA for the physical scheduled off duty.
The 5 hours of CTA will include any additional testing required, i.e. chest x-
ray or treadmill; no further compensation for follow up exams will be provided.
EFFECTIVE DATE; TRANSITION RULE:
This Administrative Instruction is effective from the date of the Chief
Administrative Officer’s signature, and will apply to all AFR members.

MILITARY VETERANS INTERVIEW PREFERENCE (2024)
ADMINISTRATIVE INSTRUCTION NO: 7-57 (2024)
TITLE: Military Veterans Interview Preference
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Human Resources
The Effective Date: This Administrative Instruction is effective immediately.
Background:
The City of Albuquerque acknowledges the people who served, or serve, in the
United States Armed Forces or the National Guard or Reserve and their spouses,
and follows specific consideration procedures within their application process
for employment.
The City of Albuquerque is committed to provide ongoing outreach services to
maximize opportunities for people in this demographic by offering them and
their spouses employment information and consultation, program referrals, and
education on City resources available for their support.
This Administrative Instruction provides general guidelines when selecting
applicants for interviews for posted classified job vacancies.
Policy:
The City of Albuquerque’s Veteran and Military Interview Preference (“Interview
Preference”) provides persons who served or applicants currently serving in
active-duty military service or the National Guard or Reserve, and their
spouses the advantage of consideration for an interview for vacant and
advertised, classified positions for which they apply and are qualified.
In order to be eligible for the Interview Preference, the applicant must be
qualified as per the minimum qualifications for the position of interest as
listed on the job posting; the applicant must attach eligibility documentation
as noted in the specified procedures below; the applicant must comply with any
and all instructions stated in the job posting and with Section 100 of the City
of Albuquerque’s Personnel Rules and Regulations, and any amendments thereto,
regarding application procedures; and the applicant must submit a completed
application through the City’s applicant tracking system.
A qualified applicant under the Interview Preference will receive consideration
as indicated below, contingent on the individual following the procedures as
described herein, as follows:
Procedures:
   1.   Interested applicants must apply by the closing date specified in the
classified job posting.
   2.   Applicants must meet the Interview Preference’s eligibility
requirements as follows:
      a.   Complete and submit an application for employment including the
applicant’s previous employment experience stated in the applicant’s own words
and with dates of employment for each previous employment experience;
      b.   Answer the required Supplemental Application Questions to
demonstrate the applicant’s relevant experience for the position and
eligibility for the Interviewing Preference;
      c.   Applicants must verifiably qualify for one of the following:
         i.   A veteran; or
         ii.   Currently serving in active-duty military service; or
         iii.   Currently in the National Guard or Reserve; or
         iv.   A spouse of one of the following: a (1) veteran; (2) a current
active-duty service member; or 3) a current National Guard or Reserve service
member.
      d.   Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications for the position as
listed on the job posting;
      e.   Applicants must provide all of the applicable eligibility documents
as described below:
         i.   DD-214; or
         ii.   Current orders of assignment; or
         iii.   If the applicant is a spouse as qualified above in Section (2)
(c)(iv): a copy of (1) the current marriage license to a veteran, an active-
duty service member, or a National Guard or Reserve member; and (2) a copy of
the current orders of assignment or the veteran’s DD- 214.
      f.   Applicants must provide documentation verifying any discharge from
military service, including other than honorable conditions. Applicants with
any discharge from military service, including discharge other than honorable
conditions, are encouraged to apply and will be considered equally for
eligibility.
   3.   Upon meeting all applicable requirements above, the applicant shall be
granted an interview.
   4.   All other hiring processes and procedures are in effect, and the City
undertakes no obligation to guarantee the applicant will be selected for the
classified position if the applicant is not the most qualified or does not meet
the minimum requirements of the position.
This Administrative Instruction will provide guidance to our departments to
follow the Interview Preference and the procedures while recognizing our
residents serving our country and communities and their spouses.

MODIFIED SICK LEAVE POLICY DURING THE COVID-19 OUTBREAK   (REVISED)
TITLE:   Modified Sick Leave Policy During the COVID-19 Outbreak (REVISED)
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:   Human Resources
BACKGROUND
The City of Albuquerque values its employees and the public’s welfare and wants
to take all appropriate precautions to restrict the spread of the COVID-19
virus. The Family First Coronavirus Relief Act, HR 6201, was signed into law by
President Trump on March 18, 2020, and creates new obligations for the City
under the FMLA and for emergency leave. The federal law will go into effect on
April 2, 2020 and expired on December 31, 2020. While no mandate to provide
leave currently exists, the City will continue to provide leave subject to the
following conditions.
POLICY
The total cumulative amount of “Public Emergency Sick” (PEM) leave available to
employees beginning on February 1, 2022 is 50 hours, regardless of the reason
for being placed in the status. However, a department director may increase the
amount of leave available on a case by case basis if they feel circumstances
justify such an increase. Time coded as PEM or PEV after January 1, 2022, shall
not be counted as time used under the FMLA.
Calling In:
No employee should come to work or have contact with the public if they are
exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19.
Beginning on January 1, 2021, all employees who exhibit symptoms of COVID-19 as
described by the Center for Disease Control (CDC), or have a household member
who is exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19, must notify their Department Director
immediately and not report to a non-telecommuting place of work. If the
employee is well and able to work from home (i.e., their “telecommuting
workplace”), they should do so in accordance with Administrative Instruction 7-
66 until they are eligible to return to work and may be allowed to do so more
than two days per week at Director discretion.
Directors may place employees calling in under this provision in a “Public
Emergency Sick” (“PEM”) paid status, subject to the 50 hours maximum set forth
above. Employees should remain in daily communication with their immediate
supervisor while on PEM status. After PEM leave is exhausted, employees will be
required to utilize any other paid leave accruals, including compensatory time
if applicable, or FMLA if eligible. If an employee has no accruals available,
they will be placed into an unpaid leave status for which they are eligible.
Employees should remain in contact with their direct supervisor on a daily
basis while in PEM status.
The City reserves the right to require medical assessment or a doctor’s note
from employees who are taking leave under this Administrative Instruction.
Vaccine Side Effects
If an employee chooses to receive a COVID-19 vaccination and they experience
side effects, they may be authorized to take up to twenty-four (24) hours of
“PEM” leave, subject to the overall limitation set forth above. After PEM leave
is exhausted, an employee is required to utilize any paid leave accruals,
including compensatory if applicable, or FMLA if eligible. If the employee does
not have any accruals available, they will be placed into an unpaid leave
status or other eligible unpaid leave status.
Symptomatic Employees at Work:
If an employee is presenting as symptomatic for COVID-19 at work, their
supervisor shall notify the Department Director immediately. The Director may
send the employee home and require that the employee not report for work under
this instruction until they meet the Return to Work Criteria as detailed below.
Employees not reporting for work under this section will be placed in a “PEM”
paid status, subject to the overall limitation set forth above. After PEM leave
is exhausted, employees will be required to utilize any other paid leave
accruals, including compensatory time if applicable, or FMLA if eligible. If
the employee has no accruals available, they will be placed into an eligible
unpaid leave status. If the employee is well and able to work from home, they
should do so in accordance with Administrative Instruction 7-66 until they are
eligible to return to work and may be allowed to do so more than two days per
week at Director discretion.
Return to Work Criteria
An employee’s Director may require that the employee not return to a non-
telecommuting workplace under this instruction as follows.
If an employee had a positive test result, they may return:
   ∙   After isolating at home for five days from the positive test results; or
   ∙   If they have no symptoms after five (5) days; or
   ∙   Receives a recommendation to return to work from a health care
professional or the Employee Health Center and provides documentation of such.
If an employee has symptoms, they may return:
   ∙   When they test negative; or
   ∙   At least five (5) days have passed after symptoms first appeared if
fever free for 24 hours without fever-reducing medication and symptoms are
improving.
   ∙   Receives a recommendation to return to work from a health care
professional or the Employee Health Center and provides documentation of such.
These criteria are based on current New Mexico Department of Health Guidelines,
which may change as new information becomes available and further research is
conducted.
Employees must abide by AI 7-61 Protective Requirement to Protect Against a
Resurgence of the Covid-19 Outbreak (2021).
Travel Reporting and Self Quarantine:
As of February 10, 2021, the State of New Mexico eliminated mandatory post-
travel self-quarantine requirements.
Leave Related to Childcare
The childcare provisions of this administrative instruction are not applicable
to “health care providers and emergency responders.”
A “health care provider” is defined as anyone employed at any doctor's office,
hospital, health care center, clinic, post-secondary educational institution
offering health care instruction, medical school, local health department or
agency, nursing facility, retirement facility, nursing home, home health care
provider, any facility that performs laboratory or medical testing, pharmacy,
or any similar institution, Employer, or entity. This includes any permanent or
temporary institution, facility, location, or site where medical services are
provided that are similar to such institutions.
An “emergency responder” is defined as anyone necessary for the provision of
transport, care, healthcare, comfort and nutrition of such patients, or others
needed for the response to COVID–19. This includes but is not limited to
military or national guard, law enforcement officers, correctional institution
personnel, fire fighters, emergency medical services personnel, other
responders to 9-1-1 calls, physicians, nurses, public health personnel,
emergency medical technicians, paramedics, emergency management personnel, 911
operators, child welfare workers and service providers, public works personnel,
and persons with skills or training in operating specialized equipment or other
skills needed to provide aid in a declared emergency, as well as individuals
who work for such facilities employing these individuals and whose work is
necessary to maintain the operation of the facility.
Employees may, upon providing appropriate certification to the Human Resources
Department that their child’s regular care provider is unavailable because of
the child’s COVID-19 illness or exposure may also be placed in a PEM paid
status, subject to the overall 50 hour limitation set forth above. This status
shall not be applied retroactively. Employees are encouraged to find
alternative solutions or use this option intermittently. Intermittent use must
be approved by the applicable Department Director.
Fifty-Six Hour Rule:
Subject to any negotiation required in these circumstances, the City will not
be enforcing the fifty-six hour rule found in the collective bargaining
agreements for employees utilizing PEM leave under this section.
Directors may require time to be recoded and may return accruals to employees
if employee time was improperly coded in accordance with previous versions of
this Administrative Instruction.
Employees who provide false or fraudulent proof of COVID-19 vaccination,
testing, or other documentation as part of the process related to this
Administrative Instruction, may be subject to disciplinary action.
To the extent necessary, the effects of this Administrative Instruction are
subject to negotiation for those employees within a collective bargaining unit.
This Administrative Instruction is effective February 1, 2022, and valid until
December 31, 2022.

AI NO: 7-62
CERTIFICATION OF DEPARTMENT FISCAL MANAGERS-OFFICERS (2020)
TITLE: CERTIFICATION OF DEPARTMENT FISCAL MANAGERS-OFFICERS
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT:    Finance & Administrative Services
BACKGROUND
The Department of Finance & Administrative Services (DFAS) reports to the Chief
Financial Officer (CFO) and is responsible for the oversight and administration
of central financial functions including, but not limited to accounting,
budgeting, purchasing and treasury. These functions and services are provided
in coordination with city departments. Each department is responsible for and
manages its budget and has staff internal to the department responsible for
making purchases, collecting payments, processing invoices, preparing budgets,
reconciling accounts at year end; all in accordance with city policy and
procedures.
POLICY
This policy requires each department director to designate a fiscal manager-
officer to manage and assume primary responsibility for the department’s fiscal
operations. The designated fiscal manager- officer must be certified annually
by the Department of Finance & Administrative Services. The purpose of the
certification is to ensure that the fiscal manager-officer has the education,
experience, skills and performance required to successfully carry-out the
duties and responsibilities of their role which in turn allows DFAS to carry
out city-wide obligations in a timely and satisfactory manner.
RESPONSIBILITIES of FISCAL MANAGER-OFFICER
The department fiscal manager-officer is responsible for the following:
   ∙   Adherence to city financial and administrative rules, regulations and
instructions. See Reference section for a list of these.
   ∙   Compliance with annual budget, fiscal year end, annual Comprehensive
Annual Financial Report (CAFR) and other intermediate deadlines related to city
finances
   ∙   Being fully available and accountable for the work and activities
assigned to your department and associated with preparing and delivering the
annual CAFR
   ∙   Tracking and review with your department management team of actual
expenditures to operating budget at least on a quarterly basis
   ∙   Familiarity with relevant business processes, including but not limited
to PeopleSoft supported processes
   ∙   Attendance at, and dissemination of information and instructions to
appropriate department staff from, monthly Fiscal Manager Meetings, Purchasing
Liaison User Group meetings, and other finance related meetings as determined
by the DFAS
   ∙   Continuing education each year as determined by the DFAS
   ∙   Any other contingencies as required by the Department of Finance &
Administrative Services Director and/or City Controller
CERTIFICATION PROCEDURE
The department director will designate a fiscal manager-officer in writing
using a standard certification request form. The form must be signed by the
department director and include a copy of the designee’s resume, telephone
numbers and email address. The form will also require specific information
regarding the education, experience and skills of the designated employee, as
well as a current department organizational chart that highlights the staff in
the department who have financial responsibilities whether or not they report
directly to the fiscal manager-officer.
The DFAS Director and City Controller will review the request and consider the
designee’s background in context with department’s size, complexity, known
financial challenges and past performance. The City Controller will notify the
department director, in writing, whether the individual designated as fiscal
manager-officer has been approved or denied. Upon approval, the City Controller
will prepare a certification letter which will require acknowledgement by the
fiscal manager-officer, department director, DFAS Director and City Controller.
The letter will list the key responsibilities of the fiscal manager-officer
position and specify any training or performance goals that will need to be
met.
Should a request for certification be denied, the reason for the denial will be
provided in writing along with specifics on what actions need to be taken to
obtain an approval. The department director will assume the approval authority
assigned to the fiscal manager-officer position until a certification is
approved for a designated fiscal manager-officer.
The initial deadline for certification letters to be completed and submitted to
the City Controller is the first day of January 2021, and thereafter every
first day of June effective for the new fiscal year beginning the first day of
July.
If at any time during the fiscal year, a fiscal manager-officer will be out of
the office and unavailable to serve for more than ten (10) consecutive days,
the department director shall notify, as soon as possible, the City Controller
to specify the timeframe the fiscal manager-officer will be out, in addition to
the contact information of the interim fiscal manager-officer.
SUSPENSION of CERTIFICATION
Failure to successfully perform the responsibilities of the fiscal manager-
officer position may result in suspension of the certification and disciplinary
action. Decisions to suspend and reinstate the certification will be made by
the DFAS Director and City Controller. The reasons for the suspension and a
corrective action plan geared toward reinstating the certification will be
documented and presented to the fiscal manager-officer and department director.
The department director will assume the approval authority assigned to the
fiscal manager-officer for the period of time that the certification is removed
suspended. The corrective action plan may include required training and/or
follow-up on to mitigate quality and other performance issues.
REFERENCES: Personnel Rules & Regulations, Code of Conduct 301.1 Duty to the
Public, 301.2 Professional Excellence, 301.11 City Funds and 301.13 City
Records and Accounting. Any failure to comply with the provisions of this
agreement may lead to disciplinary action.

AI NO: 7-65 (2021)
OFFICER AND EMPLOYEE FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE
TITLE: Officer and Employee Financial Disclosure
PRIMARY DEPARTMENT: Clerk
BACKGROUND
Effective operation of City government requires transparency from the City's
leaders to earn the public's trust. Elected officials and city employees have
various responsibilities to identify and disclose financial interests pursuant
to Article XII, Section 5 of the City Charter and Section 3-3-5 of the City
Ordinances. Accordingly, three tiers of disclosure requirements for city
officials and employees have been established to ensure compliance with the
City's Conflict of Interest rules.
POLICY
Tier 1- includes all elected officials, the Chief Administrative Officer, the
Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief of Staff, the
Deputy Chief of Staff, members of the Environmental Planning Commission,
members of the Albuquerque Development Commission, members of the Landmarks
Commission, the Planning Director, the Zoning Hearing Examiner, the Zoning
Enforcement Official, the City Engineer, the Director of Municipal Development,
the Capital Improvements Project Official, and the Administrative Hearing
Officer.
Tier 2- includes all other Department Directors including the Director of
Council Services and the Director of the Civilian Police Oversight Agency, all
Department Deputy Directors or Deputy Chiefs of the Police or Fire Departments,
the Inspector General, the Chief Procurement Officer, members of the Air
Quality Board, members of the Accountability in Government Oversight Committee,
members of the Arts Board, members of the Board of Ethics, members of the Fire
Code Board of Appeals, members of the Housing and Neighborhood Economic
Development Committee, members of the Information Services Committee, members
of the Labor-Management Relations Board, members of the Lodgers' Tax Advisory
Board, members of the Open Space Advisory Board, and members of the Urban
Enhancement Trust Fund Citizens Committee.
Tier 3- includes all other city employees and board and commission members.
By July 31, 2021 and by January 31 of each calendar year thereafter all Tier 1
and Tier 2 employees and officials shall complete a financial disclosure form
on a form designated by Clerk. Should a new conflict or potential conflict of
interest arise, all Tier 1 and Tier 2 employees and officials shall submit a
conflict of interest form within ten (10) days oflearning of the conflict or
potential conflict. Tier 1 and Tier 2 Board and Commission members shall fill
out a financial disclosure form following appointment and approval by City
Council. Tier 1 and Tier 2 Board and Commission members shall submit a conflict
of interest form within ten (10) days of learning of the conflict or potential
conflict. Tier 1 individuals shall fill out all parts of the financial
disclosure form. Tier 2 individuals shall fill out all parts other than the
fourth section regarding real estate interests.
All Tier 3 Board and Commission members shall sign an acknowledgement of the
City's Conflict of Interest Rules. All Tier 3 employees shall receive training
on ethics and conflicts of interest during new employee orientation. In the
event a conflict or potential conflict of interest arises, all Tier 3 officials
and employees shall submit a conflict of interest form within ten (10) days of
learning of the conflict or potential conflict. This form shall be a public
record.
DISCIPLINE
City employees or officials who fail to promptly disclose potential conflicts
of interest may face disciplinary action according to the Merit System
Ordinance or other applicable ordinances, the City's Personnel Rules and
Regulations, or Collective Bargaining Agreements if applicable. Board and
commission members who fail to promptly disclose potential or actual conflicts
may be subject to removal from their board or commission pursuant to ROA 1994,
2-6-1-1 et seq.
This Administrative Instruction is effective immediately.
